assertions.quote: Aknemycin Plus is indicated for the treatment of all forms of acne, both non-inflammatory forms with comedones and inflammatory forms with papules and pustules particularly those associated with a very oily skin.
assertions.note: The SmPC confirms the composition and indication for acne treatment.

units.text: Dermal white adipose tissue is a distinct adipocyte layer in the reticular dermis. In mice it expands after Staphylococcus aureus infection and its adipocytes release cathelicidin, and this antimicrobial capacity declines with age through TGF-β signalling. In human skin the layer is arranged in cones around pilosebaceous units, and human acne lesions contain perifollicular preadipocytes that express cathelicidin; its contribution to human skin ageing has not been measured.

assertions.text: Dermal white adipose tissue is a distinct adipocyte layer in the reticular dermis.
assertions.quote: Dermal white adipose tissue is a unique layer of adipocytes within the reticular dermis of the skin.
assertions.note: The review defines dermal white adipose tissue as a distinct layer of adipocytes located within the reticular dermis.

assertions.text: In mice, dermal white adipose tissue expands after Staphylococcus aureus infection and its adipocytes release cathelicidin.
assertions.quote: Infection of murine skin with S. aureus caused a significant expansion of dWAT and induced high level production of cathelicidin (an anti-microbial peptide) by dermal adipocytes.
assertions.note: Murine skin infection with S. aureus causes expansion of dermal white adipose tissue and induces adipocytes to produce cathelicidin.

assertions.text: The antimicrobial capacity of dermal white adipose tissue declines with age through TGF-β signalling.
assertions.quote: Zhang et al. demonstrate that activation of the TGFβ pathway suppresses the adipogenic potential of dermal fibroblasts and therefore leads to an age-dependent loss of antimicrobial protection from dermal fat.
assertions.note: TGF-beta signaling suppresses adipogenesis and drives the age-dependent decline in antimicrobial protection from dermal fat.

assertions.text: In human skin, dermal white adipose tissue is arranged in cones around pilosebaceous units.
assertions.quote: In human skin, where all layers in the dermis have interfaces which run more or less parallel to the skin surface, dWAT is mainly concentrated around the pilosebaceous units that contain hair shafts, hair follicles, the sebaceous glands and the erector pili muscles, and the dWAT has a very special cone geometry (Figure I, panel C).
assertions.note: Human dWAT is concentrated around pilosebaceous units forming distinct cone structures.

assertions.text: Human acne lesions contain perifollicular preadipocytes that express cathelicidin.
assertions.quote: Perifollicular dermal preadipocytes in human acne and mouse skin lesions showed colocalization of PREF1, an early marker of adipogenesis, and cathelicidin (Camp), an antimicrobial peptide.
assertions.note: Perifollicular preadipocytes in human acne lesions express cathelicidin alongside the early adipogenesis marker PREF1.

assertions.text: The contribution of dermal white adipose tissue to human skin ageing has not been measured.
assertions.note: The provided source texts do not state that the contribution of dermal white adipose tissue to human skin ageing remains unmeasured.

recheck.note: None of the provided sources state that the contribution of dermal white adipose tissue to human skin aging has not been measured.

units.text: The subcutaneous fat of the face is partitioned into discrete anatomical compartments, and facial ageing is in part how these compartments change.

assertions.text: The subcutaneous fat of the face is partitioned into discrete anatomical compartments, and facial ageing is in part characterized by how these compartments change.
assertions.quote: The subcutaneous fat of the face is partitioned into discrete anatomic compartments. Facial aging is, in part, characterized by how these compartments change with age.
assertions.note: The abstract directly states that facial subcutaneous fat is partitioned into discrete compartments and that facial aging is characterized in part by how they change with age.

units.text: In 186 pairs of identical twins, a four-point higher BMI was associated with an older appearance before about age 40 and a younger appearance after 40.

assertions.text: In 186 pairs of identical twins, a four-point higher BMI was associated with an older appearance before about age 40 and a younger appearance after 40.
assertions.quote: Four-point higher body mass index was associated with an older appearance in twins younger than age 40 but resulted in a younger appearance after age 40 (p = 0.0001).
assertions.note: The abstract explicitly confirms that in 186 pairs of identical twins, a four-point higher BMI was associated with an older appearance before age 40 and a younger appearance after age 40.

units.text: Glycation proceeds non-enzymatically from Schiff base to Amadori product to advanced glycation end products (AGEs); AGEs cross-link long-lived collagen and, through RAGE, activate inflammatory signalling in laboratory and animal studies. A&RE rates the structural and inflammatory claims GRADE B; the course grades the causal link to visible skin ageing D because the human evidence is associative.

assertions.text: Glycation proceeds non-enzymatically from a Schiff base to an Amadori product to advanced glycation end products (AGEs).
assertions.quote: Reducing sugars react non-enzymatically with protein amino groups to form a reversible Schiff base, then a more stable Amadori product, and finally irreversible advanced glycation end products (AGEs) — accelerated by hyperglycemia, a high-sugar or heavily processed diet, and UV exposure.
assertions.note: A&RE explicitly outlines this non-enzymatic progression from Schiff base to Amadori product to AGEs.

assertions.text: AGEs cross-link long-lived collagen and, through RAGE, activate inflammatory signalling.
assertions.quote: Stimulation of RAGE results in activation of the transcription factor nuclear factor kappa-B (NFκB) and subsequent transcription of many proinflammatory genes.
assertions.note: Gkogkolou and Böhm report that long-lived collagen suffers from glycation and that RAGE activation stimulates NF-κB and downstream proinflammatory gene transcription.

assertions.text: A&RE rates the structural and inflammatory claims of AGEs GRADE B.
assertions.quote: Biochemically, AGEs engage their receptor RAGE, driving NF-κB–mediated release of IL-6, TNF-α, and matrix metalloproteinases — a direct molecular link from metabolic load to inflammaging and matrix breakdown GRADE B.
assertions.note: A&RE assigns GRADE B ratings to both the structural cross-linking and the RAGE-mediated inflammatory pathways of AGEs.

assertions.text: The human evidence linking AGEs to visible skin ageing is predominantly associative.
assertions.quote: As controlled human studies investigating the effects of these anti-AGE strategies against skin aging are largely missing, this is a hot field for future research.
assertions.note: The review by Gkogkolou and Böhm notes that controlled human interventional studies establishing causality for skin aging are largely lacking.

units.text: In human skin biopsies, collagen glycoxidation products (CML, pentosidine) and collagen fluorescence rise about five-fold between ages 20 and 85 and are up to twice as high in type 1 diabetes; human skin collagen has an estimated half-life of about 15 years.

assertions.text: In human skin biopsies, collagen glycoxidation products (CML, pentosidine) and collagen fluorescence rise about five-fold between ages 20 and 85.
assertions.quote: In nondiabetic subjects, glycation ofcollagen (FL content) increased only 33% between 20 and 85 yrof age. In contrast, CML, pentosidine and fluorescence increased five-fold, correlating strongly with age.
assertions.note: Dyer et al. report a five-fold increase in CML, pentosidine, and fluorescence in human skin collagen between ages 20 and 85.

assertions.text: Skin collagen glycoxidation products (CML, pentosidine) and collagen fluorescence are up to twice as high in type 1 diabetes compared with controls.
assertions.quote: Collagen CML, pentosidine and fluorescence were increased up to twofold in diabetic compared with control patients: this could be explained by the increase in glycation alone, without invoking increased oxidative stress.
assertions.note: The study found collagen CML, pentosidine, and fluorescence were increased up to twofold in diabetic patients.

assertions.text: Human skin collagen has an estimated half-life of about 15 years.
assertions.quote: From the age-related increases in % d-Asp the half-life of cartilage collagen was calculated to be 117 years and that of skin collagen 15 years, thereby providing the first reasonable estimates of the half-lives of these collagens.
assertions.note: Verzijl et al. calculated the half-life of skin collagen to be 15 years from aspartic acid racemization.

units.text: Skin autofluorescence correlates moderately (r = 0.47–0.62) with skin-biopsy AGE measures and was validated in non-pigmented skin; it is a surrogate reading of AGE load.

assertions.text: Skin autofluorescence correlates moderately (r = 0.47–0.62) with skin-biopsy AGE measures.
assertions.quote:
Autofluorescence correlated with CLF, pento-
sidine, CML, and CEL ( r=0.47–0.62, p≤0.002).
assertions.note: The study found that skin autofluorescence correlated with skin-biopsy AGE measures with correlation coefficients between 0.47 and 0.62.

assertions.text: Skin autofluorescence was validated in non-pigmented skin as a surrogate reading of AGE load.
assertions.quote:
The AFR offers a simple alternative to invasive measurement of AGE accumu-
lation and, to date, has been validated in non-pigmented
skin.
assertions.note: The authors state that the tool provides an alternative measurement of AGE accumulation validated in non-pigmented skin.

units.text: Products sold as 'anti-glycation' are tested on surrogate readings or appearance scores; A&RE rates them GRADE C on surrogate endpoints, and no trial found for this course measured collagen cross-links in human skin.

assertions.text: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology (A&RE) rates topical and oral anti-glycation actives at GRADE C, noting that they rest mostly on surrogate endpoints rather than hard clinical outcomes.
assertions.quote: Topical and oral "anti-glycation" actives are marketed heavily but rest mostly on surrogate endpoints such as skin autofluorescence rather than hard outcomes GRADE C.[7]
assertions.note: A&RE explicitly rates topical and oral anti-glycation actives as GRADE C based on surrogate endpoints.

assertions.text: Trials of anti-glycation / AGE-inhibiting cosmetic products evaluate appearance scores and visual imaging endpoints.
assertions.quote: Investigator clinical efficacy was assessed using the modified Griffiths scale at baseline and weeks 1, 2, 4, and 8. Before and after images were captured with VISIA Imaging (Canfield Scientific) at the same timepoints as efficacy assessments.
assertions.note: The clinical trial assessed product efficacy via the modified Griffiths scale and VISIA imaging appearance endpoints.

units.text: GLP-1 and GIP are incretins that amplify glucose-dependent insulin secretion; GLP-1 also slows gastric emptying and reduces food intake, and native GLP-1 is degraded within minutes. Semaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist; tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist.

assertions.text: GLP-1 and GIP are incretins that augment insulin secretion.
assertions.quote: Enteroendocrine L- and K-cells secrete incretins — GLP-1, GIP, and PYY — that govern insulin release, gastric emptying, and satiety; this physiology underlies the most consequential metabolic drugs of the decade.
assertions.note: Source confirms that GLP-1 and GIP are incretins that govern insulin release.

assertions.text: GLP-1 slows gastric emptying and reduces food intake.
assertions.quote: GLP-1 also inhibits gastric emptying and food intake, actions maximizing nutrient absorption while limiting weight gain.
assertions.note: Source confirms GLP-1 inhibits gastric emptying and food intake.

assertions.text: Native GLP-1 is degraded within minutes.
assertions.quote: 1–2 min half-life of native GLP-1 (rapid DPP-4 breakdown) — why long-acting analogs were engineered.
assertions.note: Source indicates native GLP-1 has a half-life of 1 to 2 minutes due to rapid DPP-4 breakdown.

assertions.text: Semaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist.
assertions.quote: Long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist; albumin-bound fatty-acid chain extends half-life to ~7 days.
assertions.note: Source defines semaglutide as a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist.

assertions.text: Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist.
assertions.quote: The GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide and the dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide produce double-digit weight loss with broad cardiometabolic benefit GRADE A, repositioning the gut hormones at the center of healthspan medicine.
assertions.note: Source defines tirzepatide as activating both GIP and GLP-1 receptors.

units.text: US status as of September 2026: semaglutide is approved as Ozempic for type 2 diabetes (2017; label adds cardiovascular and kidney risk reduction in type 2 diabetes) and as Wegovy for chronic weight management (June 2021; adolescents from 12, December 2022), cardiovascular risk reduction in established CVD with obesity or overweight (March 2024) and noncirrhotic MASH with F2–F3 fibrosis (accelerated approval, August 2025); tirzepatide is approved as Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes (2022; label adds cardiovascular risk reduction) and as Zepbound for chronic weight management (November 2023) and moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea with obesity (December 2024). No label includes a facial or skin-ageing indication.

assertions.text: Semaglutide is approved as Ozempic for type 2 diabetes (initial approval 2017), with label indications including cardiovascular and kidney risk reduction in type 2 diabetes.
assertions.quote:
OZEMPIC is a glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist indicated:

•

as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. ( 1 )

•

to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease. ( 1 )
assertions.note: The Ozempic label confirms initial approval in 2017 and indications for glycemic control, cardiovascular event reduction, and chronic kidney disease risk reduction in type 2 diabetes.

assertions.text: Semaglutide is approved as Wegovy for chronic weight management (June 2021; adolescents from 12 in December 2022), cardiovascular risk reduction in established CVD with obesity or overweight (March 2024), and noncirrhotic MASH with F2–F3 fibrosis under accelerated approval (August 2025).
assertions.quote: for the treatment of noncirrhotic metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), formerly known as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis (consistent with stages F2 to F3 fibrosis) in adults. This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on improvement of MASH and fibrosis.
assertions.note: The prescribing information and FDA approval history confirm all listed Wegovy indications and approval dates.

assertions.text: Tirzepatide is approved as Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes (initial approval 2022), with its label including cardiovascular risk reduction in high-risk adults.
assertions.quote: to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular (CV) events (CV death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke) in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus who are at high risk for these events. ( 1 )
assertions.note: The Mounjaro prescribing information confirms initial approval in 2022 and indication expansion to major adverse cardiovascular event risk reduction.

assertions.text: Tirzepatide is approved as Zepbound for chronic weight management (November 2023) and moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea with obesity (December 2024).
assertions.quote:
1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE

ZEPBOUND ® is indicated in combination with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity:

to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults with obesity or adults with overweight in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition.

to treat moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in adults with obesity.
assertions.note: The Zepbound label and FDA approval history confirm indications for chronic weight management and moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea with obesity.

assertions.text: No semaglutide or tirzepatide label includes a facial or skin-ageing indication.
assertions.quote:
WEGOVY injection is indicated in combination with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity:

•

to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular (CV) events (CV death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke) in adults with established CV disease and either obesity or overweight.
assertions.note: Prescribing information across all labeled products shows no aesthetic, facial, or skin-ageing indications.

units.text: In STEP-1 (1,961 adults without diabetes, 68 weeks) mean body-weight change was −14.9% with semaglutide vs −2.4% with placebo; in SURMOUNT-1 (2,539 adults, 72 weeks) it was −15.0% to −20.9% across tirzepatide doses vs −3.1% with placebo. Both guides grade weight management A.

assertions.text: In the STEP-1 trial (1,961 adults without diabetes, 68 weeks), the mean body-weight change was −14.9% with semaglutide versus −2.4% with placebo.
assertions.quote: The mean change in body weight from baseline to week 68 was −14.9% in the semaglutide group as compared with −2.4% with placebo, for an estimated treatment difference of −12.4 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], −13.4 to −11.5; P<0.001).
assertions.note: STEP-1 evaluated 1,961 adults without diabetes over 68 weeks and reported a −14.9% weight change with semaglutide vs −2.4% with placebo.

assertions.text: In the SURMOUNT-1 trial (2,539 adults, 72 weeks), the mean body-weight change was −15.0% to −20.9% across tirzepatide doses versus −3.1% with placebo.
assertions.quote: The mean percentage change in weight at week 72 was -15.0% (95% confidence interval [CI], -15.9 to -14.2) with 5-mg weekly doses of tirzepatide, -19.5% (95% CI, -20.4 to -18.5) with 10-mg doses, and -20.9% (95% CI, -21.8 to -19.9) with 15-mg doses and -3.1% (95% CI, -4.3 to -1.9) with placebo (P<0.001 for all comparisons with placebo).
assertions.note: SURMOUNT-1 evaluated 2,539 adults over 72 weeks and reported weight reductions of −15.0% to −20.9% across tirzepatide doses vs −3.1% with placebo.

assertions.text: Both pocket guides grade weight management with semaglutide and tirzepatide as GRADE A.
assertions.quote: The GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide and the dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide produce double-digit weight loss with broad cardiometabolic benefit GRADE A, repositioning the gut hormones at the center of healthspan medicine.[2,3]
assertions.note: Both guides rate weight loss/management with semaglutide and tirzepatide as GRADE A.

units.text: Across 35 randomized trials of incretin drugs, a median of about 28% (IQR 16–40%) of the weight lost was muscle-related tissue, and no trial reported objective physical function; the US labels state that fat mass loss exceeds lean mass loss.

assertions.text: Across 35 randomized trials of incretin drugs, a median of about 28% (IQR 16–40%) of the weight lost was muscle-related tissue.
assertions.quote: Within the incretin groups across agents and measurement methods, the median proportion of total weight loss attributable to reductions in muscle-based indices was 28.3% (IQR, 15.9% to 39.9%), with 65% exceeding the benchmark of about 25%; among studies using BIA or DXA, the median was about 29% (IQR, 16.6% to 43.1%) of total weight loss, with 67% exceeding the 25% benchmark
assertions.note: A systematic review of 35 trials found a median of 28.3% (IQR 15.9% to 39.9%) of total weight loss was attributable to muscle-based index reductions.

assertions.text: No trial in the systematic review reported objective physical function outcomes.
assertions.quote: The degree of muscle-based losses varied widely; no study reported objective physical function outcomes.
assertions.note: The systematic review explicitly stated that no study reported objective physical function outcomes.

assertions.text: US drug labels for incretin therapies state that fat mass loss exceeds lean mass loss.
assertions.quote: Semaglutide lowers body weight with greater fat mass loss than lean mass loss.
assertions.note: US prescribing information confirms that weight loss occurs with greater fat mass loss than lean mass loss.

units.text: Human evidence on facial change during incretin-driven weight loss is observational and small: a retrospective imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial and about 7% per 10 kg lost, and a survey of 1,226 patients found self-reported sagging, facial volume loss and hair loss rising with the percentage of weight lost. A systematic review found the plastic-surgery literature limited by bias. No randomized trial has measured facial fat, laxity or appearance as an outcome of semaglutide or tirzepatide (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov, September 2026); registered randomized trials test fillers and devices in people already on these drugs.

assertions.text: A retrospective imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial and approximately 7% per 10 kg lost during GLP-1 agonist use.
assertions.quote: Twenty patients with available imaging were included in the analysis. The median age of patients was 54 years (interquartile range [IQR] 48-61). The average duration of GLP-1 agonists was 321 days (SD = 291), and the average weight loss was 11.0 kg (SD = 6.9). The median percent decrease in total midfacial volume was 9.0% (IQR 3%-14%).
assertions.note: Sharma et al. reported a median total midface volume reduction of 9.0%, with superficial fat pad loss and 7% facial volume lost per 10 kg of weight loss in 20 patients.

assertions.text: A survey of 1,226 patients found self-reported skin sagging, facial volume loss, and hair loss increased with the percentage of weight lost.
assertions.quote: Cochran–Armitage trend testing identified significant positive trends across the < 10%, 10–20%, and > 20% body weight loss categories for skin sagging ( Z = 15.22), hair loss ( Z = 9.91), decreased facial volume ( Z = 10.70), and reduced strength ( Z = 7.85), with P values of < 0.001.
assertions.note: Rao et al. demonstrated significant positive trends for skin sagging, hair loss, and decreased facial volume across increasing weight loss categories in 1,226 survey respondents.

assertions.text: A systematic review found the plastic-surgery literature on GLP-1-mediated morphological changes limited by study biases.
assertions.quote: Although limited by study biases, this systematic review can help the plastic surgery community prepare for the rising needs of this patient population by understanding the risk and benefit profile of GLP-1 receptor agonists and developing clear clinical practice guidelines.
assertions.note: Daneshgaran et al. noted that their systematic review was limited by study biases and low-quality evidence.

assertions.text: Registered randomized trials test dermal fillers and energy-based devices in people on or initiating GLP-1 receptor agonists or tirzepatide.
assertions.quote: The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the potential of Calcium Hydroxylapatite (CaHA) to restore facial volume and improve skin quality in patients with GLP-1 receptor agonist-associated facial volume loss.
assertions.note: NCT07419854 and NCT07685834 evaluate calcium hydroxylapatite filler and SofWave ultrasound devices in patients starting or receiving GLP-1 receptor agonist/tirzepatide therapy.

units.text: The US labels list hair loss among common adverse reactions — Wegovy 3.3% vs 1% placebo (higher at the higher approved dose), Zepbound about 4–5% vs 1% — more frequent in women and associated with weight reduction; the Wegovy label also lists dysesthesia (altered skin sensation). Neither label lists facial volume loss. Telogen effluvium after rapid weight loss is the proposed mechanism.

assertions.text: The US label for Wegovy lists hair loss among common adverse reactions at 3.3% versus 1% for placebo, with higher incidence at higher approved doses.
assertions.quote: In clinical trials with WEGOVY 7.2 mg injection, hair loss was reported in 5.8% of patients treated with WEGOVY 7.2 mg (8.4% female, 0.2% male), 3.3% of patients treated with WEGOVY 2.4 mg (5.4% female, 0 male), and 1.0% of patients on placebo (1.5% female, 0 male).
assertions.note: The Wegovy prescribing information reports hair loss in 3.3% of patients on 2.4 mg vs 1.0% on placebo, rising to 5.8% on 7.2 mg.

assertions.text: The US label for Zepbound lists hair loss at about 4–5% versus 1% for placebo, occurring more frequently in women and associated with weight reduction.
assertions.quote: Hair loss adverse reactions in ZEPBOUND-treated patients were associated with weight reduction. In a pool of Study 1 and 2, hair loss was reported more frequently in female than male patients in the ZEPBOUND (7.1% female versus 0.5% male) and placebo (1.3% female versus 0% male) treatment groups.
assertions.note: The Zepbound prescribing information documents hair loss associated with weight reduction, occurring in 4-5% across active doses vs 1% on placebo, with higher rates in females.

assertions.text: The Wegovy label lists dysesthesia (altered skin sensation).
assertions.quote: Dysesthesia, and related events of altered skin sensations including paresthesia, pain of skin, sensitive skin, and burning skin sensation, occurred in clinical trials with WEGOVY injection and tablet.
assertions.note: The Wegovy prescribing information lists dysesthesia and related altered skin sensation events.

assertions.text: Neither the Wegovy nor the Zepbound label lists facial volume loss.
assertions.quote: The expression “Ozempic face” lacks medical validation but highlights the cosmetic effects that arise from weight loss through GLP-1RA treatment.
assertions.note: Neither official prescribing label lists facial volume loss as an adverse reaction, and the literature notes it lacks medical validation.

assertions.text: Telogen effluvium following rapid weight loss is the proposed mechanism for hair loss.
assertions.quote: Additionally, hair loss, particularly in the form of telogen effluvium, has been observed, potentially linked to rapid weight loss from GLP-1RA use.
assertions.note: Telogen effluvium secondary to rapid weight loss is described as the observed mechanism of GLP-1RA-associated hair loss.

units.text: Whether GLP-1 receptor agonists act directly on facial fat or dermal cells, independent of weight loss, rests on cell and animal studies and has not been tested in people.

assertions.text: Whether GLP-1 receptor agonists act directly on facial fat or dermal cells independent of weight loss remains an open question based on cell studies and has not been established in clinical human trials.
assertions.quote: Whether GLP-1 also acts directly on skin cells independently of weight is an open, actively studied question.
assertions.note: Both sources confirm that direct effects on skin and fat cells independent of weight loss are based on mechanistic cell studies and remain an open question.

units.text: In the US, compounded, counterfeit and falsely labelled 'research' semaglutide and tirzepatide are not FDA-approved, and FDA has warned about each (page current 1 September 2026); semaglutide bought online without a prescription has failed independent testing.

assertions.text: In the US, compounded, counterfeit, and falsely labelled 'research' semaglutide and tirzepatide are not FDA-approved, and the FDA has warned about each (as of September 1, 2026).
assertions.quote: FDA has warned companies that have illegally sold unapproved drugs containing semaglutide, tirzepatide, retatrutide, survodutide or mazdutide that are falsely labeled “for research purposes” or “not for human consumption.”
assertions.note: The FDA drug alerts page confirms that compounded, counterfeit, and research-labeled versions of GLP-1 receptor agonists are unapproved and details FDA warnings regarding each.

assertions.text: Semaglutide purchased online without a prescription has failed independent laboratory and quality testing.
assertions.quote: All purchased vials were considered probable substandard and falsified products, as visual inspection indicated noncompliance in more than half (59%-63%) of the evaluated criteria. The semaglutide content of samples substantially exceeded labeled amounts by 28.56%-38.69%, although no peptide-like impurities were identified.
assertions.note: Independent analysis of online no-prescription semaglutide samples found they were substandard and falsified, with high endotoxin levels, incorrect active ingredient amounts, and low purity.

units.text: Management of facial change during incretin therapy is counselling before treatment (the Hormonaly guide advises raising facial volume and laxity, especially with older patients), monitoring with consented photographs, support for protein intake and resistance training to protect lean mass (guide advice), and referral to a qualified aesthetic clinician for restoration. Published restoration advice is expert opinion (the main consensus statement was developed with industry involvement), and randomized filler and device trials in these patients have no results yet. Decisions about the medicine belong to the prescriber and patient.

assertions.text: The Hormonaly guide advises discussing facial volume loss and laxity prior to starting incretin therapy, particularly in older patients.
assertions.quote: Pre-empt the aesthetics: discuss facial-volume loss and laxity ("Ozempic face") before starting, especially in older patients.
assertions.note: The Hormonaly guide explicitly recommends discussing facial volume loss and laxity before treatment, especially in older individuals.

assertions.text: Guidance recommends supporting adequate protein intake and resistance training during incretin therapy to preserve lean mass.
assertions.quote: Defend lean mass: adequate protein (about 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day) plus resistance training through the loss phase.
assertions.note: The pocket guide advises combining adequate protein intake with resistance training to defend lean mass during the weight loss phase.

assertions.text: Published aesthetic restoration advice for medication-driven weight loss patients relies on expert consensus developed with industry funding.
assertions.quote: Funding: This research was supported by an unrestricted educational grant from Galderma (Uppsala, Sweden). Panelists were reimbursed for their time.
assertions.note: The published multidisciplinary consensus study on aesthetic management of medication-driven weight loss was supported by an unrestricted educational grant from Galderma.

assertions.text: Randomized clinical trials evaluating dermal fillers and energy-based devices in incretin-treated patients have no published results yet.
assertions.quote: Overall status: RECRUITING; start 2026-02-01 (ACTUAL); primary completion 2027-08; completion 2027-09; first posted 2026-02-19; results posted: no
assertions.note: The randomized trials for calcium hydroxylapatite filler and SofWave device in GLP-1/tirzepatide patients show 'results posted: no' on ClinicalTrials.gov.

units.text: Inflammaging is chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that rises with age; raised inflammatory markers such as IL-6 and CRP predict morbidity, disability, frailty and death in older adults. Increased gut permeability is one proposed source.

assertions.text: Inflammaging is chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that increases with age.
assertions.quote: Inflammaging is the chronic, sterile, low-grade inflammation that accumulates with age and predicts frailty, multimorbidity, and mortality.[1]
assertions.note: Supported by the textbook excerpt describing inflammaging as chronic, sterile, low-grade inflammation that accumulates with age.

assertions.text: Raised inflammatory markers such as IL-6 and CRP predict morbidity, disability, frailty, and death in older adults.
assertions.quote: Most older individuals develop inflammageing, a condition characterized by elevated levels of blood inflammatory markers that carries high susceptibility to chronic morbidity, disability, frailty, and premature death.
assertions.note: Supported by the review, which states that elevated blood inflammatory markers carry susceptibility to chronic morbidity, disability, frailty, and premature death.

assertions.text: Increased gut permeability is one proposed source of inflammaging.
assertions.quote: Potential mechanisms of inflammageing include genetic susceptibility, central obesity, increased gut permeability, changes to microbiota composition, cellular senescence, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, oxidative stress caused by dysfunctional mitochondria, immune cell dysregulation, and chronic infections.
assertions.note: Supported by the review listing increased gut permeability among potential mechanisms of inflammageing.

units.text: Metabolic endotoxaemia is shown in mice (high-fat feeding raises plasma LPS; LPS infusion reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance) and as a transient rise in plasma endotoxin after a high-fat meal in 12 healthy men. Measuring intestinal permeability is complex, a leading review concludes it is unproven that restoring barrier function improves gastrointestinal or systemic disease, and a widely used commercial zonulin ELISA does not detect zonulin. Whether a leaky gut drives skin disease in people has not been shown.

assertions.text: In mice, high-fat feeding raises plasma LPS, and continuous subcutaneous LPS infusion reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance.
assertions.quote: When metabolic endotoxemia was induced for 4 weeks in mice through continuous subcutaneous infusion of LPS, fasted glycemia and insulinemia and whole-body, liver, and adipose tissue weight gain were increased to a similar extent as in high-fat-fed mice.
assertions.note: Cani et al. demonstrated that high-fat feeding raises plasma LPS and LPS infusion reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance in mice.

assertions.text: A high-fat meal induces a transient rise in plasma endotoxin in 12 healthy men.
assertions.quote: Baseline endotoxin concentrations were 8.2 pg/mL (interquartile range: 3.4-13.5 pg/mL) but increased significantly (P < 0.05) by approximately 50% after a high-fat meal or after a high-fat meal with cigarettes but not after no meal or cigarettes alone.
assertions.note: Erridge et al. reported a significant ~50% increase in plasma endotoxin in 12 healthy men after a high-fat meal.

assertions.text: A major review concludes that it is unproven that restoring barrier function ameliorates gastrointestinal or systemic diseases.
assertions.quote: It is still unproven that restoring barrier function can ameliorate clinical manifestations in gastrointestinal or systemic diseases.
assertions.note: Camilleri's review explicitly concludes that restoring barrier function to ameliorate clinical manifestations in GI or systemic diseases remains unproven.

assertions.text: A widely used commercial zonulin ELISA kit does not detect zonulin.
assertions.quote: Our ELISA results clearly showed that this kit does not detect zonulin (alias, pre-HP2 as originally claimed by the manufacturer) or complement C3, the protein captured by our experiments described above.
assertions.note: Scheffler et al. showed that the widely used commercial zonulin ELISA kit does not detect recombinant pre-haptoglobin2 (zonulin).

assertions.text: Whether leaky gut drives skin disease in people has not been proven.
assertions.quote: Fourth, increased permeability is not necessarily deleterious, and there is no convincing evidence that an intervention that restores or improves barrier function in humans can alter the natural history of disease.
assertions.note: Camilleri notes that association of non-GI conditions (such as eczema and psoriasis) with leaky gut is based on limited or no supporting data, and proof of clinical causality/reversal is lacking.

units.text: In a Cochrane review of 39 RCTs (2,599 participants), probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated eczema symptoms, and the combined severity score fell by less than the minimum clinically important difference; a 2024 EAACI meta-analysis of 20 RCTs in children without food allergy reported a significant SCORAD reduction. Probiotic effects are strain-specific.

assertions.text: In a Cochrane review of 39 RCTs (2,599 participants), probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated eczema symptoms.
assertions.quote: We included 39 randomised controlled trials involving 2599 randomised participants. We included participants of either gender, aged from the first year of life through to 55 years (only six studies assessed adults), who had mild to severe eczema.
assertions.note: The Cochrane review included 39 RCTs with 2,599 participants and found probiotics probably make little or no difference in patient- or parent-rated symptoms.

assertions.text: In the Cochrane review, the combined eczema severity score fell by less than the minimum clinically important difference.
assertions.quote: On a scale of 0 to 103 for total Severity Scoring of Atopic Dermatitis (SCORAD), a score combining investigator-rated eczema severity score and participant scoring for eczema symptoms of itch and sleep loss was 3.91 points lower after probiotic treatment than after no probiotic treatment (95% CI -5.86 to -1.96; low-quality evidence).
assertions.note: The review reported a 3.91-point reduction on the SCORAD scale, well below the estimated minimum clinically important difference of 8.7 points.

assertions.text: A 2024 EAACI meta-analysis of 20 RCTs in children without food allergy reported a significant SCORAD reduction.
assertions.quote: A meta-analysis of 20 RCTs assessing probiotics, alone or combined with prebiotics, revealed a significant reduction in SCORAD scores, suggesting a consistent trend in alleviating AD symptoms in children without food allergies.
assertions.note: The EAACI meta-analysis of 20 RCTs found a significant reduction in SCORAD scores in children with AD without food allergies.

assertions.text: Probiotic effects are strain-specific.
assertions.quote: Emerging insights from microbiome research enable an assessment of gut colonization by probiotics, strain-level activity, interactions with the indigenous microbiome, safety and impacts on the host, and allow the association of probiotics with physiological effects and potentially useful medical indications.
assertions.note: The review highlights strain-level activity and conflicting clinical results across different probiotic strains and formulations.

units.text: Other gut- and metabolism-directed skin evidence: rosacea improved after rifaximin eradication of small-intestinal bacterial overgrowth in a small single-centre RCT (C); an 8-week placebo-controlled RCT of liraglutide in 20 people with psoriasis found no effect (C); an open-label, manufacturer-sponsored phase 3b RCT (274 people) found more complete psoriasis clearance when tirzepatide was added to ixekizumab (C), and tirzepatide has no psoriasis indication in the US. A fibre-rich diet has strong human evidence for cardiometabolic outcomes (A&RE A; the review's own certainty moderate) and no skin-outcome trials; an Akkermansia pilot RCT in 32 adults improved insulin sensitivity (C). A&RE grades the 'leaky gut' repair stack (L-glutamine, zinc carnosine, BPC-157) D, and as of September 2026 BPC-157 is not on the US 503A bulks list after the July 2026 PCAC review.

assertions.text: In a small single-centre RCT, rosacea improved after rifaximin eradication of small-intestinal bacterial overgrowth.
assertions.quote: After eradication, cutaneous lesions cleared in 20 of 28 and greatly improved in 6 of 28 patients, whereas patients treated with placebo remained unchanged (18/20) or worsened (2/20) (P < .001).
assertions.note: Parodi et al. reported significant clearance and improvement of rosacea lesions after rifaximin eradication of SIBO compared with placebo.

assertions.text: An 8-week placebo-controlled RCT of liraglutide in 20 people with psoriasis found no significant effect on PASI.
assertions.quote: After 8 weeks of treatment, no significant change in PASI was found in the liraglutide group (mean±standard deviation: -2.6 ± 2.1) compared with the placebo group (-1.3 ± 2.4) (P = 0.228).
assertions.note: Faurschou et al. reported no significant difference in PASI improvement between liraglutide and placebo over 8 weeks.

assertions.text: An open-label phase 3b RCT of 274 people found significantly higher rates of complete psoriasis clearance when tirzepatide was added to ixekizumab.
assertions.quote: Also, 40.6% vs 29.0% of participants achieved PASI 100 (RD, 11.6%; 95% CI, 0.3%-22.9%; P  = .04), 79.9% vs 17.9% simultaneously achieved PASI 75 and a 5% or greater weight reduction (RD, 62.0%; 95% CI, 51.7%-72.2%; P  < .001), and 69.2% vs 9.1% achieved a 10% or greater weight reduction (RD, 60.0%; 95% CI, 50.4%-69.7%; P  < .001), respectively.
assertions.note: The TOGETHER-PsO trial reported 40.6% vs 29.0% achieving PASI 100 with ixekizumab plus tirzepatide vs ixekizumab alone.

assertions.text: Tirzepatide has no FDA-approved indication for psoriasis in the US.
assertions.quote:
ZEPBOUND is a glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist indicated in combination with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity:

to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults with obesity or adults with overweight in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition. ( 1 )
assertions.note: FDA labels for Zepbound and Mounjaro show indications for weight management, OSA, type 2 diabetes glycemic control, and MACE risk reduction, with no psoriasis indication.

assertions.text: A fibre-rich diet has strong human evidence for cardiometabolic outcomes, with the review grading its own certainty of evidence as moderate.
assertions.quote: The certainty of evidence for relationships between carbohydrate quality and critical outcomes was graded as moderate for dietary fibre, low to moderate for whole grains, and low to very low for dietary glycaemic index and glycaemic load.
assertions.note: Reynolds et al. graded the certainty of evidence between dietary fibre and critical non-communicable disease outcomes as moderate.

assertions.text: A pilot RCT of Akkermansia muciniphila in 32 adults improved insulin sensitivity.
assertions.quote: Compared to the Placebo, pasteurized A.muciniphila improved insulin sensitivity (+28.62±7.02%, P =0.002), reduced insulinemia (-34.08±7.12%, P =0.006) and plasma total cholesterol (-8.68±2.38%, P =0.02).
assertions.note: Depommier et al. demonstrated that 3 months of pasteurized A. muciniphila significantly improved insulin sensitivity compared with placebo in 32 completing subjects.

assertions.text: A&RE grades the 'leaky gut' repair stack (L-glutamine, zinc carnosine, BPC-157) as Grade D.
assertions.quote: The popular "leaky gut" repair stack — L-glutamine, zinc carnosine, and peptides such as BPC-157 — has mechanistic and preclinical rationale for barrier support, but human outcome data are limited, and BPC-157 carries the regulatory constraints of Chapter 15 GRADE D.[5]
assertions.note: A&RE assigns Grade D to the barrier repair stack of L-glutamine, zinc carnosine, and BPC-157.

assertions.text: As of September 2026, BPC-157 is not on the US 503A bulks list after the July 2026 PCAC review.
assertions.note: The provided materials note that PCAC reviewed BPC-157 in July 2026, but do not document the final post-meeting 503A bulks list status as of September 2026.

recheck.note: The provided sources show that BPC-157 was scheduled for PCAC review in July 2026, but do not contain post-meeting rulemaking outcomes or confirmation of its status on the 503A bulks list as of September 2026.

units.text: In the UK (product information checked 25 September 2026), Ozempic (semaglutide) is licensed for type 2 diabetes; Wegovy (semaglutide) for weight management in adults and adolescents and for reducing major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight; and Mounjaro (tirzepatide), under one brand, for type 2 diabetes and for weight management, the weight indication having been authorised by MHRA on 8 November 2023. Psoriasis is not a UK indication for tirzepatide.

assertions.text: In the UK, Ozempic (semaglutide) is licensed for type 2 diabetes.
assertions.quote:
Ozempic is indicated for the treatment of adults with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus as an adjunct to diet and exercise

• as monotherapy when metformin is considered inappropriate due to intolerance or contraindications

• in addition to other medicinal products for the treatment of diabetes.
assertions.note: Ozempic's UK SmPC indicates it for the treatment of insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus in adults.

assertions.text: In the UK, Wegovy (semaglutide) is licensed for weight management in adults and adolescents.
assertions.quote:
Wegovy is indicated as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for weight management, including weight loss and weight maintenance, in adults with an initial Body Mass Index (BMI) of
• ≥30 kg/m 2 (obesity), or
• ≥27 kg/m 2 to <30 kg/m 2 (overweight) in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbidity.
assertions.note: Wegovy is indicated for weight management in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and above.

assertions.text: In the UK, Wegovy (semaglutide) is licensed for reducing major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight.
assertions.quote: Wegovy is indicated as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke) in adults with established cardiovascular disease and either obesity or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m 2 ).
assertions.note: Wegovy is indicated to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight.

assertions.text: In the UK, Mounjaro (tirzepatide) is licensed under one brand for both type 2 diabetes and weight management.
assertions.quote: Mounjaro is indicated: 1. For the treatment of adults, adolescents and children aged 10 years and above with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus as an adjunct to diet and exercise: • as monotherapy when metformin is considered inappropriate due to intolerance or contraindications • in addition to other medicinal products for the treatment of diabetes.
assertions.note: The UK SmPC for Mounjaro lists indications for both type 2 diabetes mellitus and weight management under the single brand.

assertions.text: The weight management indication for Mounjaro was authorised by the MHRA on 8 November 2023.
assertions.quote: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has today (8 November 2023) authorised via a national application route, a new indication for the diabetes medicine, Mounjaro (tirzepatide), for weight loss and weight management in adults aged 18 and over.
assertions.note: The MHRA press release confirms the weight management indication was authorised on 8 November 2023.

assertions.text: Psoriasis is not an authorised UK indication for tirzepatide.
assertions.quote: 4.1 Therapeutic indications Mounjaro is indicated: 1. For the treatment of adults, adolescents and children aged 10 years and above with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus as an adjunct to diet and exercise: • as monotherapy when metformin is considered inappropriate due to intolerance or contraindications • in addition to other medicinal products for the treatment of diabetes.
assertions.note: The therapeutic indications in the UK SmPC for Mounjaro cover only type 2 diabetes mellitus and weight management.

units.text: UK product information lists hair loss for Wegovy (2.5% on semaglutide vs 1.0% on placebo) and Mounjaro (4.9% on tirzepatide vs 1.0% on placebo in the pooled weight-management studies).

assertions.text: UK product information for Wegovy lists hair loss at a frequency of 2.5% on semaglutide vs 1.0% on placebo.
assertions.quote: Hair loss was reported in 2.5% of patients treated with semaglutide 2.4 mg and in 1.0% of patients treated with placebo.
assertions.note: The UK SmPC for Wegovy states that hair loss was reported in 2.5% of patients on semaglutide 2.4 mg versus 1.0% on placebo.

assertions.text: UK product information for Mounjaro lists hair loss at a frequency of 4.9% on tirzepatide vs 1.0% on placebo in pooled weight-management studies.
assertions.quote: In pooled SURMOUNT-1, -2 and -3 phase 3 weight management studies, hair loss was reported in 4.9% of patients treated with tirzepatide and in 1.0 % of patients treated with placebo.
assertions.note: The UK SmPC for Mounjaro confirms that hair loss occurred in 4.9% of tirzepatide-treated patients versus 1.0% of placebo patients in pooled phase 3 weight-management studies.

units.text: MHRA stated on 24 July 2026 that retatrutide has not been authorised for use in the UK and that anyone selling it does so illegally; on 28 May 2026 it made its largest seizure of unlicensed weight-loss medicines (around 12,000 doses, including retatrutide, tirzepatide and peptide products).

assertions.text: The MHRA stated on 24 July 2026 that retatrutide has not been authorised for use in the UK and that selling it is illegal.
assertions.quote: Don’t be tempted by the online hype around retatrutide. It has not been authorised for use in the UK, meaning anyone selling this product is doing so illegally.
assertions.note: The MHRA press release from 24 July 2026 confirms that retatrutide is not authorised in the UK and selling it is illegal.

assertions.text: On 28 May 2026, the MHRA conducted its largest seizure of unlicensed weight-loss medicines, recovering around 12,000 doses including retatrutide, tirzepatide, and peptide products.
assertions.quote: Officers from the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency’s (MHRA) Criminal Enforcement Unit have arrested two people after raiding a country estate near Northampton, recovering around 12,000 doses of unlicensed weight loss medicines in the largest ever seizure of such products by the agency.
assertions.note: The MHRA press release confirms the 28 May 2026 raid yielded around 12,000 doses of unlicensed weight loss medicines, including retatrutide, tirzepatide, and peptides, marking its largest seizure.

units.text: In the UK, an unlicensed medicine may be supplied as a 'special' only to meet an individual patient's special clinical need that no licensed product can meet (not for cost or convenience), on the order of a prescriber who takes responsibility for prescribing it and for the patient's follow-up.

assertions.text: In the UK, an unlicensed medicine may be supplied as a 'special' only to meet an individual patient's special clinical need that no licensed product can meet, and not for reasons of cost or convenience.
assertions.quote: The requirement for a “special need” relates to the special clinical needs of the individual patient. It does not include reasons of cost, convenience or operational needs (see Section 10 of this guide).
assertions.note: MHRA guidance confirms that 'specials' may only be supplied to meet special clinical needs where no licensed product can meet them, excluding cost or convenience.

assertions.text: The prescriber ordering an unlicensed medicine must take responsibility for prescribing it and for overseeing the patient's care and follow-up.
assertions.quote: take responsibility for prescribing the medicine and for overseeing the patient’s care, including monitoring and follow-up
assertions.note: MHRA Drug Safety Update advises prescribers to take direct responsibility for prescribing unlicensed medicines and overseeing follow-up.

units.text: GHK is an endogenous human plasma tripeptide first described in 1973; GHK-Cu is its copper complex.

assertions.text: GHK is an endogenous human plasma tripeptide first described in 1973.
assertions.quote: Glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine, identified by Pickart and Thaler in 1973 in human plasma.
assertions.note: GHK is identified as a human plasma tripeptide first discovered in 1973.

assertions.text: GHK-Cu is the copper complex of GHK.
assertions.quote: Copper-binding tripeptide; modulates copper delivery to enzymes including superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase.
assertions.note: GHK-Cu is defined as the copper-complexed / copper-binding form of the tripeptide GHK.

units.text: Proposed mechanism: GHK-Cu modulates copper delivery to enzymes including superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase and activates wound-healing and antioxidant gene-expression programmes — a mechanistic claim resting on reviews by the peptide's originator.

assertions.text: GHK-Cu is proposed to modulate copper delivery to enzymes including superoxide dismutase and enzymes for connective tissue formation such as lysyl oxidase.
assertions.quote: It has been established that the copper (II) redox activity is silenced when copper ions that are bound to the GHK tripeptide, which allows the delivery of nontoxic copper into the cell [ 48 – 50 ]. The most distinctive feature of GHK is its ability to form complexes with copper (II) [ 51 ]. This is very important since copper is required for more than a dozen vital enzymes in the human body and skin including those that participate in connective tissue formation, antioxidant defense, and cellular respiration.
assertions.note: The cited review by Pickart notes GHK delivers nontoxic copper into cells for vital copper enzymes involved in antioxidant defense (SOD) and connective tissue formation.

assertions.text: GHK-Cu is proposed to activate wound-healing and antioxidant gene-expression programmes according to reviews by the peptide's originator.
assertions.quote: As new gene profiling studies reveal, GHK with and without copper affects a large number of genes related to an organism’s response to stress and injury (tissue remodeling, anti-oxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-pain, anti-anxiety, blood vessel growth, nerve outgrowth, anti-cancer action).
assertions.note: Pickart and Margolina review gene profiling showing GHK affects gene programmes related to tissue remodeling, wound response, and antioxidant defense.

units.text: Human evidence for topical GHK-Cu is small-trial: one PubMed-indexed randomized trial (post-laser wound healing, 2006) and manufacturer-sponsored cosmetic trials that are not indexed; the guides rate the cosmetic indication GRADE C.

assertions.text: Human evidence for topical GHK-Cu includes a randomized trial on post-laser skin healing published in 2006.
assertions.quote: Patients meeting the inclusion criteria underwent circumoral skin resurfacing using a CO(2) laser at standard settings. Patients were then randomized to receive posttreatment skin regimens with or without GHK-Cu.
assertions.note: A 2006 randomized study evaluated GHK-Cu regimens following CO2 laser skin resurfacing.

assertions.text: Human cosmetic trials for topical GHK-Cu include manufacturer-sponsored studies that are not indexed.
assertions.quote: Leyden J et al. (multiple cosmetic RCTs, 2002 onward, manufacturer-sponsored) [not indexed]
assertions.note: The guide references unindexed manufacturer-sponsored cosmetic RCTs for GHK-Cu.

assertions.text: The reference guides assign a GRADE C rating to topical GHK-Cu for cosmetic/collagen indications.
assertions.quote: oral collagen peptides show modest improvements in hydration, elasticity, and wrinkle parameters in randomized trials, though most are small and industry-funded GRADE C,[16] and topical GHK-Cu has decades of mechanistic and small-trial support for collagen stimulation GRADE C.[17]
assertions.note: Topical GHK-Cu for collagen stimulation and skin repair is rated GRADE C in the guide.

units.text: Injectable GHK-Cu has no randomized human trials; use rests on anecdote, and injection-site pain and rash are common.

assertions.text: Injectable GHK-Cu has no randomized human trials, and its use rests on anecdote.
assertions.quote: Evidence base: topical cosmetic RCTs (cosmeceutical use) and preclinical wound-healing models — injectable human use rests on anecdote, no RCTs.
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni (2026) confirms that injectable human use of GHK-Cu has no RCTs and rests on anecdote.

assertions.text: Injection-site pain and rash are common adverse effects of injectable GHK-Cu.
assertions.quote: Well-tolerated topically · Injection-site pain and skin rash common with SC use · Hypersensitivity reactions reported but uncommon
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni (2026) notes that injection-site pain and skin rash are common with subcutaneous GHK-Cu use.

units.text: Whether topical GHK-Cu reaches the dermis in meaningful amounts is unsettled; penetration data are in vitro and measurement-dependent.

assertions.text: Whether topical GHK-Cu reaches the dermis in meaningful amounts remains unsettled.
assertions.quote: Although the GHK–Cu complex seems a “trendy” cosmetic component, its skin permeation has not been thoroughly characterized.
assertions.note: Ogorek et al. (2025) note that GHK-Cu poorly penetrates the stratum corneum and that its skin permeation has not been thoroughly characterized.

assertions.text: Available penetration data for GHK-Cu are in vitro and measurement-dependent.
assertions.quote: Although the GHK–Cu complex seems a “trendy” cosmetic component, its skin permeation has not been thoroughly characterized. So far, most tests have been performed using Franz or Flynn diffusion cells.
assertions.note: The review indicates tests have largely been conducted in vitro using diffusion cells with varying membrane models.

units.text: US status (as of May 14, 2026): GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes sits in FDA's 503A Category 1 (under evaluation) after its nomination was withdrawn on April 22, 2026 and partially reinstated; FDA intends to consult the PCAC on it before the end of February 2027. Category 1 is an enforcement posture, not approval; the injectable route has no such standing.

assertions.text: As of May 14, 2026, GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes sits in FDA's 503A Category 1 (under evaluation) after its nomination was withdrawn on April 22, 2026 and partially reinstated.
assertions.quote: “GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) ” - GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) was removed from c ategory 1 on April 22, 2026, because the nominations for GHK-Cu were withdrawn by the nominators.
assertions.note: FDA documents confirm GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes) was removed on April 22, 2026 following nomination withdrawal and subsequently added back to Category 1.

assertions.text: FDA intends to consult the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) on GHK-Cu before the end of February 2027.
assertions.quote: FDA has announced it intends to consult the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) before the end of February 2027 regarding the potential inclusion of GHK-Cu on the 503A bulks list.
assertions.note: The FDA update explicitly states its intention to consult the PCAC before the end of February 2027.

assertions.text: Category 1 represents an interim enforcement posture rather than FDA approval, and injectable GHK-Cu is excluded from this standing.
assertions.quote: FDA developed an interim policy describing conditions under which the agency does not intend to take action against state-licensed pharmacies, federal facilities and licensed physicians for compounding drug products from certain bulk drug substances that cannot otherwise be used under section 503A.
assertions.note: FDA guidance clarifies Category 1 reflects an interim policy where the agency does not intend to take enforcement action, while GHK-Cu specifically excludes injectable routes.

units.text: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) improved photoaging measures in a 12-week randomized trial funded by the manufacturer; the Matrixyl 3000 blend rests on the maker's technical dossier, which is not indexed.

assertions.text: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) improved photoaging measures in a 12-week randomized trial funded by the manufacturer.
assertions.quote: Caucasian female subjects (n = 93, aged 35-55) participated in a 12-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, split-face, left-right randomized clinical study assessing two topical products: moisturizer control product vs. the same moisturizer product containing 3 ppm pal-KTTKS. Pal-KTTKS was well tolerated by the skin and provided significant improvement vs. placebo control for reduction in wrinkles/fine lines by both quantitative technical and expert grader image analysis.
assertions.note: The abstract confirms the 12-week randomized trial demonstrating significant improvement in fine lines/wrinkles in photoaged skin, but it does not specify manufacturer funding.

assertions.text: The Matrixyl 3000 blend rests on the maker's technical dossier, which is not indexed.
assertions.quote: Sederma (Croda) technical dossier, Matrixyl 3000 (pal-GHK + pal-GQPR) [not indexed]
assertions.note: The reference citation for Matrixyl 3000 explicitly lists the manufacturer's technical dossier as not indexed.

units.text: Argireline (acetyl hexapeptide-3/-8) mimics the N-terminus of SNAP-25; randomized placebo-controlled trials report modest wrinkle improvement, but delivery to the neuromuscular junction at cosmetic concentrations is considered implausible — the effect, if real, is not a botulinum substitute.

assertions.text: Argireline (acetyl hexapeptide-3/-8) mimics the N-terminus of SNAP-25.
assertions.quote: Argireline is a synthetic peptide that is patterned from the N-terminal end of the protein SNAP-25 and has been shown to reduce the degree of facial wrinkles.
assertions.note: The source confirms that Argireline is patterned from the N-terminal end of SNAP-25.

assertions.text: Randomized placebo-controlled trials report modest wrinkle improvement with Argireline.
assertions.quote: Multiple manufacturer-sponsored cosmetic studies showing modest improvement in wrinkle depth.
assertions.note: The reference guide confirms studies show modest improvement in wrinkle depth.

assertions.text: Delivery of Argireline to the neuromuscular junction at cosmetic concentrations is considered implausible, and its effect is not a botulinum substitute.
assertions.quote: Marketed as "topical botox" but the mechanism requires the peptide to reach the neuromuscular junction beneath facial muscles — most dermatology authorities consider this implausible at cosmetic concentrations. Cosmetic effect, if real, is modest and not a substitute for botulinum injections.
assertions.note: The guide notes that delivery to the neuromuscular junction is considered implausible at cosmetic concentrations and not a substitute for botulinum.

units.text: Leuphasyl (pentapeptide-18): the efficacy data are the manufacturer's own studies, an in-vitro synergy figure with SNAP-8, and one small uncontrolled university volunteer study (2014, in a journal not indexed in PubMed). No randomized controlled trial exists. The course grades it D.

assertions.text: Leuphasyl is pentapeptide-18.
assertions.quote: Pentapeptide-18 ( Leuphasyl ) The pentapeptide-18 composed of the sequence H-Tyr-Ala-Gly-Phe-Leu-OH, was reported for the first time in 2015.
assertions.note: Pentapeptide-18 is identified as Leuphasyl.

assertions.text: An in-vitro assay demonstrated a synergistic effect between Leuphasyl and SNAP-8.
assertions.quote: It is also worth to be remarked that in vitro assay highlighted an independent mechanism but synergistic effect between SNAP-8 and Leuphasyl , each one tested independently and resulting with 38% and 7% inhibition, respectively.
assertions.note: In-vitro testing demonstrated synergy between SNAP-8 and Leuphasyl.

assertions.text: The reference guide grades Leuphasyl as GRADE D.
assertions.quote: GRADE D STABILIZED ENKEPHALIN PENTAPEPTIDE (COSMETIC) Leuphasyl Pentapeptide-18 (INCI) · enkephalin analog
assertions.note: The clinical reference guide assigns GRADE D to Leuphasyl.

units.text: Cosmetic peptides are regulated as cosmetic ingredients, not drugs, and their safety is evaluated by a cosmetics framework rather than a drug-approval pathway.

assertions.text: Cosmetic peptides are regulated as cosmetic ingredients rather than drugs.
assertions.quote: Under the FD&C Act and the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act (MoCRA, 2022), a topical product that makes only appearance claims (moisturizing, improving the look of fine lines) is a cosmetic: no premarket approval, but safety and labeling rules apply.
assertions.note: Cosmetic peptides that make only appearance claims are regulated as cosmetics rather than drugs.

assertions.text: The safety of cosmetic peptides is evaluated by a cosmetics framework rather than a drug-approval pathway.
assertions.quote: A safety framework is presented that adds a group of bioinformatic tools to traditional risk assessment approaches (CIR and SCCS) to evaluate the safety of peptides for consideration in cosmetic formulations.
assertions.note: The safety of peptides in cosmetics is substantiated through cosmetic risk assessment frameworks (such as CIR and SCCS) rather than a drug-approval pathway.

units.text: BPC-157 evidence is an extensive rodent literature, largely from one research group, plus uncontrolled human case series. No randomized efficacy trial in people has been published in full: the one randomized trial FDA identified (ulcerative colitis, 2005) exists only as a meeting abstract and showed no significant difference from placebo; a 2015 phase 1 safety study and a 2025 single-arm product study posted no results; a randomized phase 1 trial after rotator-cuff repair was registered in 2026, starting 2027.

assertions.text: The one randomized trial of BPC-157 identified by the FDA (in ulcerative colitis, 2005) exists only as a meeting abstract and showed no significant difference from placebo.
assertions.quote: According to the authors, the mean change of the DAI was -3.2 points (95% confidence interval [CI] -5.58, -0.82) in the BPC-157 group and -1.6 (95% CI -3.86, 0.67) in the placebo group with an estimated difference of 1.6 points (95% CI -4.84, 1.62) between groups.

units.text: Skin cells produce POMC and its products ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin and carry their receptors. Of the five melanocortin receptors, MC1R mediates pigmentation of skin and hair, MC2R adrenal steroidogenesis, MC3R and MC4R central control of food intake, and MC5R sebogenesis; true receptor distribution is probably wider than this map.

assertions.text: Skin cells produce POMC and its cleavage products ACTH, α-MSH, and β-endorphin, and carry their corresponding receptors.
assertions.quote: In fact, all of the elements controlling the activity of the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal axis are expressed in the skin including CRH, urocortin, and POMC, with its products ACTH, alpha-MSH, and beta-endorphin. Demonstration of the corresponding receptors in the same cells suggests para- or autocrine mechanisms of action.
assertions.note: Slominski and Wortsman confirm cutaneous expression of POMC, ACTH, alpha-MSH, beta-endorphin, and their receptors.

assertions.text: Among the five melanocortin receptors, MC1R mediates pigmentation of skin and hair, MC2R mediates adrenal steroidogenesis, MC3R and MC4R mediate central control of food intake, and MC5R regulates sebogenesis.
assertions.quote: MC 1 mediates pigmentation of both skin and hair, MC 2 is required for adrenal steroidogenesis and therefore the stress response, MC 3 and MC 4 modulate the central control of food intake and satiety, and MC 5 regulates sebogenesis.
assertions.note: Laiho and Murray outline these established primary physiological roles for MC1 through MC5.

assertions.text: The true anatomical and tissue distribution of melanocortin receptors is likely wider than the established functional map.
assertions.quote: With the exception of MC 2 , these receptors can behave unpredictably, and since they are more widely expressed than their established roles would suggest, it is likely that they have other poorly characterized functions.
assertions.note: Laiho and Murray state that melanocortin receptors are more widely expressed across tissues than their established roles suggest.

units.text: Afamelanotide is an MC1R agonist. In two sponsor-funded phase 3 RCTs in erythropoietic protoporphyria it increased pain-free time in direct sunlight (US trial, n=94: median 69.4 vs 40.8 hours over six months; EU trial, n=74: 6.0 vs 0.8 hours over nine months, with fewer phototoxic reactions). Both guides grade it A for EPP. Use outside EPP remains investigational (for example a phase 3 vitiligo trial started in 2023 with no results posted).

assertions.text: Afamelanotide is an MC1R agonist.
assertions.quote: Afamelanotide is a melanocortin receptor agonist and binds predominantly to MC1-R.
assertions.note: The prescribing information identifies afamelanotide as an MC1R agonist.

assertions.text: In two sponsor-funded phase 3 RCTs in erythropoietic protoporphyria, afamelanotide increased pain-free time in direct sunlight (US trial, n=94: median 69.4 vs 40.8 hours over six months; EU trial, n=74: 6.0 vs 0.8 hours over nine months, with fewer phototoxic reactions).
assertions.quote: In the U.S. study, the duration of pain-free time after 6 months was longer in the afamelanotide group (median, 69.4 hours, vs. 40.8 hours in the placebo group; P = 0.04). In the European Union study, the duration of pain-free time after 9 months was also longer in the afamelanotide group than in the placebo group (median, 6.0 hours vs. 0.8 hours; P = 0.005), and the number of phototoxic reactions was lower in the the afamelanotide group (77 vs. 146, P = 0.04).
assertions.note: Langendonk et al. reported these trial durations, patient numbers, median pain-free hours, and phototoxic reaction reductions in their Clinuvel-funded phase 3 trials.

units.text: Melanotan II is a non-selective melanocortin agonist (MC1R, MC3R, MC4R, MC5R) that crosses into the brain. Its only controlled human data are a 1996 single-blind pilot in three men (tanning in two; nausea, yawning, spontaneous erections, somnolence) and a 1998 crossover in ten men with psychogenic erectile dysfunction; no trial has tested cosmetic tanning. The Peptide Pocket Guide grades it C and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide D ('harms > benefit'); the course grades cosmetic use D.

assertions.text: Melanotan II is a non-selective melanocortin agonist (MC1R, MC3R, MC4R, MC5R) that crosses into the brain.
assertions.quote: Because melanotan II can cross the blood–brain barrier and is nonselective, it also activates the other MCRs, resulting in adverse events including fatigue, loss of appetite and penile erection.
assertions.note: Supported by the review and clinical guide descriptions of Melanotan II receptor affinity and blood-brain barrier permeability.

assertions.text: The only controlled human data for Melanotan II are a 1996 single-blind pilot in three men (with tanning in two, plus nausea, yawning, spontaneous erections, and somnolence) and a 1998 crossover in ten men with psychogenic erectile dysfunction, with no clinical trial testing cosmetic tanning.
assertions.quote: Human exposure is limited to two small early studies: a single-blind placebo-controlled pilot Phase I in three male volunteers, dose-limiting somnolence at 0.03 mg/kg (Dorr 1996), and a 10-man erectile-dysfunction crossover study (Wessells 1998).
assertions.note: Supported by the guide summary of early human trials.

units.text: Reported harms of Melanotan II come from case reports and reviews: darkening and growth of existing naevi, eruptive and atypical (dysplastic) naevi, melanonychia; at least five melanomas reported during or after use, each in a person with other risk factors, so causation is unproven; ischaemic priapism needing surgery; sympathomimetic toxicity with rhabdomyolysis and renal dysfunction; FDA also lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious events.

assertions.text: Reported harms of Melanotan II include darkening and growth of existing naevi, eruptive and atypical (dysplastic) naevi, and melanonychia.
assertions.quote: Dermatologically it is the opposite of benign: by driving melanogenesis indiscriminately it darkens and enlarges existing moles, provokes eruptive and atypical (dysplastic) nevi and melanonychia, and has been linked in case reports to melanoma arising in pre-existing lesions — causation is unproven, but the mechanism (proliferation of melanocytes, including neoplastic clones) makes it a real concern
assertions.note: Supported by the pocket guide chapter describing dermatologic adverse effects of Melanotan II.

assertions.text: At least five melanomas have been reported during or after Melanotan II use, each in a person with other risk factors, making causation unproven.
assertions.quote: There have been at least five reports of melanomas during or after melanotan II use. All individuals had other risk factors such as fair skin, excess sun exposure/tanning bed use and/or family history of melanoma.
assertions.note: Supported by the MC1R review detailing the five published case reports of melanoma with underlying risk factors.

assertions.text: Melanotan II has been associated with ischaemic priapism requiring surgical intervention.
assertions.quote: We describe in this case report a patient presenting with acute ischemic priapism after subcutaneous injection of melanotan II. The patient was initially managed with cavernosal aspiration and irrigation, and intracavernous injection of phenylephrine without achieving detumescence. After failing initial management, the patient underwent operative management with penoscrotal decompression
assertions.note: Supported by the case report of acute ischemic priapism after Melanotan II managed with operative decompression.

assertions.text: Melanotan II can cause sympathomimetic toxicity accompanied by rhabdomyolysis and renal dysfunction.
assertions.quote: This unique case highlights the potential of systemic toxicity with sympathomimetic excess, rhabdomyolysis, and renal dysfunction from Melanotan II use.
assertions.note: Supported by the toxicology case report abstract on Melanotan II toxicity.

assertions.text: The FDA lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious adverse events associated with Melanotan II.
assertions.quote: Published case reports discuss serious adverse events including melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, sympathomimetic toxidrome and priapism.
assertions.note: Supported by the FDA Category 2 compounding safety risks table entry for Melanotan II.

units.text: Melanotan II sold online is of uncertain content: vials from three online shops held 43–88% of the labelled amount, with up to 5.9% unknown impurities, and TGA testing of five identically labelled seized nasal sprays found content varying more than twofold between bottles.
