She has read that senolytic supplements clear so-called zombie cells and reverse skin ageing, and she asks whether to start one she found online. She does not wear sunscreen every day. Three facts frame the conversation. Senescent cells really do accumulate in human skin, and their number tracks with w…
units.sourceNote: Fictional case · Waaijer 2016 · Baker 2016 · Hickson 2019 · Hughes 2013 · Sitohang 2022 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 17

assertions.text: Senescent cells accumulate in human skin, and their number correlates with facial wrinkling and perceived age.
assertions.quote: The p16INK4a positive epidermal cells (identified as primarily melanocytes) were also significantly associated with more facial wrinkles and a higher perceived age.
assertions.note: Waaijer et al. found epidermal p16INK4a-positive cell counts in sun-protected skin significantly associated with facial wrinkling and higher perceived age.

assertions.text: Evidence for the benefits of senescent cell clearance comes from mouse studies, while human studies to date consist of small pilot trials measuring tissue biomarkers.
assertions.quote: Senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin; fisetin) clear senescent cells and extend healthspan in mice;[1] first-in-human pilots in pulmonary fibrosis and diabetic kidney disease show feasibility and reduced senescent-cell burden but are small, surrogate-only, and not outcome-powered, so any human healthspan claim remains GRADE C.[2,3]
assertions.note: The pocket guide notes that healthspan extension via senolytics has been demonstrated in mice, whereas human studies are small surrogate-marker pilot trials.

assertions.text: Daily sunscreen use and topical retinoids are supported by randomized controlled trials evaluating visible skin outcomes.
assertions.quote: With regard to efficacy, all studies consistently reported that topical tretinoin was efficacious in improving clinical appearance of photoaging in terms of wrinkling, mottled hyperpigmentation, sallowness, and lentigines as early as 1 month and lasted after 24 months.
assertions.note: Sitohang et al. reviewed RCTs demonstrating topical tretinoin's efficacy on visible photoaging outcomes, alongside Hughes et al.'s RCT of daily sunscreen.

assertions.text: The Aesthetic and Regenerative Endocrinology guide recommends keeping senolytics within clinical trials.
assertions.quote: Senolytics belong in trials. The preclinical story is compelling; human outcome evidence is not yet there. Intermittent dasatinib + quercetin and similar regimens should generally stay within registered studies.
assertions.note: The clinical pearls in the pocket guide advise that senolytics should generally be confined to clinical trials.

units.text:
What do you do first?
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Support a trial of the supplement: senescent cells clearly age skin, so clearing them should help.
Explanation: The human evidence is an association and the clearing evidence is in mice. No trial has tested senolytics on skin-ageing outcomes.
Correct answer: Explain what is known in people and what only in mice, point her to the measures with trials (daily sunscreen, and a topical retinoid discussed with a prescriber), and mention that senolytics are being studied in trials.
Explanation: Right. It keeps the registers apart and moves her toward the levers with human outcome data. The guide advises that senolytics generally be confined to clinical trials.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Tell her senescence is a mouse phenomenon with no relevance to human skin.
Explanation: Senescent cells are measurable in hu…

assertions.text: Senescent cell numbers in human skin are measurable and track with facial wrinkles and perceived age.
assertions.quote: The p16INK4a positive epidermal cells (identified as primarily melanocytes) were also significantly associated with more facial wrinkles and a higher perceived age.
assertions.note: Epidermal p16INK4a-positive senescent cells were significantly associated with more wrinkles and higher perceived age.

assertions.text: Evidence of benefits from clearing senescent cells has been demonstrated in mice.
assertions.quote: Clearance of p16 Ink4a -positive cells delayed tumorigenesis and attenuated age-related deterioration of several organs without apparent side effects, including kidney, heart and fat, where clearance preserved the functionality of glomeruli, cardio-protective K ATP channels, and adipocytes, respectively.
assertions.note: Clearing p16Ink4a-positive cells attenuated age-related deterioration across several organs in mice.

assertions.text: Measures with randomized trial evidence for preventing or treating skin aging include daily sunscreen and topical retinoids.
assertions.quote: The daily sunscreen group showed no detectable increase in skin aging after 4.5 years. Skin aging from baseline to the end of the trial was 24% less in the daily sunscreen group than in the discretionary sunscreen group (relative odds, 0.76 [95% CI, 0.59 to 0.98]).
assertions.note: A randomized trial showed that regular daily sunscreen use retards skin aging over 4.5 years.

assertions.text: The clinical guide advises that senolytics should generally be confined to clinical trials.
assertions.quote: Senolytics in particular should generally be confined to clinical trials.
assertions.note: The clinical pocket guide specifically states that senolytics should generally be confined to clinical trials.

assertions.text: No trial has tested senolytics on skin-ageing outcomes, and senolytics remain investigational with human outcome data lacking.
assertions.quote: NAD⁺ precursors raise NAD⁺ but lack outcome data; spermidine is promising-but-investigational (C) and senolytics remain investigational with no human outcome data (D).
assertions.note: The guide notes that senolytics remain investigational without human outcome data.

units.text:
Which statement about senescence and skin ageing matches the evidence?
Explanation: Name the species before you weigh the finding.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Randomized trials show that senolytics reverse human skin ageing.
Explanation: No randomized trial of a senolytic with clinical skin-ageing outcomes was found. Human data are small pilots measuring tissue markers.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Senescence has been seen only in mice and cultured cells.
Explanation: p16-positive cells are measurable in human skin and become more common with age.
Correct answer: In human skin, senescent cells increase with age and track with wrinkles; the evidence that clearing them improves ageing comes from mice.
Explanation: Correct. Human association, mouse causation: two registers, kept apart.

assertions.text: p16-positive cells are measurable in human skin and become more common with age.
assertions.quote: We show that the number of p16INK4A positive cells is significantly higher in elderly individuals compared to the younger age groups.
assertions.note: p16-positive cells are detectable in human skin biopsies and increase significantly with donor age.

assertions.text: In human skin, senescent cells increase with age and track with wrinkles.
assertions.quote: The p16INK4a positive epidermal cells (identified as primarily melanocytes) were also significantly associated with more facial wrinkles and a higher perceived age.
assertions.note: Senescent cells in human skin correlate with chronological age and are significantly associated with facial wrinkling.

assertions.text: Evidence that clearing senescent cells improves ageing phenotypes comes from mouse models.
assertions.quote: Clearance of p16 Ink4a -positive cells delayed tumorigenesis and attenuated age-related deterioration of several organs without apparent side effects, including kidney, heart and fat, where clearance preserved the functionality of glomeruli, cardio-protective K ATP channels, and adipocytes, respectively.
assertions.note: Genetic clearance of senescent cells in mice attenuated age-related deterioration across multiple organs and extended healthy lifespan.

Closing Module 1 (fictional case). A 41-year-old with a low serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D says she will stop sunscreen because 'skin makes vitamin D'. Which reply keeps the physiology and the evidence straight?

Correct answer: Skin synthesis does feed her blood level, but field trials of daily sunscreen did not lower 25-hydroxyvitamin D; keep sun protection and treat the low level as its own clinical question.
Explanation: Correct. The signal runs skin to body, and the human trials, not the mechanism alone, set the advice.

units.text:
Systemic hormones and the skin · three lessons
Lesson 2.1 Cortisol on the skin · Lesson 2.2 Estrogen, menopause and collagen · Lesson 2.3 Skin signs that need an endocrinologist.
Module 02 · Hormones written on the skin
The face that might be a diagnosis.
Most skin changes you see are ageing or lifestyle. A few are the first visible sign of endocrine disease. In three lessons you will separate them: what local and systemic hormones do to skin, what hormone therapy can and cannot do for it, and which signs belong with an endocrinologist.
2.1 Cortisol on the skin: local 11β-HSD1 and Cushing's syndrome
2.2 Estrogen, menopause and collagen: what the trials show
Your turn
'Is this cortisol face?'
One question to close lesson 2.1.
'Hormones for my skin.'
One question to close lesson 2.2.
Hair removal, or referral?
One question to close lesson 2.3.
Cortisol signatures: local 11β-HSD1 and Cushin…

Mechanism
The skin regenerates its own cortisol.
Skin expresses the machinery of a local stress axis, including CRH and POMC with its product ACTH. Keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts also carry 11β-HSD1, the enzyme that turns inactive cortisone back into active cortisol inside the cell. In human skin samples its activity is higher with age and in sun-exposed skin, and local cortisol availability is set independently of blood levels. Cortisol slows collagen production in dermal fibroblasts, and mice lacking the enzyme kept their dermal thickness with age.
Local axis: CRH, POMC and ACTH are made in skin
11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol inside skin cells
Mechanism register: human samples, cultured cells and mice
Narration: Picture the skin as a small endocrine organ with its own stress axis. Skin cells make CRH and ACTH, the same signals that drive the adrenal glands, and they carry the rece…
units.sourceNote: Slominski & Wortsman 2000 · Tiganescu 2011, 2013 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 8

assertions.text: Skin expresses the elements of a local stress axis, including CRH and POMC with its product ACTH.
assertions.quote: In fact, all of the elements controlling the activity of the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal axis are expressed in the skin including CRH, urocortin, and POMC, with its products ACTH, alpha-MSH, and beta-endorphin.
assertions.note: The source explicitly states that skin expresses all elements of the HPA axis including CRH and POMC with products such as ACTH.

assertions.text: Epidermal keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts carry 11β-HSD1, an enzyme that converts inactive cortisone into active cortisol.
assertions.quote: 11β-HSD1 (which activates cortisol), but not 11β-HSD2 (which inactivates cortisol), was expressed in epidermal keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts in human skin and also in outer hair follicle root sheath cells in murine skin.
assertions.note: The source confirms 11β-HSD1 expression in epidermal keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts and its role in activating cortisol.

assertions.text: 11β-HSD1 activity is increased with age and in sun-exposed skin, setting local glucocorticoid availability independently of circulating levels.
assertions.quote: Within target tissues, GC availability is regulated at a prereceptor level, independently of systemic levels, by isozymes of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (11β-HSD) that interconvert active cortisol and inactive cortisone.
assertions.note: The source confirms glucocorticoid availability is regulated independently of systemic levels and 11β-HSD1 increases with age and photoexposure.

assertions.text: Cortisol inhibits collagen production in human dermal fibroblasts, and 11β-HSD1 knockout mice are protected from age-induced dermal atrophy.
assertions.quote: Age-induced dermal atrophy with deranged collagen structural organization was prevented in 11β-HSD1 KO mice, which also exhibited increased collagen density. We found that treatment of HDFs with physiological concentrations of cortisol inhibited rate-limiting steps in collagen biosynthesis and processing.
assertions.note: The study demonstrates that cortisol inhibits collagen biosynthesis in dermal fibroblasts and 11β-HSD1 knockout prevents age-induced dermal atrophy.

units.text:
Four registers
11β-HSD1: four separate answers.
Local cortisol regeneration is a real and interesting mechanism. Each register below answers a different question, and blending them produces the line you will hear online: that blocking cortisol in the skin reverses ageing.
Mechanism
Plausible
Enzyme activity rises with age and sun exposure in human skin samples; knockout mice resist age-related dermal thinning

The evidence
Rare, and usually from a prescription.
Endogenous Cushing's syndrome is uncommon: European population studies put it at two to three new cases per million people a year. The commonest cause of Cushing's syndrome is iatrogenic, from glucocorticoids given as medicine. The Endocrine Society therefore asks for a drug history first, covering tablets, inhalers, injections and creams, including skin-bleaching products, and recommends testing when features are multiple and progressive.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Reassure the many, refer the few.
When a patient asks about 'cortisol face', start with the drug history: steroid creams, skin-lighteners, herbal tonics and injections. Then look for the discriminating features. Without them, the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide reads most puffiness as sleep, alcohol, salt and fluid, and the Endocrine Society recommends against widespread testing. With them, especially when they are progressing, the next step is formal testing and an endocrinologist. A cortisol supplement or a consumer cortisol panel answers the wrong question.

Look for bruising, plethora, proximal weakness, wide purple striae

units.text:
Lesson 2.2 · Concept
Estrogen and the dermis.
Skin carries estrogen receptors (ERα, ERβ and the membrane receptor GPER) in both sun-protected and sun-damaged sites. In postmenopausal women, two weeks of topical estradiol raised collagen production in sun-protected hip skin; photoaged facial skin showed no such response. After menopause, small biopsy studies found skin collagen and thickness falling year by year, following years since menopause more closely than age. That is mechanism and natural history. What hormone therapy does to a face is a separate question.
Receptors: ERα, ERβ and GPER in aged and photoaged skin
Topical estradiol raises collagen in sun-protected skin only
Collagen loss follows years since menopause
Narration: Estrogen is the hormone the guide says dominates the visible ageing of women's skin, so start with what it does in the dermis. Skin carries estrogen receptors…

The evidence
One to two per cent a year.
In small biopsy studies of postmenopausal women, skin collagen content and skin thickness fell by about 1–2% a year, in step with bone mass, and followed years since menopause more than age. Reviews, and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide, quote a steeper early loss of up to 30% in the first five years. That figure traces to the same small studies, and a check of their abstracts in September 2026 did not find it stated.

Biopsy gains, mirror results.
Hormone therapy has two kinds of trial behind it. Small trials measure the dermis; larger trials measure the face. They point in different directions, so read them separately. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades the skin benefit B; the North American Menopause Society rates the same evidence 'limited or inconsistent'. This course grades the structural gains C and teaches the negative wrinkle trials alongside them.

units.text:
Regulatory status and indications
Symptoms and bone. Skin is a bystander.
In the US, as of February 2026, FDA-approved menopausal hormone therapy is for moderate-to-severe hot flashes, vaginal and vulvar symptoms and, for some products, preventing bone loss. FDA's 2025–26 labeling changes removed cardiovascular, breast-cancer and dementia statements from the boxed warning; skin did not become an indication. The North American Menopause Society's 2022 statement finds benefit outweighs risk for bothersome symptoms and bone protection when therapy starts before 60 or within 10 years of menopause, and finds insufficient evidence for compounded 'bioidentical' hormones. Under US rules an over-the-counter 'hormone cream' is an unapproved drug. For the skin itself, daily sunscreen has a large randomized trial behind it, and one tretinoin cream is FDA-approved as an adjunct for fine facial wrinkl…

units.text:
A 52-year-old with no hot flashes, no sleep disturbance and no vaginal symptoms asks for estrogen 'to stop my face ageing'. What does the evidence support?
Explanation: Symptoms decide hormone therapy; skin gets skin-directed care.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Estrogen rebuilds collagen, so hormone therapy is a reasonable anti-ageing choice.
Explanation: That is the mechanism talking. Small trials show thicker skin, the largest trials found no difference in wrinkles, and skin is not an approved indication.

units.text:
Lesson 2.3 · Concept
Some syndromes show on the skin first.
A handful of inherited endocrine syndromes appear on the skin before the glands declare themselves. In multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1), multiple facial angiofibromas and collagenomas are common. In Carney complex, lentigines on the lips, eyelids and canthi, blue naevi and small skin myxomas sit alongside myxomas of the heart and cortisol-secreting adrenal disease. In MEN2A, an itchy, rippled, pigmented plaque between the shoulder blades can precede medullary thyroid cancer.
MEN1: facial angiofibromas, collagenomas
Carney complex: lip and eyelid lentigines, myxomas
MEN2A: lichen amyloidosis between the shoulder blades
Narration: Some endocrine syndromes are written on the skin years before the glands give them away. In multiple endocrine neoplasia type one, most patients in one careful series had several facial angiofi…
units.sourceNote: Darling 1997 · Kirschner 2000 · Correa 2015 · Stanescu 2024 · Lause 2017 · the guide's inherited-syndromes chapter

assertions.text: In multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1), multiple facial angiofibromas—identical to those seen in tuberous sclerosis—and collagenomas commonly appear on the skin.
assertions.quote: Multiple facial angiofibromas were observed in 28 (88%) of the patients with MEN1, with 16 patients (50%) having 5 or more. Angiofibromas were clinically and histologically identical to those in individuals with tuberous sclerosis. Collagenomas were observed in 23 patients (72%).
assertions.note: Darling et al. found facial angiofibromas identical to those in tuberous sclerosis in 88% and collagenomas in 72% of MEN1 patients.

assertions.text: Carney complex is commonly caused by inactivating PRKAR1A variants and features lentigines on the lips, eyelids, and canthi, blue naevi, and skin myxomas alongside cardiac myxomas and cortisol-producing adrenal disease.
assertions.quote: The disease is caused by inactivating mutations or large deletions of the PRKAR1A gene located at 17q22–24 coding for the regulatory subunit type I alpha of protein kinase A (PKA) gene.
assertions.note: Correa et al. review the PRKAR1A etiology and characteristic findings including facial/mucosal lentigines, blue naevi, myxomas, and cortisol-producing PPNAD.

assertions.text: In MEN2A, cutaneous lichen amyloidosis (a pruritic, rippled, pigmented plaque between the shoulder blades) can appear long before medullary thyroid cancer is diagnosed.
assertions.quote: Typically, CLA is detected at an early age (from childhood until young adulthood) before the actual MTC identification unless RET screening protocols are already applied.
assertions.note: Stanescu et al. report that interscapular cutaneous lichen amyloidosis typically presents at an early age before the identification of medullary thyroid cancer.

units.text:
The evidence
Eighty-eight per cent.
In a consecutive series of 32 people with MEN1 examined at the US National Institutes of Health, 88% had multiple facial angiofibromas and 72% had collagenomas. The angiofibromas were clinically and histologically identical to those of tuberous sclerosis. The authors concluded that angiofibromas in someone without tuberous sclerosis call for biochemical testing for MEN1.
of 32 people with MEN1 had multiple facial angiofibromas
Darling et al., 1997 — collagenomas in 72%
What it means: Multiple facial angiofibromas are common in MEN1 and can be its first visible sign; in someone without tuberous sclerosis they are a reason for endocrine testing, whatever the cosmetic plan.
What it does not mean: It does not mean a single facial papule is MEN1. This is one small referral-centre series, and angiofibromas have other causes, tuberous sclerosis above all.

units.text:
Concept
The everyday endocrine signs.
Most endocrine skin signs you meet come from common disease. New generalised darkening, strongest in skin creases, scars, mucosa and sun-exposed skin, can signal primary adrenal insufficiency, which can turn into a life-threatening crisis. Hirsutism that appears fast, keeps progressing, or comes with a deepening voice or clitoromegaly makes an androgen-secreting tumour more likely. Velvety dark plaques of acanthosis nigricans track insulin resistance, pretibial myxoedema points to Graves' disease, and cold, dry skin suggests hypothyroidism.
Darkening in creases, scars and gums: adrenal insufficiency
Rapid hirsutism or virilization: exclude a tumour
Acanthosis, pretibial plaques, dry cool skin: metabolic and thyroid
Narration: Most of the endocrine skin signs you will actually meet come from common conditions. New, generalised darkening, most obvious …

assertions.text: New generalised darkening, strongest in skin creases, scars, mucosa and sun-exposed skin, can signal primary adrenal insufficiency.
assertions.quote: Whatever the cause, the skin sign is the same and is mechanistically elegant: loss of cortisol feedback drives POMC-derived ACTH and α-MSH, so melanocortin signaling rises and the patient develops hyperpigmentation — darkest in palmar creases, scars, and mucosa — with congenital adrenal hyperplasia adding androgen-driven hirsutism and acne.
assertions.note: Primary adrenal insufficiency presents with hyperpigmentation darkest in creases, scars, and mucosa.

assertions.text: The Endocrine Society recommends testing for primary adrenal insufficiency with a low threshold in acutely ill patients.
assertions.quote: We recommend diagnostic tests for the exclusion of primary adrenal insufficiency in all patients with indicative clinical symptoms or signs. In particular, we suggest a low diagnostic (and therapeutic) threshold in acutely ill patients, as well as in patients with predisposing factors.
assertions.note: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends diagnostic testing in all patients with indicative signs or symptoms and a low threshold in acutely ill patients.

assertions.note: Rapid virilization with clitoromegaly, deepening voice, or rapid hirsutism prompts concern for an androgen-secreting tumor.

assertions.note: Acanthosis nigricans is described as a cutaneous manifestation of insulin resistance.

assertions.text: Pretibial myxoedema points to Graves' disease.

Freckles before the wedding.
A 29-year-old asks for laser removal of 'freckles' on her lips and at the corners of her eyes before her wedding. You notice a soft, skin-coloured papule on one eyelid. She mentions her father had 'a heart tumour' removed in his thirties. This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence; choose the first move that fits it.
Lip and canthal lentigines: typical of Carney complex
Eyelid papule: a possible cutaneous myxoma
A family heart tumour: the reason not to wait

Module 03 · Fat, incretins and the ageing face
The face changes when the fat does.
Facial shape depends on fat as much as on collagen. In three lessons you will separate what is known about the skin's own fat, sugar damage to the dermis, weight-loss drugs and the gut from what is still mechanism, marketing or an open question.
3.1 Dermal fat and sugar damage to collagen
3.2 Semaglutide, tirzepatide and the changing face
3.3 The gut barrier, endotoxaemia and inflammaging

Mechanism
The skin keeps its own fat.
Beneath the dermis lies subcutaneous fat. Within the reticular dermis itself sits a thinner layer, dermal white adipose tissue. In mice, this layer expands rapidly after a Staphylococcus aureus infection, its new fat cells release the antimicrobial peptide cathelicidin, and the capacity fades with age through TGF-β signalling. Human skin arranges this fat differently, in cones around hair follicles, and human acne lesions contain perifollicular preadipocytes that make cathelicidin. What the layer contributes to human skin ageing has not been measured.
A second fat layer inside the dermis
In mice: antimicrobial, and lost with age
In people: a different shape, and an open question about ageing
Narration: Most people picture skin fat as one layer under the dermis. There is a second, thinner layer inside the reticular dermis itself, called dermal white a…

units.text:
Human evidence
Fat that holds the face up.
Cadaver dissection shows that the face's subcutaneous fat sits in separate compartments, and facial ageing is partly how each compartment changes. Weight shows the same thing from the outside. In a study of 186 pairs of identical twins, the twin with the higher body-mass index looked older before about age 40 and younger after it.
pairs of identical twins compared for facial ageing
Guyuron et al., 2009 — a four-point higher BMI tracked with an older look before about 40 and a younger look after it
What it means: From midlife on, facial fat goes with a younger-looking face. That fits the anatomy: the face ages partly as its fat compartments change. GRADE C, observational.
What it does not mean: It is an observational comparison of photographs. It does not show that gaining weight rejuvenates, or that fat loss on a drug changes the skin itself.
units.sourceNote: Rohrich & Pessa 2007 · Guyuron 2009

assertions.text: Cadaver dissection shows that the subcutaneous fat of the face is partitioned into discrete anatomic compartments, and facial aging is partly characterized by how these compartments change with age.
assertions.quote: The subcutaneous fat of the face is partitioned into discrete anatomic compartments. Facial aging is, in part, characterized by how these compartments change with age.
assertions.note: Rohrich and Pessa (2007) confirmed through cadaver dissections that subcutaneous facial fat sits in discrete compartments and changes with age.

assertions.text: In a study of 186 pairs of identical twins, a four-point higher body mass index was associated with an older appearance in twins younger than age 40 but resulted in a younger appearance after age 40.
assertions.quote: Four-point higher body mass index was associated with an older appearance in twins younger than age 40 but resulted in a younger appearance after age 40 (p = 0.0001).
assertions.note: Guyuron et al. (2009) evaluated 186 pairs of identical twins and found a 4-point higher BMI was linked to an older appearance before 40 and a younger appearance after 40.

units.text:
Mechanism
Sugar that sticks to collagen.
Glycation is a slow, non-enzymatic reaction. Reducing sugars attach to protein amino groups, rearrange into Amadori products and end as advanced glycation end products, or AGEs. On long-lived dermal collagen, AGEs form cross-links that stiffen the matrix. Through their receptor, RAGE, AGEs switch on inflammatory signalling in laboratory studies. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates the structural and inflammatory effects B; the course grades the causal link to visible ageing D, because the human data are associations.
Sugar + protein → Schiff base → Amadori product → AGE
Cross-links stiffen long-lived collagen
RAGE signalling: shown in the laboratory
Narration: Glycation is chemistry before it is biology. Reducing sugars attach to the amino groups of proteins, rearrange into more stable products, and end as advanced glycation end…
units.sourceNote: Gkogkolou & Böhm 2012 · Dyer 1993 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 13

assertions.text: Glycation is a non-enzymatic reaction where reducing sugars attach to protein amino groups, rearrange into Amadori products, and form advanced glycation end products (AGEs).
assertions.quote: During the classical Maillard reaction electrophilic carbonyl groups of glucose or other reactive sugars react with free amino groups of amino acids (especially of basic lysine or arginine residues), forming a non-stable Schiff base. 16 Further rearrangement leads to formation of a more stable ketoamine (Amadori product) ( Fig. 1 ).
assertions.note: The source details the non-enzymatic reaction of sugars with protein amino groups to form Schiff bases, Amadori products, and AGEs.

assertions.text: On dermal collagen, AGEs form intermolecular cross-links that stiffen the matrix.
assertions.quote: Intermolecular crosslinks of adjacent collagen fibers change its biomechanical properties leading to stiffness and decreased flexibility, thus increasing its susceptibility to mechanical stimuli. 74
assertions.note: The source describes how intermolecular cross-links formed by glycation alter collagen biomechanics and cause stiffness.

assertions.text: AGEs binding to RAGE activates inflammatory signalling and matrix-degrading enzymes in laboratory studies.
assertions.quote: In skin cells RAGE has been shown to decrease cell proliferation, induce apoptosis and increase MMPs production. 47
assertions.note: The source confirms that RAGE activation in skin cells induces apoptosis, NF-kappaB-driven inflammatory signaling, and matrix metalloproteinase production.

assertions.text: The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide assigns a Grade B rating to the structural and inflammatory effects of AGEs.
assertions.quote: Structurally, they covalently cross-link long-lived collagen and elastin, stiffening the dermis and arterial wall and producing the loss of elasticity that reads as aged skin GRADE B.
assertions.note: The guide assigns Grade B to both structural matrix cross-linking/stiffening and RAGE-mediated inflammatory and matrix breakdown pathways.

units.text:
Human evidence
Fifteen years on the same collagen.
Human skin collagen turns over slowly; tissue analysis puts its half-life at about 15 years. In skin biopsies, glycoxidation products in collagen rose about five-fold between ages 20 and 85, and were up to twice as high in type 1 diabetes. Skin autofluorescence, a non-invasive reading, correlates moderately with those biopsy measures and was validated in non-pigmented skin.
~15 years
estimated half-life of human skin collagen
Verzijl et al., 2000 · AGE content of skin collagen rises about five-fold from age 20 to 85 (Dyer et al., 1993)
What it means: Glycation damage accumulates on the same collagen for years, and faster with higher glucose exposure. That much is measured in human skin: direct, observational, GRADE C.
What it does not mean: It does not show how much of visible ageing AGEs cause, or that any product reverses established c…
units.sourceNote: Verzijl 2000 · Dyer 1993 · Meerwaldt 2004

assertions.text: Tissue analysis estimates the half-life of human skin collagen at about 15 years.
assertions.quote: From the age-related increases in % d-Asp the half-life of cartilage collagen was calculated to be 117 years and that of skin collagen 15 years, thereby providing the first reasonable estimates of the half-lives of these collagens.
assertions.note: Verzijl et al. calculated the half-life of skin collagen to be 15 years based on aspartic acid racemization.

assertions.text: In skin biopsies, glycoxidation products in collagen increased about five-fold between ages 20 and 85.

In nondiabetic subjects, glycation ofcollagen (FL content) increased only 33% between 20 and 85 yrof age.
In contrast, CML, pentosidine and fluorescence increased five-

Collagen CML, pentosidine and fluorescence were increased up to twofold in diabetic compared with control pa-
tients: this could be explained by the increase in glycation
alone, without invoking increased oxidative stress.
assertions.note: Dyer et al. showed skin collagen CML, pentosidine, and fluorescence were increased up to twofold in diabetic patients.

assertions.note: Meerwaldt et al. reported correlation coefficients of r=0.47 to 0.62 between skin autofluorescence and biopsy AGE measures.

assertions.quote:
The AFR offers a simple alternative to invasive measurement of AGE accumu-
lation and, to date, has been validated in non-pigmented
skin.

units.text:
Lesson 3.2 · Concept
Two gut hormones, re-engineered.
GLP-1 and GIP are incretins, hormones the gut releases after a meal that amplify glucose-dependent insulin release; GLP-1 also slows gastric emptying and reduces appetite. Native GLP-1 is broken down within minutes. Semaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist, and tirzepatide activates both GIP and GLP-1 receptors. In the US, as of September 2026, both are FDA-approved drugs for defined indications, set out in the next moment. In the UK both are licensed by the MHRA, and tirzepatide's diabetes and weight-management uses share one brand, Mounjaro.
Incretins amplify insulin after meals
Semaglutide: GLP-1 receptor agonist
Tirzepatide: GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist
Narration: After a meal, the gut releases two hormones called incretins, GLP-1 and GIP. Both amplify insulin release when glucose is high, and GLP-1 also slows the sto…

units.text:
Human evidence
Large trials, measured on the scale.
In STEP-1, 1,961 adults without diabetes lost a mean 14.9% of body weight on semaglutide over 68 weeks, against 2.4% on placebo. In SURMOUNT-1, 2,539 adults lost 15.0% to 20.9% on tirzepatide over 72 weeks, depending on dose, against 3.1% on placebo. Both Hormonaly guides grade weight management A. Across 35 randomized trials of incretin drugs, a median of about 28% of the weight lost was muscle-related tissue.
14.9% · 20.9%
mean weight loss in STEP-1 (semaglutide, 68 weeks) and SURMOUNT-1 (tirzepatide, highest dose, 72 weeks)
Placebo 2.4% and 3.1% · both trials industry-funded, both the basis for approval
What it means: These drugs produce large, reproducible weight loss in randomized trials: GRADE A for the approved indications. Part of what is lost is lean tissue, which is why the Hormonaly guide pairs treatment with protein and resi…
units.sourceNote: Wilding 2021 · Jastreboff 2022 · Batsis 2026

assertions.text: In the STEP-1 trial, 1,961 adults without diabetes lost a mean of 14.9% of body weight on semaglutide over 68 weeks, compared to 2.4% on placebo.
assertions.quote: The mean change in body weight from baseline to week 68 was −14.9% in the semaglutide group as compared with −2.4% with placebo, for an estimated treatment difference of −12.4 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], −13.4 to −11.5; P<0.001).
assertions.note: STEP-1 confirmed a 14.9% mean weight loss with semaglutide versus 2.4% with placebo in 1,961 adults without diabetes over 68 weeks.

assertions.text: In the SURMOUNT-1 trial, 2,539 adults lost 15.0% to 20.9% of body weight on tirzepatide over 72 weeks (dose-dependent), compared to 3.1% on placebo.
assertions.quote: The mean percentage change in weight at week 72 was -15.0% (95% confidence interval [CI], -15.9 to -14.2) with 5-mg weekly doses of tirzepatide, -19.5% (95% CI, -20.4 to -18.5) with 10-mg doses, and -20.9% (95% CI, -21.8 to -19.9) with 15-mg doses and -3.1% (95% CI, -4.3 to -1.9) with placebo (P<0.001 for all comparisons with placebo).
assertions.note: SURMOUNT-1 reported mean weight losses of 15.0% (5 mg), 19.5% (10 mg), and 20.9% (15 mg) versus 3.1% on placebo across 2,539 participants.

assertions.text: Both STEP-1 and SURMOUNT-1 were industry-funded trials.
assertions.quote: (Funded by Novo Nordisk; STEP 1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03548935).
assertions.note: STEP-1 was funded by Novo Nordisk and SURMOUNT-1 was supported by Eli Lilly.

assertions.text: Across 35 randomized trials of incretin drugs, a median of about 28% of total weight lost was muscle-related tissue.
assertions.quote: Among 8102 titles and abstracts, 35 primary studies met criteria (median duration, 26 weeks; median of 78 participants); 42.9% were at low risk of bias and 10 (28.6%) prespecified body composition as a primary outcome.
assertions.note: The systematic review of 35 trials found a median 28.3% of total weight lost was attributable to muscle-based indices.

assertions.text: The Hormonaly guide recommends pairing GLP-1 therapy with adequate protein and resistance training to preserve lean mass.
assertions.quote: Treat a GLP-1 agonist as an endocrine intervention with aesthetic and musculoskeletal consequences: pair it with adequate protein and resistance training to defend lean mass, watch nutritional adequacy at reduced intake, and set realistic expectations about facial volume.
assertions.note: The pocket guide emphasizes pairing GLP-1 therapy with protein intake and resistance training to defend lean tissue.

units.text:
Four registers
'Ozempic face', answer by answer.
The phrase bundles four kinds of statement. Kept apart, they tell a patient far more than the headline does.
Mechanism
Volume loss
Losing fat deflates the superficial facial compartments and unmasks laxity that was already there.
Human evidence
Observational and small: C to D
One imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial, about 7% per 10 kg lost. A survey of 1,226 patients found sagging, facial volume loss and hair shedding reported more often the more weight was lost. A systematic review of the plastic-surgery literature found it limited by study bias. No randomized trial has measured the face.
Regulatory status (US and UK, September 2026)
Hair loss labelled; facial change unlisted
Both labels list hair loss (about 3–6% on drug against about 1% on placebo, mostly in women, linked to weight r…
units.sourceNote: Sharma 2025 · Rao 2026 · Daneshgaran 2025 · US labels 2026 · Paschou 2025 · UK SmPCs (Sept 2026)

assertions.text: Losing fat deflates the superficial facial compartments and unmasks laxity that was already there.
assertions.quote: Rapid, large-volume weight loss strips subcutaneous fat from the face, producing the hollowed, prematurely aged look popularly called "Ozempic face" — a volume change rather than accelerated skin aging, though it unmasks pre-existing laxity; restoration (filler, fat grafting, energy-based tightening) is the usual remedy.
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni (2026) notes that rapid weight loss strips subcutaneous facial fat, unmasking pre-existing laxity.

assertions.text: One imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial, about 7% per 10 kg lost.
assertions.quote: Twenty patients with available imaging were included in the analysis. The median age of patients was 54 years (interquartile range [IQR] 48-61). The average duration of GLP-1 agonists was 321 days (SD = 291), and the average weight loss was 11.0 kg (SD = 6.9). The median percent decrease in total midfacial volume was 9.0% (IQR 3%-14%).
assertions.note: Sharma et al. (2025) reported a median 9.0% midfacial volume decrease in 20 patients, primarily in superficial fat pads, equaling 7% per 10 kg lost.

assertions.text: A survey of 1,226 patients found sagging, facial volume loss and hair shedding reported more often the more weight was lost.
assertions.quote: Responses ( n = 1226) were sorted by the percent body weight lost and categorized by medication regimen (glucagon-like peptide 1-receptor agonists; GLP-1RA, nonGLP-1RA, or combination therapy). Patients reported dermatologic and overall physical changes. Results Dermatologic effects were reported more frequently with greater weight loss.
assertions.note: Rao et al. (2026) evaluated 1,226 survey respondents and found reports of skin sagging, decreased facial volume, and hair loss increased significantly with greater weight loss.

assertions.text: A systematic review of the plastic-surgery literature found it limited by study bias.
assertions.quote: Although limited by study biases, this systematic review can help the plastic surgery community prepare for the rising needs of this patient population by understanding the risk and benefit profile of GLP-1 receptor agonists and developing clear clinical practice guidelines.
assertions.note: Daneshgaran et al. (2025) noted in their systematic review that existing literature is limited by study biases.

assertions.text: Both US labels list hair loss (about 3–6% on drug against about 1% on placebo, mostly in women, linked to weight reduction).
assertions.quote: Hair loss adverse reactions in WEGOVY injection-treated patients were associated with weight reduction. In a pool of studies 2, 3, and 4, hair loss was reported in 3.3% of patients treated with WEGOVY 2.4 mg (4% female, 0.9% male) and in 1% of patients treated with placebo (2% female, 0 male).
assertions.note: Both US labels report hair loss in approximately 3–6% on active drug versus 1% on placebo, predominantly in females, associated with weight reduction.

assertions.text: The semaglutide label also lists altered skin sensation.
assertions.quote: Dysesthesia, and related events of altered skin sensations including paresthesia, pain of skin, sensitive skin, and burning skin sensation, occurred in clinical trials with WEGOVY injection and tablet.
assertions.note: The Wegovy prescribing information includes dysesthesia and altered skin sensation events.

assertions.text: Facial volume loss is not a labelled adverse reaction.
assertions.quote: Notably, although considerations about facial fat loss and accelerated aging are important, these are not mentioned in the Ozempic prescribing information.
assertions.note: Daneshgaran et al. (2025) note that facial fat loss is not mentioned in the prescribing information.

assertions.text: UK product information also lists hair loss: 2.5% on Wegovy and 4.9% on Mounjaro in the weight-management trials, against 1.0% on placebo.
assertions.quote: Hair loss was reported in 2.5% of patients treated with semaglutide 2.4 mg and in 1.0% of patients treated with placebo.
assertions.note: The UK SmPCs report hair loss in 2.5% of Wegovy patients and 4.9% of Mounjaro weight-management patients, versus 1.0% on placebo.

assertions.text: Whether these drugs act on facial fat or skin cells beyond the effect of weight loss rests on cell studies and has not been tested in people.
assertions.quote: Whether GLP-1 also acts directly on skin cells independently of weight is an open, actively studied question.
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni (2026) points out that whether GLP-1 acts directly on skin cells independently of weight loss remains an open question.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Counsel before, record during, refer when asked.
Raise facial volume change and hair shedding before treatment starts; the Hormonaly guide advises this especially for older patients. During treatment, photograph the face with consent, and support the protein intake and resistance training the guide recommends to protect lean mass. When a patient wants the face restored, refer to a qualified aesthetic or dermatology colleague. Published advice on restoration is expert opinion, the main consensus statement was developed with industry involvement, and randomized trials of fillers and devices in these patients are registered without results. Decisions about the medicine itself stay with the prescriber and the patient.
Before: set expectations about face and hair
During: photographs with consent, protect lean mass
When asked: refer for restoration
Narration: Three mom…
units.sourceNote: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 12, 14 · Nikolis 2025 · ClinicalTrials.gov, checked 24 Sep 2026

assertions.text: The Hormonaly guide advises clinicians to raise facial volume loss and hair shedding before treatment starts, especially for older patients.
assertions.quote: Pre-empt the aesthetics: discuss facial-volume loss and laxity ("Ozempic face") before starting, especially in older patients.
assertions.note: The pocket guide recommends discussing facial volume loss before starting GLP-1 therapy, noting it is most pronounced in older patients, and noting telogen effluvium can follow rapid weight loss.

assertions.text: The Hormonaly guide recommends protein intake and resistance training to protect lean mass during treatment.
assertions.quote: Treat a GLP-1 agonist as an endocrine intervention with aesthetic and musculoskeletal consequences: pair it with adequate protein and resistance training to defend lean mass, watch nutritional adequacy at reduced intake, and set realistic expectations about facial volume.
assertions.note: The guide explicitly advises pairing GLP-1 therapy with adequate protein and resistance training to defend lean mass.

assertions.text: Published clinical advice on restoring facial volume after medication-driven weight loss is based on expert opinion.
assertions.quote: Given the surge in popularity of mdWL medications, high‐quality research such as randomized controlled trials are lacking. Therefore, for such a heterogeneous topic (i.e., the aesthetic needs of mdWL patients), the application of methods aiming to increase the homogeneity of clinical guidelines is useful and appropriate.
assertions.note: The Delphi consensus paper notes that randomized controlled trials are lacking and guidelines had to be formulated based on expert consensus.

assertions.text: The main consensus statement on aesthetic management of medication-driven weight loss was developed with industry involvement.
assertions.quote: Funding: This research was supported by an unrestricted educational grant from Galderma (Uppsala, Sweden). Panelists were reimbursed for their time.
assertions.note: The consensus study was supported by an educational grant from Galderma, included a Galderma employee, and panel members declared relationships with aesthetic companies.

assertions.text: Randomized clinical trials investigating fillers and devices for facial volume and laxity after GLP-1 weight loss are registered without posted results.
assertions.quote: Study type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: PHASE4; allocation: RANDOMIZED; masking: SINGLE; enrollment: 48 (ESTIMATED)
assertions.note: Registered interventional trials evaluating calcium hydroxylapatite and ultrasound devices in GLP-1 patients are randomized and indicate results have not been posted.

units.text:
Fictional case
Ten months in, and unhappy with the mirror.
A 58-year-old patient has taken semaglutide for obesity for ten months, prescribed by her physician, and has lost 18% of her body weight. Her blood pressure and glucose have improved. She is distressed by hollow cheeks, new laxity along the jaw and more hair in her brush, and asks whether she should stop the injections. This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence; there is one right first move.
Facial volume loss tracks the weight lost
Hair loss is a labelled side effect, more common in women
The indication is responding; the medicine decision is the prescriber's
Narration: Picture a fifty-eight-year-old patient, fictional and built from this lesson's evidence. She has taken semaglutide for obesity for ten months, prescribed by her physician, and has lost eighteen percent of her body weight. Her blood pressure and g…
units.sourceNote: Sharma 2025 · Rao 2026 · Wegovy label 2026 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 12

assertions.text: In studies of patients on GLP-1 receptor agonists, facial volume loss tracks the amount of weight lost.
assertions.quote: Linear regression showed a loss of 7% facial volume for every 10 kg of weight lost (r = 0.063, SE = 0.003, P = .0293).
assertions.note: Sharma 2025 demonstrated that midfacial volume loss correlated with weight loss magnitude.

assertions.text: Hair loss is a labeled side effect of semaglutide, reported more frequently in women and linked to weight reduction.
assertions.quote: Hair loss adverse reactions in WEGOVY injection-treated patients were associated with weight reduction. In a pool of studies 2, 3, and 4, hair loss was reported in 3.3% of patients treated with WEGOVY 2.4 mg (4% female, 0.9% male) and in 1% of patients treated with placebo (2% female, 0 male).
assertions.note: The prescribing information notes that hair loss reactions were associated with weight reduction and occurred at higher rates in females.

units.text:
What do you do first?
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Tell her to stop the injections; her face matters more than the scale.
Explanation: That is a medication decision made on one side effect, outside her prescriber's care, and it sets aside an indication that is working.
Correct answer: Acknowledge the change, explain that it follows the weight lost, record it with consented photographs, and take the stop-or-continue question to her prescriber, with a referral for restoration if she wants one.
Explanation: Right. Counsel, record, refer. The medicine decision stays with her prescriber, and restoration goes to someone qualified to provide it.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Reassure her that her face will fill out again once her weight settles.
Explanation: That promise has no evidence behind it; no study found for this course followed facial volume after the w…

assertions.text: Facial volume loss following GLP-1 agonist therapy tracks with the amount of weight lost.
assertions.quote: Linear regression showed a loss of 7% facial volume for every 10 kg of weight lost (r = 0.063, SE = 0.003, P = .0293).
assertions.note: Sharma et al. showed a direct relationship between midfacial volume loss and total weight loss.

units.text:
Which statement about facial change on semaglutide or tirzepatide matches the evidence as of September 2026?
Explanation: Name the evidence type before the effect: here, small observational studies.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Randomized trials show these drugs age facial skin directly.
Explanation: No randomized trial has measured the face, and a direct effect on skin is a hypothesis from cell studies.
Correct answer: Facial volume loss is reported in small observational studies and tracks the amount of weight lost; no randomized trial has measured it.
Explanation: Correct. Observational, small, and consistent with weight loss as the driver.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Facial volume loss is a labelled adverse reaction in the US prescribing information.
Explanation: Hair loss is labelled. Facial volume loss is not.

assertions.text: Facial volume loss on GLP-1 receptor agonists is reported in small observational studies and correlates with the amount of weight lost.
assertions.quote: Linear regression showed a loss of 7% facial volume for every 10 kg of weight lost (r = 0.063, SE = 0.003, P = .0293).
assertions.note: Sharma et al. showed in a 20-patient retrospective cohort that midfacial volume loss correlated with total weight lost.

assertions.text: Hair loss is an adverse reaction listed in US prescribing information for semaglutide, while facial volume loss is not labelled.
assertions.quote: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%) in adults or pediatric patients aged 12 years and older are: nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, abdominal pain, dysesthesia, headache, fatigue, dyspepsia, dizziness, abdominal distension, eructation, hypoglycemia in patients with type 2 diabetes, flatulence, gastroenteritis, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and hair loss.
assertions.note: The Wegovy FDA prescribing information lists hair loss among adverse reactions, while facial volume loss is not included.

units.text:
Lesson 3.3 · Concept
Inflammation that comes with age.
Inflammaging is the chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that rises with age. In older adults, higher IL-6 and CRP predict frailty and death. One proposed source is the gut. In mice, a high-fat diet raises circulating bacterial lipopolysaccharide, and infusing it reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance. In 12 healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised plasma endotoxin within four hours. Whether a leaky gut drives skin disease in people has not been shown.
Inflammaging: low-grade, sterile, age-related
Metabolic endotoxaemia: gut bacterial LPS in the blood
Gut to skin in people: not shown
Narration: Ageing brings a slow rise in background inflammation, called inflammaging. It is low-grade and sterile, and in older adults higher IL-6 and C-reactive protein predict frailty, disability and death. One proposed source is the gut. …
units.sourceNote: Franceschi 2000 · Ferrucci & Fabbri 2018 · Cani 2007 · Erridge 2007 · Camilleri 2019

assertions.text: Inflammaging is the chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that rises with age.
assertions.quote: In this paper we extend the "network theory of aging," and we argue that a global reduction in the capacity to cope with a variety of stressors and a concomitant progressive increase in proinflammatory status are major characteristics of the aging process. This phenomenon, which we will refer to as "inflamm-aging," is provoked by a continuous antigenic load and stress.
assertions.note: Franceschi describes inflamm-aging as a progressive increase in proinflammatory status characterizing aging.

assertions.text: In older adults, higher levels of IL-6 and CRP predict frailty, disability, and death.
assertions.quote: High levels of pro-inflammatory markers in the blood and other tissues are often detected in older individuals and predict the risk of cardiovascular diseases, frailty, multimorbidity, and decline of physical and cognitive function.
assertions.note: Ferrucci and Fabbri report that elevated inflammatory markers in older individuals predict frailty, disability, and mortality.

assertions.text: In mice, a high-fat diet raises circulating bacterial lipopolysaccharide, and infusing it reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance.
assertions.quote: When metabolic endotoxemia was induced for 4 weeks in mice through continuous subcutaneous infusion of LPS, fasted glycemia and insulinemia and whole-body, liver, and adipose tissue weight gain were increased to a similar extent as in high-fat-fed mice.
assertions.note: Cani et al. demonstrate that high-fat diet increases plasma LPS and subcutaneous LPS infusion induces weight gain and insulin resistance in mice.

assertions.text: In 12 healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised plasma endotoxin within four hours.
assertions.quote: Plasma endotoxin and endotoxin neutralization capacity were measured for 4 h in 12 healthy men after no meal, 3 cigarettes, a high-fat meal, or a high-fat meal with 3 cigarettes by using the limulus assay. Results Baseline endotoxin concentrations were 8.2 pg/mL (interquartile range: 3.4-13.5 pg/mL) but increased significantly (P < 0.05) by approximately 50% after a high-fat meal
assertions.note: Erridge et al. observed significant increases in plasma endotoxin measured over 4 hours following a high-fat meal in 12 healthy men.

assertions.text: Whether restoring the gut barrier improves disease outside the gut (such as skin disease) remains unproven in humans.
assertions.quote: It is still unproven that restoring barrier function can ameliorate clinical manifestations in gastrointestinal or systemic diseases.
assertions.note: Camilleri confirms that restoring intestinal barrier function has not been proven to improve systemic or extra-intestinal diseases.

units.text:
The evidence
Thirty-nine trials of probiotics for eczema.
An independent Cochrane review pooled 39 randomized trials, with 2,599 participants, of oral probiotics for eczema. Probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated symptoms, and investigator-rated severity fell by less than the minimum clinically important difference. A 2024 European task-force meta-analysis in children without food allergy reported a significant fall in severity scores.
39 RCTs
in the Cochrane review of oral probiotics for treating eczema
2,599 participants · little or no difference in patient-rated symptoms (moderate-certainty evidence)
What it means: The most direct test of 'treat the gut, help the skin' in a common inflammatory skin disease shows, at most, a small effect. GRADE B for little or no benefit a patient would notice.
What it does not mean: It does not rule out benefit from particul…
units.sourceNote: Makrgeorgou 2018 (Cochrane) · Vassilopoulou 2024 · Suez 2019

assertions.text: An independent Cochrane review pooled 39 randomized trials with 2,599 participants evaluating oral probiotics for eczema.
assertions.quote: We included 39 randomised controlled trials involving 2599 randomised participants.
assertions.note: The Cochrane review included 39 RCTs with 2,599 randomized participants.

assertions.text: In the Cochrane review, probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated eczema symptoms, supported by moderate-certainty evidence.
assertions.quote: Probiotics probably make little or no difference in participant- or parent-rated symptoms of eczema (13 trials; 754 participants): symptom severity on a scale from 0 to 20 was 0.44 points lower after probiotic treatment (95% confidence interval (CI) -1.22 to 0.33; moderate-quality evidence).
assertions.note: The Cochrane review concluded probiotics probably make little or no difference in participant- or parent-rated symptoms with moderate-quality evidence.

assertions.text: In the Cochrane review, investigator-rated severity fell by less than the minimum clinically important difference.
assertions.quote: On a scale of 0 to 103 for total Severity Scoring of Atopic Dermatitis (SCORAD), a score combining investigator-rated eczema severity score and participant scoring for eczema symptoms of itch and sleep loss was 3.91 points lower after probiotic treatment than after no probiotic treatment (95% CI -5.86 to -1.96; low-quality evidence). The minimum clinically important difference for SCORAD has been estimated to be 8.7 points.
assertions.note: The reduction in SCORAD was 3.91 points, compared to an estimated minimum clinically important difference of 8.7 points.

assertions.text: A 2024 European task-force meta-analysis in children without food allergy reported a significant fall in eczema severity scores (SCORAD) with probiotics.
assertions.quote: A meta-analysis of 20 RCTs assessing probiotics, alone or combined with prebiotics, revealed a significant reduction in SCORAD scores, suggesting a consistent trend in alleviating AD symptoms in children without food allergies.
assertions.note: The 2024 EAACI task force meta-analysis found a significant reduction in SCORAD scores in children without food allergies.

units.sourceNote: Makrgeorgou 2018 · Parodi 2008 · Lebwohl 2026 · Faurschou 2015 · Reynolds 2019 · Depommier 2019

assertions.text: Probiotic capsules have been tested on skin outcomes in randomized controlled trials.
assertions.quote: We included 39 randomised controlled trials involving 2599 randomised participants.
assertions.note: A Cochrane systematic review evaluated 39 randomized controlled trials of oral probiotics for treating eczema.

assertions.text: Rifaximin for rosacea in patients with small intestinal bacterial overgrowth has been tested on skin outcomes in a randomized controlled trial.
assertions.quote: Patients positive for SIBO were randomized to receive rifaximin therapy (1200 mg/day for 10 days) or placebo.
assertions.note: A randomized trial tested rifaximin versus placebo in rosacea patients with SIBO and assessed clearance of cutaneous lesions.

assertions.text: Tirzepatide added to a psoriasis biologic has been tested on skin outcomes in a randomized controlled trial.
assertions.quote: Participants were randomized (1:1) to ixekizumab plus tirzepatide or ixekizumab as adjunct to diet and exercise in both treatment arms.
assertions.note: A randomized phase 3b trial evaluated ixekizumab with or without tirzepatide for skin clearance (PASI scores) in adults with moderate to severe psoriasis.

assertions.text: A high-fibre, plant-rich diet has been tested in clinical trials in humans for metabolic and non-skin outcomes rather than skin endpoints.
assertions.quote: Dietary fiber and minimally processed, plant-rich eating consistently improve metabolic and inflammatory markers and feed short-chain-fatty-acid–producing microbes that support the barrier GRADE A.[1]
assertions.note: Meta-analyses and clinical guides confirm dietary fiber has been tested extensively in human trials for cardiometabolic, mortality, and gut barrier outcomes rather than skin conditions.

assertions.text: Akkermansia supplementation has been tested in humans on metabolic and safety parameters rather than skin endpoints.
assertions.quote: The primary endpoints were on safety, tolerability and metabolic parameters (i.e., insulin resistance, circulating lipids, visceral adiposity, body mass).
assertions.note: A proof-of-concept randomized controlled trial evaluated Akkermansia muciniphila in humans for safety, tolerability, and metabolic parameters.

assertions.text: A 'leaky gut' stack consisting of L-glutamine, zinc carnosine, and BPC-157 has little or no human outcome data.
assertions.quote: The popular "leaky gut" repair stack — L-glutamine, zinc carnosine, and peptides such as BPC-157 — has mechanistic and preclinical rationale for barrier support, but human outcome data are limited, and BPC-157 carries the regulatory constraints of Chapter 15 GRADE D.[5]
assertions.note: The clinical reference guide states that barrier repair stacks containing L-glutamine, zinc carnosine, and BPC-157 have limited human outcome data and rely mostly on preclinical evidence.

units.text:
What stands behind it?
One at a time: what has actually been tested?
Sorting item (the learner sorts this statement; the course's claim is only the category): "Probiotic capsules" → Tested on skin in randomized trials
Explanation: Thirty-nine trials pooled by Cochrane: little or no difference in patient-rated eczema symptoms (B). Newer analyses in children report small gains.
Sorting item (the learner sorts this statement; the course's claim is only the category): "Rifaximin for rosacea with bacterial overgrowth" → Tested on skin in randomized trials
Explanation: One small single-centre randomized trial: rosacea improved after the overgrowth was cleared (C). A prescription antibiotic, chosen after testing.
Sorting item (the learner sorts this statement; the course's claim is only the category): "Tirzepatide added to a psoriasis biologic" → Tested on skin in randomized trials
Explanation:…

assertions.text: A Cochrane systematic review pooling 39 trials found that probiotics make little or no difference in patient-rated eczema symptoms.
assertions.quote: Probiotics probably make little or no difference in participant- or parent-rated symptoms of eczema (13 trials; 754 participants): symptom severity on a scale from 0 to 20 was 0.44 points lower after probiotic treatment (95% confidence interval (CI) -1.22 to 0.33; moderate-quality evidence).
assertions.note: Supported by the Cochrane review abstract, which includes 39 trials and reports little or no difference in participant- or parent-rated symptoms.

assertions.text: Newer analyses of probiotics in children report small gains in eczema.
assertions.quote: Probiotics may make little or no difference in QoL for people with eczema nor in investigator-rated eczema severity score (combined with participant scoring for eczema symptoms of itch and sleep loss); for the latter, the observed effect was small and of uncertain clinical significance.
assertions.note: The Cochrane review update (predominantly evaluating pediatric trials) found that probiotics slightly reduced investigator-rated eczema severity scores, though the observed effect was small.

recheck.note: The Cochrane review update (predominantly evaluating pediatric trials) found that probiotics slightly reduced investigator-rated eczema severity scores, though the observed effect was small.

assertions.text: In a randomized trial, rosacea improved after small intestinal bacterial overgrowth was cleared with rifaximin.
assertions.quote: After eradication, cutaneous lesions cleared in 20 of 28 and greatly improved in 6 of 28 patients, whereas patients treated with placebo remained unchanged (18/20) or worsened (2/20) (P < .001).
assertions.note: Supported by the randomized trial abstract showing rosacea lesions cleared or improved following SIBO eradication with rifaximin.

assertions.text: An open-label phase 3b trial of 274 participants found significantly more complete clearance (PASI 100) at 36 weeks when tirzepatide was added to ixekizumab.
assertions.quote: In this randomized clinical trial of 274 participants, 27.1% receiving ixekizumab plus tirzepatide vs 5.8% receiving ixekizumab alone simultaneously achieved Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI) 100 and 10% or greater weight reduction; 40.6% vs 29.0% achieved PASI 100 at week 36, respectively. Treatment differences were significant.
assertions.note: Supported by the TOGETHER-PsO trial results at week 36.

assertions.text: An earlier 20-person placebo-controlled trial of liraglutide found no significant effect on psoriasis.
assertions.quote: After 8 weeks of treatment, no significant change in PASI was found in the liraglutide group (mean±standard deviation: -2.6 ± 2.1) compared with the placebo group (-1.3 ± 2.4) (P = 0.228).
assertions.note: Supported by the randomized trial finding no significant change in PASI between liraglutide and placebo in 20 patients.

assertions.text: Tirzepatide's UK licence does not include psoriasis as an approved indication.
assertions.quote: 4.1 Therapeutic indications Mounjaro is indicated: 1. For the treatment of adults, adolescents and children aged 10 years and above with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus as an adjunct to diet and exercise: • as monotherapy when metformin is considered inappropriate due to intolerance or contraindications • in addition to other medicinal products for the treatment of diabetes.
assertions.note: Supported by the UK Summary of Product Characteristics, which lists only type 2 diabetes mellitus and weight management.

assertions.text: A systematic review and meta-analysis on carbohydrate quality rated the certainty of evidence moderate for dietary fibre's protective effects on critical health outcomes.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Diet first, a bottle last.
When a patient links their skin to their gut, start with what has evidence: diet quality, treating metabolic disease directly, and established treatment for the skin condition itself. A widely used commercial zonulin assay has been shown to detect proteins other than zonulin, so a result cannot tell you whether a gut is leaky. Restoring barrier function has not been shown to improve disease outside the gut. Investigational peptides sold for gut repair come last, if at all.
Start with diet, metabolic health and the skin diagnosis
Zonulin tests may not measure zonulin
Gut-repair peptides: last, if at all
Narration: Patients often link their skin to their gut. Start where the evidence is. Diet quality, treatment of metabolic disease and the established treatment for the skin condition itself all come first. Be careful with tests. A widely …

assertions.text: A widely used commercial zonulin assay has been shown to detect proteins other than zonulin, meaning a result cannot determine whether a gut is leaky.

A patient asks for a zonulin blood test to prove that her rosacea comes from a leaky gut. What is the most accurate reply?
Explanation: Ask what a test measures before you ask what it shows.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The test will show whether her gut barrier is causing the rosacea.
Explanation: A widely used zonulin assay detects other proteins, and a zonulin result cannot tell you what is causing her rosacea.
Correct answer: The test is unreliable and would not change care: treat the rosacea on its own evidence, and assess any gut symptoms clinically.
Explanation: Correct. The small trial that linked gut bacteria to rosacea used breath testing and clinical assessment, and no zonulin test.

assertions.text: A randomized trial evaluating bacterial overgrowth in rosacea used breath testing and found that eradication of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth improved cutaneous rosacea lesions.
assertions.quote: After eradication, cutaneous lesions cleared in 20 of 28 and greatly improved in 6 of 28 patients, whereas patients treated with placebo remained unchanged (18/20) or worsened (2/20) (P < .001).
assertions.note: Parodi et al. assessed SIBO using breath tests and found significant clearing/improvement of rosacea lesions following antibiotic eradication.
