Matrix peptides and wound healing · three lessons
Lesson 4.1 Copper peptides · Lesson 4.2 Signal peptides, oral collagen and SNAP-25 mimics · Lesson 4.3 Repair peptides and the compounding line.
Module 04 · Matrix peptides and wound healing
The peptide your patient already bought.
Most skin peptides reach your clinic before any evidence does. In three lessons you will sort them by what the human trials actually show, who paid for those trials, and where each one stands with the regulator.
4.1 Copper peptides: GHK and GHK-Cu
4.2 Signal peptides, oral collagen and the 'topical Botox' family
4.3 Repair peptides, one negative trial, and the compounding line
Set your path
How will you use this module?
The evidence, grades and regulatory status are the same for everyone. What changes is the 'what you do next' at the end of each lesson, so it fits what your licence lets you do.
Choose the one c…

Mechanism
A plasma tripeptide with a copper habit.
GHK is a tripeptide found in human plasma, first described in 1973. Bound to copper it becomes GHK-Cu, which is proposed to deliver copper to enzymes such as superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase and to switch on wound-healing and antioxidant gene programmes. Most of that mechanistic literature comes from the group that discovered the peptide.
Endogenous: GHK circulates in human plasma
Proposed: copper delivery to matrix and antioxidant enzymes
Mechanism register only — written largely by the originator
Narration: Start with the molecule. GHK is a three-amino-acid peptide that circulates in human plasma; it was first described in 1973. It binds copper readily, and the copper complex, GHK-Cu, is what skin-care labels mean when they say copper peptide. The proposed mechanism is that GHK-Cu delivers copper to enzymes that build and protect…
units.sourceNote: Pickart & Thaler 1973 · Pickart 2008, 2015, 2018 · Peptide Pocket Guide

assertions.text: GHK is a tripeptide (three-amino-acid peptide) found in human plasma.
assertions.quote: GHK is a tripeptide with the amino acid sequence glycyl-histidyl-lysine. It naturally occurs in human plasma, saliva, and urine.
assertions.note: Pickart (2015) explicitly states that GHK is a tripeptide present in human plasma.

assertions.text: GHK was first described in 1973.
assertions.quote: The human copper-binding peptide GHK-Cu (glycyl-l-histidyl-l-lysine) is a small, naturally occurring tri-peptide present in human plasma that also can be released from tissues in case of an injury. Since its discovery in 1973, GHK-Cu established itself as a powerful protective and regenerative ingredient, which is currently widely used in skin and hair products
assertions.note: Pickart & Margolina (2018) note that GHK-Cu was discovered in 1973.

assertions.text: GHK binds copper to form GHK-Cu.
assertions.quote: Subsequent studies established this activity as a tripeptide with an amino acid sequence glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine with a strong affinity for copper that readily formed the complex GHK-Cu.
assertions.note: Pickart (2015) confirms GHK has strong affinity for copper and forms GHK-Cu.

assertions.text: GHK-Cu is proposed to deliver copper to enzymes such as superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase.
assertions.quote: Copper-binding tripeptide; modulates copper delivery to enzymes including superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase.
assertions.note: The Peptide Pocket Guide confirms the proposed mechanism of delivering copper to superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase.

assertions.text: GHK-Cu is proposed to switch on wound-healing and antioxidant gene programs / shift gene expression toward wound healing.
assertions.quote: Activates wound-healing gene expression programs via copper-dependent signaling.
assertions.note: The Peptide Pocket Guide confirms GHK-Cu activates wound-healing and antioxidant gene programs.

assertions.text: Most of the mechanistic literature on GHK/GHK-Cu comes from the group that discovered the peptide (Loren Pickart's group).
assertions.quote: Decades of dermatologic research (Pickart et al., 2015, 2017) support roles in collagen synthesis, antioxidant defense, and skin/hair benefits.
assertions.note: The Peptide Pocket Guide cites Pickart et al. as the primary evidence base for GHK and GHK-Cu.

units.text:
Human evidence
One indexed randomized trial.
A search of PubMed in September 2026 found one randomized controlled trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin: 2006, healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing. The cosmetic trials cited for anti-ageing claims are manufacturer-sponsored and not indexed. Both Hormonaly guides grade topical use C.
1
indexed randomized trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin
Miller et al., 2006 — healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing, not photoageing
What it means: The human evidence for topical GHK-Cu is small: one small indexed trial plus sponsor-run cosmetic studies. GRADE C is the honest ceiling.
What it does not mean: It does not show that GHK-Cu fails, that it treats photoageing, or anything about injecting it. A thin evidence base is an unknown, not a negative.
units.sourceNote: Miller 2006 · Peptide Pocket Guide · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology

assertions.text: Miller et al. (2006) conducted a randomized controlled trial evaluating topical GHK-Cu for healing after CO2 laser resurfacing in human skin.
assertions.quote: To evaluate the role of skin care products that contain a copper tripeptide complex, glycyl-l-histidyl-l-lysine-Cu(2+) (GHK-Cu), in treating carbon dioxide (CO(2)) laser-resurfaced skin.
assertions.note: The abstract confirms an RCT of GHK-Cu products on CO2 laser-resurfaced skin.

assertions.text: The cosmetic trials cited for topical GHK-Cu anti-ageing claims are manufacturer-sponsored and not indexed in PubMed.
assertions.quote: Leyden J et al. (multiple cosmetic RCTs, 2002 onward, manufacturer-sponsored) [not indexed]
assertions.note: The Peptide Pocket Guide flags the cosmetic RCTs for GHK-Cu as manufacturer-sponsored and not indexed.

assertions.text: Both Hormonaly reference guides assign a GRADE C rating to topical GHK-Cu use.
assertions.quote:
Topical GHK-Cu
Collagen, skin repair · GRADE C small trials · Cat. 1
(topical)
assertions.note: Both guides explicitly grade topical GHK-Cu as GRADE C.

units.text:
Four registers
Keep the four answers apart.
Every peptide question has four separate answers. For GHK-Cu they point in different directions, which is exactly why they must not be blended into one sentence.
Mechanism
Plausible
Copper delivery to matrix and antioxidant enzymes; gene-expression data from the originator
Human evidence
Topical: GRADE C · Injectable: none
One small indexed RCT and sponsor-run cosmetic trials; no randomized trials of injection
Regulatory status (US, 14 May 2026; UK, September 2026)
Non-injectable: 503A Category 1
Category 1 means FDA is still evaluating and does not intend to act against compounders who meet its conditions; an advisory-committee consultation is planned before the end of February 2027. The injectable route has no such standing. In the UK, a GHK-Cu serum sold for appearance is a cosmetic, and cosmetics law excludes anything injected.
Open questio…
units.sourceNote: Registry m04 · FDA 503A category list, updated 14 May 2026 · UK Cosmetics Regulation art. 2 · MHRA Guidance Note 8

assertions.text: GHK-Cu functions through copper delivery to matrix and antioxidant enzymes, with broad gene-expression modulation data documented by the originator.
assertions.quote: The most distinctive feature of GHK is its ability to form complexes with copper (II) [ 51 ]. This is very important since copper is required for more than a dozen vital enzymes in the human body and skin including those that participate in connective tissue formation, antioxidant defense, and cellular respiration.
assertions.note: Pickart (2015) describes GHK-Cu delivering copper required for connective tissue and antioxidant enzymes as well as extensive gene modulation.

assertions.text: Human clinical evidence for topical GHK-Cu consists of small trials and sponsor-run cosmetic studies, whereas there are no randomized controlled trials of injectable GHK-Cu.
assertions.quote: Clinical caveat. Evidence base: topical cosmetic RCTs (cosmeceutical use) and preclinical wound-healing models — injectable human use rests on anecdote, no RCTs.
assertions.note: The Peptide Pocket Guide confirms the clinical evidence base is limited to topical cosmetic RCTs and preclinical models, with no injectable RCTs.

assertions.text: In the US as of May 2026, non-injectable GHK-Cu is in 503A Category 1 with an advisory committee consultation planned before late February 2027, whereas the injectable route has no Category 1 standing.
assertions.quote: GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) will be added back to category 1. FDA has announced it intends to consult the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) before the end of February 2027 regarding the potential inclusion of GHK-Cu on the 503A bulks list.
assertions.note: FDA 503A updates confirm non-injectable GHK-Cu was restored to Category 1, injectable was withdrawn, and a PCAC consultation is scheduled before end of February 2027.

assertions.text: Under UK cosmetics regulation, any substance or mixture intended to be injected into the human body is excluded from being classified as a cosmetic product.
assertions.quote: 2. For the purposes of point (a) of paragraph 1, a substance or mixture intended to be ingested, inhaled, injected or implanted into the human body shall not be considered to be a cosmetic product.
assertions.note: Article 2(2) of UK Retained Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 explicitly excludes injected substances from cosmetic product classification.

assertions.text: Human skin penetration data for GHK-Cu are evaluated in vitro and depend on the model and analytical methodology used.
assertions.quote: The skin retention and penetration characteristics of copper applied as glycyl- l -histidyl- l -lysine cuprate diacetate were evaluated in vitro in order to assess the potential for its transdermal delivery as anti-inflammatory agent.
assertions.note: Hostynek et al. report in vitro evaluation of skin retention and penetration characteristics across different skin layers.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Serum yes, syringe no.
Topical GHK-Cu is a reasonable cosmetic conversation at GRADE C. Injected GHK-Cu is a different product: no randomized trials, injection-site pain and rash are common because copper irritates tissue, and in the US the injectable route sits outside the Category 1 listing. In the UK, anything injected falls outside cosmetics law, and MHRA decides whether it is a medicine from its claims, form and use.
Topical: modest, small-trial support
Injectable: anecdote, common local reactions
Say which route you mean every time
Narration: Here is what that means in the room. Topical GHK-Cu is a reasonable cosmetic conversation, as long as you describe the evidence honestly: small trials, modest effects, grade C. Injected GHK-Cu is not the same product in a stronger form. There are no randomized trials of injection, injection-site pain and rash are commo…
units.sourceNote: Peptide Pocket Guide · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 15 · FDA 503A categories · UK Cosmetics Regulation art. 2 · MHRA Guidance Note 8

assertions.text: Topical GHK-Cu has modest, small-trial evidence supporting cosmetic use (GRADE C).
assertions.quote: GHK-Cu, a copper-binding tripeptide, has a long mechanistic record for collagen and matrix synthesis and modest clinical support in topical use GRADE C.[1]
assertions.note: Topical GHK-Cu has small-trial support and is graded C in the cited clinical guide.

assertions.text: There are no randomized controlled trials evaluating injectable GHK-Cu, and clinical use rests on anecdote.
assertions.quote: Evidence base: topical cosmetic RCTs (cosmeceutical use) and preclinical wound-healing models — injectable human use rests on anecdote, no RCTs.
assertions.note: The clinical guide confirms that injectable human use of GHK-Cu rests on anecdote with no RCTs.

assertions.text: Injection-site pain, rash, and irritation are common with injectable GHK-Cu because copper irritates tissue.
assertions.quote: Second, local reactions: injectable GHK-Cu commonly causes injection-site irritation and inflammation (copper is locally irritating); standard measures help — rotate sites, lower the concentration or volume, apply a cold compress, and pause if persistent.
assertions.note: The guide notes that injectable GHK-Cu commonly causes injection-site irritation because copper is locally irritating.

assertions.text: In the US, the injectable route of GHK-Cu sits outside the 503A Category 1 listing, which covers only non-injectable routes.
assertions.quote: On May 5, 2026, one of those nominators clarified that it intended to withdraw only its nomination of the injectable route of administration with respect to GHK-Cu and would like to retain its nomination for GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes of administration. GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) will be added back to category 1.
assertions.note: The FDA Category 1 listing specifies GHK-Cu except for injectable routes of administration following nominator clarification.

assertions.text: In the UK, injected substances fall outside cosmetic products regulations.
assertions.quote: 2. For the purposes of point (a) of paragraph 1, a substance or mixture intended to be ingested, inhaled, injected or implanted into the human body shall not be considered to be a cosmetic product.
assertions.note: Article 2 of the UK-retained cosmetics regulation explicitly excludes substances intended to be injected from the definition of a cosmetic product.

assertions.text: In the UK, the MHRA decides whether a product is a medicine based on factors including its claims/presentation, form, and use/function.
assertions.quote:
When classifying a product, the Agency looks at the way the product is presented (especially 
any claims) and at its function, that is, its effects (when administered) on human physiology. This is in line with the definition of a medicinal product that is set out in Regulation 2 of The 
Human Medicines Regulations 2012 (S.I 2012/1916)
assertions.note: MHRA classifies borderline products on a case-by-case basis based on presentation (claims), form, and physiological function.

units.text:
Lesson 4.2 · Concept
Three families, one question: who ran the trial?
Signal peptides such as palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) are meant to tell fibroblasts to make matrix. SNAP-25 mimics (Argireline and its longer cousin SNAP-8) and Leuphasyl, an enkephalin analogue, are meant to quieten expression lines. Oral collagen peptides are swallowed, not applied. All three families have a trial record, and in all three the question that matters most is who funded it.
Signal peptides: 'make more matrix'
SNAP-25 mimics: 'relax the line'
Oral collagen: the supplement aisle
Narration: Lesson two covers three families that fill the cosmetic and supplement shelves. Signal peptides, like palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, sold as Matrixyl, are fragments of matrix proteins meant to tell fibroblasts to make more collagen. SNAP-25 mimics, Argireline and its longer cousin SNAP-8, copy part of a nerve…
units.sourceNote: Lupo & Cole 2007 · Lintner & Peschard 2000 · Blanes-Mira 2002 · Errante 2020

assertions.text: Signal peptides such as palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) are fragments of matrix proteins intended to signal fibroblasts to stimulate collagen and extracellular matrix synthesis.
assertions.quote: Matrixyl ® is the new version of Pentapeptide-4 (palmitoylated Lys-Thr-Thr-Lys-Ser-OH), the well-known signal peptide fragment of the C-terminal propeptide of type I collagen. It stimulates feedback regulation of new collagen synthesis and ECM proteins.
assertions.note: Errante 2020 describes Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4) as a fragment of the propeptide of type I collagen that stimulates new collagen and ECM synthesis.

assertions.text: SNAP-25 mimics such as Argireline and SNAP-8 emulate parts of the nerve-terminal protein targeted by botulinum neurotoxin to reduce muscle contraction and expression lines.
assertions.quote: One of the best known peptide with neurotransmitter-inhibiting properties is a synthetic hexapeptide, so-called acetyl hexapeptide-3 and coined Argireline . The sequence Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-NH 2 (Blanes-Mira et al., 2002 ), covers the N-terminal fragment domain of SNAP-25, promoting the inhibition of Ca 2+ -dependent catecholamine release through the interrupted formation of SNARE complex.
assertions.note: Errante 2020 confirms that Argireline covers the N-terminal domain of SNAP-25 and SNAP-8 mimics SNAP-25 to decrease muscle contraction.

assertions.text: Leuphasyl is an enkephalin analogue peptide used to reduce wrinkles and expression lines.
assertions.quote: Pentapeptide-18 ( Leuphasyl ) The pentapeptide-18 composed of the sequence H-Tyr-Ala-Gly-Phe-Leu-OH, was reported for the first time in 2015. It became one of the most popular active peptide ingredients in anti-aging formulations (Lipotec s.a., 2005 ). It acts like enkephalins, decreasing the ACh secretion in the synaptic cleft. Both instrumental and volunteer-involving studies acknowledge its effectiveness in wrinkles reduction (Dragomirescu et al., 2014 ).
assertions.note: Errante 2020 notes that Leuphasyl acts like enkephalins and reduces wrinkles.

assertions.text: Oral collagen peptides are consumed orally as dietary supplements and have a trial record that is predominantly small and industry funded.
assertions.quote: Oral collagen peptides show modest improvements in hydration, elasticity, and wrinkle parameters in randomized trials, though most are small and industry-funded GRADE C,[16] and topical GHK-Cu has decades of mechanistic and small-trial support for collagen stimulation GRADE C.[17]
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni 2026 notes that oral collagen peptides are backed by randomized trials that are mostly small and industry-funded.

units.text:
The evidence
Twenty-three trials, split by who paid.
Pooled, oral collagen trials show better hydration, elasticity and wrinkle scores, and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades them C. A 2025 meta-analysis split the same kind of trials by funding and by quality. The benefit appeared only in pharmaceutical-funded and low-quality trials. Unfunded and high-quality trials showed no effect.
23 RCTs
in the 2025 meta-analysis that split oral-collagen trials by funding and quality
1,474 participants
What it means: The pooled benefit of oral collagen disappears when you look only at independent or high-quality trials. The course keeps the guide's GRADE C and shows why a downgrade has been proposed to its author.
What it does not mean: It does not show collagen is harmful, and it does not rule out benefit for an individual. It is a statement about the evidence, and it says nothi…
units.sourceNote: Myung & Park, Am J Med 2025 · Pu 2023 · de Miranda 2021 · Kim 2018

assertions.text: Pooled oral collagen trials show improvements in skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkle scores.
assertions.quote: In the meta-analysis, a grouped analysis of studies showed favorable results of hydrolyzed collagen supplementation compared with placebo in terms of skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles.
assertions.note: Supported by the pooled meta-analysis findings.

assertions.text: The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide gives oral collagen peptides a GRADE C rating.
assertions.quote: Oral collagen peptides show modest improvements in hydration, elasticity, and wrinkle parameters in randomized trials, though most are small and industry-funded GRADE C,[16] and topical GHK-Cu has decades of mechanistic and small-trial support for collagen stimulation GRADE C.[17]
assertions.note: Supported by the guide's evidence rating.

assertions.text: A 2025 meta-analysis of 23 RCTs with 1,474 participants found that oral collagen benefits appeared only in pharmaceutical-funded and low-quality trials, whereas non-industry-funded and high-quality trials showed no significant effect.
assertions.quote: A total of 23 RCTs with 1474 participants were analyzed. In a meta-analysis of all 23 RCTs, collagen supplements significantly improved skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles. However, in the subgroup meta-analysis by funding source, studies not receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies revealed no effect of collagen supplements for improving skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles, while those receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies did show significant effects. Similarly, high-quality studies revealed no significant effect in all categories, while low-quality studies revealed a significant improvement in elasticity.
assertions.note: Supported by the 2025 meta-analysis abstract.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Cosmetic, supplement, drug: three rulebooks.
In the US, cosmetic peptides are cosmetic ingredients, not drugs, and their safety is assessed under a cosmetics framework. Oral collagen is a dietary supplement: it may not claim to treat disease, and product quality and content vary. Neither route has to prove efficacy before sale — which is why the funding question matters. In the UK, a peptide serum is a cosmetic: its responsible person needs a safety assessment and must notify the regulator before sale, and must be able to prove its claims. Oral collagen is a food supplement: no food may claim to prevent, treat or cure disease, and only authorised health claims may be used. In May 2026 the UK advertising regulator ruled a peptide serum's 'clinically proven' lifting claim misleading because the study behind it was small and uncontrolled.
Cosmetic ingredient: no eff…

The Responsible Person should: know which ingredients are used in their cosmetic product, including those which are harmful or nanomaterials know about restrictions on what can be put in cosmetic products keep an up to date document with information on the cosmetic product (called the ‘Product Information File’ or ‘PIF’) make any information on the packaging, labelling and instructions for the cosmetic product clearly visible let the Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS) know about the cosmetic product (called notification ) before it is made available to consumers tell OPSS about any serious harmful effects which are reported about the cosmetic product be able to prove that any claims made when marketing the product are correct

KPV, a tripeptide from the end of α-MSH, calms inflammation in mouse colitis and has no randomized human trial.

units.text:
The evidence
One abstract, no published trial.
As of September 2026 no randomized efficacy trial of BPC-157 in people has been published in full. FDA's July 2026 briefing found one randomized, placebo-controlled trial reported only as a 2005 meeting abstract: 53 people with ulcerative colitis, two weeks of treatment, and no significant difference from placebo. ClinicalTrials.gov adds a 2015 phase 1 safety study that never posted results, a completed 2025 single-arm product study with no results posted, and a randomized phase 1 trial after rotator-cuff surgery due to start in 2027.

One 2005 ulcerative-colitis trial exists only as a meeting abstract (no significant difference from placebo) · registered: phase 1 safety study (2015, no results) · single-arm product study (2025, no results) · randomized phase 1…

units.text:
Worked example
Two trials, one peptide: LL-37.
LL-37, the skin's own cathelicidin, is the one repair peptide with two randomized trials in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers. Read them in order.
First trial (2014)
Positive at low dose
First-in-human, randomized, dose-ranging; 34 patients
Second trial (2021)
Negative in the full cohort
Multicentre phase IIb, placebo-controlled; only a post hoc subgroup signal
Who ran them
The developer, both times
Sponsorship does not make a trial wrong; it is one more reason to wait for replication
Grade
C — inconsistent
A small positive trial followed by an adequately powered negative one
Callout: A small positive trial is a hypothesis. LL-37 is what happens when someone tests it.
units.sourceNote: Grönberg 2014 · Mahlapuu 2021 · Schauber & Gallo 2008

assertions.text: LL-37 is the skin's endogenous cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide.
assertions.quote: Cathelicidins are unique AMPs that protect the skin through 2 distinct pathways: (1) direct antimicrobial activity and (2) initiation of a host response resulting in cytokine release, inflammation, angiogenesis, and reepithelialization.
assertions.note: The abstract confirms that cathelicidins are skin antimicrobial peptides involved in defense and repair.

assertions.text: The 2014 first-in-human trial of LL-37 was a randomized, dose-ranging study of 34 patients with hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers that was positive at low dose.
assertions.quote: This first-in-man trial included 34 participants with VLUs and comprised a 3-week, open-label, run-in period on placebo, followed by a 4-week randomized double-blind treatment phase with twice weekly applications of LL-37 (0.5, 1.6, or 3.2 mg/mL) or placebo, and a 4-week follow-up.
assertions.note: The 2014 study was a first-in-man randomized dose-ranging trial in 34 patients showing improved healing at lower doses.

assertions.text: The 2021 multicentre phase IIb trial of LL-37 was negative in the full cohort, showing only a post hoc subgroup signal.
assertions.quote: Efficacy analysis performed on the full study population did not identify any significant improvement in healing in patients treated with LL‐37 as compared with the placebo. In contrast, a post hoc analysis revealed statistically significant improvement with LL‐37 treatment in several interrelated healing parameters in the subgroup of patients with large target wounds (a wound area of at least 10 cm 2 at randomization), which is a known negative prognostic factor for healing.
assertions.note: The phase IIb trial showed no significant healing improvement in the full cohort, with an improvement seen only in a post hoc subgroup analysis of large wounds.

assertions.text: Both clinical trials of LL-37 were run/sponsored by the peptide's developer.
assertions.quote: The study was financed by Promore Pharma AB, Solna, Sweden.
assertions.note: The provided text confirms the developer sponsored the 2021 trial, but does not provide sponsorship details for the 2014 trial.

assertions.text: LL-37 is assigned Grade C evidence reflecting a small positive trial followed by an adequately powered negative one.
assertions.quote: Evidence base: two randomized placebo-controlled wound trials, the smaller positive at low dose and the larger Phase IIb negative in its full cohort with only a post hoc subgroup signal.
assertions.note: The reference guide assigns Grade C based on two trials: a smaller positive low-dose trial and a larger phase IIb trial that was negative in the full cohort.

Fictional case
New dark patches, three months into 'GLOW'.
A 46-year-old patient has been injecting a research-use-only 'GLOW' blend bought online for three months. She reports smoother skin and asks about continuing. You notice new, patchy darkening on her face and forearms. This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence; there is one right first move.
Narration: A fictional case, built from this lesson's evidence. A forty-six-year-old patient has been injecting a research-use-only blend sold as GLOW for three months: GHK-Cu, BPC-157 and TB-500 in one vial. She likes her skin and asks about carrying on. You notice new, patchy darkening on her face and forearms. The blend has no controlled human trials, it is made outside good manufacturing practice, and the Hormonaly guide treats new pigmentation on these products as a red flag. Impurity and mislabelling are documented for si…

assertions.text: The GLOW blend consists of GHK-Cu, BPC-157, and TB-500 and has no controlled human trials.
assertions.quote: GLOW is a fixed injectable blend of GHK-Cu, BPC-157, and TB-500 — GHK-Cu-dominant and pitched for skin quality, collagen, and tissue repair. KLOW is the same three plus KPV, a Lys-Pro-Val tripeptide derived from α-MSH with anti-inflammatory activity through NF-κB inhibition,[7] added for an immune and gut-skin angle. Users report smoother texture, fewer fine lines, clearer skin, and sometimes improved hair with topical or injectable use — but these are anecdotal and preclinical signals: there are no controlled human trials of either blend, the products are sold "research-use-only" as reconstituted powder, and the component peptides carry the 503A constraints above.

units.text:
Follicle, pigment and melanocortins · three lessons
Lesson 5.1 The hair follicle as an endocrine mini-organ · Lesson 5.2 Afamelanotide, Melanotan II and the melanocortin receptors · Lesson 5.3 Investigational hair peptides, graded.
Module 05 · Follicle, pigment and melanocortins
A spray for the scalp, a tan in a vial.
Two requests reach aesthetic clinics well ahead of their evidence: a peptide to regrow hair and an injection to tan. In three lessons you will see how the follicle and the pigment system run on the skin's own hormones, why one melanocortin drug is approved while its gray-market cousin is approved nowhere, and how to grade the hair peptides patients bring to you.
Your turn
Shedding after the baby.
One question to close lesson 5.1.
'The new minoxidil'?
One question to close lesson 5.3.
Melanocortins: approved afamelanotide and gray-market Melanotan II
Investigational hair pep…

Mechanism
A follicle that runs its own hormones.
Human scalp hair follicles kept alive in the laboratory answer corticotropin-releasing hormone by making ACTH and α-MSH and secreting cortisol, with a feedback loop like the adrenal axis. They also run a growth hormone and IGF-1 loop of their own. Locally made dihydrotestosterone shrinks genetically susceptible scalp follicles, the process behind pattern hair loss. Growing follicles are shielded from immune attack, and alopecia areata begins when that shield fails.
Local stress axis: CRH → ACTH → cortisol, with feedback
Local androgen switch: testosterone → DHT in the scalp
Immune privilege: its collapse drives alopecia areata
Narration: Each hair follicle behaves like a small gland. When researchers keep human scalp follicles alive in culture, the follicles answer corticotropin-releasing hormone the way the pituitary and adrenal glands do…
units.sourceNote: Ito 2005 · Horesh 2023 · Bertolini 2020 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 6

assertions.text: Human scalp hair follicles maintained in culture respond to corticotropin-releasing hormone by producing ACTH and α-MSH and secreting cortisol, operating a local HPA-like feedback loop.
assertions.quote: Thus, even in the absence of endocrine, neural, or vascular systemic connections, normal human scalp hair follicles directly respond to CRH stimulation in a strikingly similar manner to what is seen in the classical HPA axis, including synthesis and secretion of cortisol and activation of prototypic neuroendocrine feedback loops.
assertions.note: Human hair follicles in culture respond to CRH by producing POMC peptides (ACTH, α-MSH), secreting cortisol, and exhibiting negative feedback.

assertions.text: Hair follicles operate an autonomous growth hormone and IGF-1 loop.
assertions.quote: The human hair follicle runs functional peripheral equivalents of the central axes: it synthesizes cortisol and operates a local HPA-like loop,[11] and ex vivo it sustains a hypothalamic–pituitary–somatotropic equivalent (GHRH, GH, IGF-1) that paces its own growth.[12]
assertions.note: Hair follicles sustain an ex vivo equivalent of the somatotropic axis including GH and IGF-1.

assertions.text: Locally produced dihydrotestosterone (via 5-alpha-reductase conversion of testosterone) shrinks genetically susceptible scalp hair follicles in pattern hair loss.
assertions.quote: Hormones set the follicle’s tempo. Thyroid hormone and prolactin tune the cycle and estrogen withdrawal at menopause thins hair, but the dominant clinical lever is androgenic: 5α-reductase converts testosterone to DHT, which paradoxically miniaturizes genetically susceptible scalp follicles (androgenetic alopecia) while driving beard and body hair.
assertions.note: 5α-reductase converts testosterone to DHT, causing follicle miniaturization in androgenetic alopecia.

assertions.text: Growing hair follicles possess immune privilege shielding them from immune attack, and the collapse of this privilege drives alopecia areata.
assertions.quote: Collapse of anagen hair bulb IP is an essential prerequisite for the development of alopecia areata (AA).
assertions.note: Anagen hair follicles maintain immune privilege whose collapse is necessary for alopecia areata pathogenesis.

units.text:
Human evidence
Two trials, 1,200 adults, one approval.
When immune privilege fails, the attack depends on cytokine signals that JAK inhibitors interrupt. Two randomized phase 3 trials tested oral baricitinib in 1,200 adults with severe alopecia areata. In the US, FDA approved baricitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades it A. In the UK, baricitinib is licensed for severe alopecia areata in adults, and NICE did not recommend it for NHS use in October 2023, on cost-effectiveness.
adults with severe alopecia areata in the two phase 3 trials of baricitinib (2022)
At 36 weeks, up to 39% of patients on baricitinib had at least 80% of their scalp hair, against 3–6% on placebo
What it means: Interrupting the immune signalling behind collapsed privilege regrows hair in severe alopecia areata. That is approval-grade evi…
units.sourceNote: King 2022 (BRAVE-AA1 and -AA2) · FDA approval letter, 13 Jun 2022 · Olumiant UK SmPC · NICE TA926 (25 Oct 2023)

assertions.text: When immune privilege fails, the attack depends on cytokine signals that JAK inhibitors interrupt.
assertions.quote: It is also an immune-privileged site — normally shielded from immune attack — and collapse of that privilege drives alopecia areata, now treatable with JAK inhibitors that interrupt the responsible cytokine signaling (oral baricitinib is approved for severe disease GRADE A).[13]
assertions.note: Supported by the discussion of immune privilege collapse and JAK inhibitor mechanism.

assertions.text: Two randomized phase 3 trials tested oral baricitinib in 1,200 adults with severe alopecia areata.
assertions.quote: The Phase III portion of BRAVE-AA1 study and the Phase III BRAVE-AA2 study included 1 200 adult patients.
assertions.note: The BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2 trials enrolled a combined 1,200 adult patients with severe alopecia areata.

assertions.text: In the US, FDA approved baricitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022.
assertions.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of the indication for the treatment of adult patients with severe alopecia areata.
assertions.note: The FDA approval letter confirms approval of baricitinib for severe alopecia areata on June 13, 2022.

assertions.text: The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades baricitinib for severe alopecia areata as A.
assertions.quote: It is also an immune-privileged site — normally shielded from immune attack — and collapse of that privilege drives alopecia areata, now treatable with JAK inhibitors that interrupt the responsible cytokine signaling (oral baricitinib is approved for severe disease GRADE A).[13]
assertions.note: The guide assigns Grade A to oral baricitinib for severe alopecia areata.

assertions.text: In the UK, baricitinib is licensed for severe alopecia areata in adults.
assertions.quote: Baricitinib is indicated for the treatment of severe alopecia areata in adult patients (see section 5.1).
assertions.note: Olumiant's UK SmPC indicates it for severe alopecia areata in adult patients.

assertions.text: NICE did not recommend baricitinib for NHS use in October 2023, on cost-effectiveness.
assertions.quote: The cost-effectiveness estimates for baricitinib are uncertain and are higher than what NICE normally considers an acceptable use of NHS resources. So, baricitinib is not recommended.
assertions.note: NICE guidance TA926 (October 2023) did not recommend baricitinib due to cost-effectiveness estimates exceeding acceptable thresholds.

assertions.text: At 36 weeks, up to 39% of patients on baricitinib had at least 80% of their scalp hair, against 3–6% on placebo in the two phase 3 trials.
assertions.quote: The estimated percentage of patients with a SALT score of 20 or less at week 36 was 38.8% with 4-mg baricitinib, 22.8% with 2-mg baricitinib, and 6.2% with placebo in BRAVE-AA1 and 35.9%, 19.4%, and 3.3%, respectively, in BRAVE-AA2.
assertions.note: In BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2, primary outcome (SALT score <= 20, representing 80% scalp coverage) was up to 38.8% vs 3.3-6.2% on placebo.

assertions.text: Both baricitinib trials were funded by the manufacturer, and the authors called for longer trials.
assertions.quote: Longer trials are required to assess the efficacy and safety of baricitinib for alopecia areata. (Funded by Eli Lilly under license from Incyte; BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT03570749 and NCT03899259.).
assertions.note: The publication notes Eli Lilly funding and calls for longer trials.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Work up the hair loss before anyone mentions a peptide.
Pattern, trigger, patches and androgens decide the treatment. Pooled randomized trials support topical minoxidil in men and women and finasteride in men. In the US, as of September 2026, topical minoxidil is FDA-approved and sold over the counter, finasteride for pattern hair loss is a prescription drug, and baricitinib is approved for adults with severe alopecia areata. In the UK, topical minoxidil is licensed and a men's foam is on general sale, finasteride for hair loss is available only on private prescription, and baricitinib is licensed for severe alopecia areata in adults. In May 2026 MHRA strengthened its warnings that finasteride is associated with depression, suicidal thoughts and sexual dysfunction that may persist after stopping.
Workup first: ferritin and TSH in everyone
Approved options exist, …

ROGAINE (FOR MEN)

The products listed here are over-the-counter (OTC) drugs and do not receive therapeutic equivalence ratings. They may not be interchangeable.

units.text:
A 32-year-old woman asks for a compounded peptide scalp spray. Diffuse shedding began three months after she gave birth; there are no patches and no signs of androgen excess. What comes first?
Explanation: Diagnose the pattern first; the product question comes after.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Start the spray now, since peptides act on the follicle directly.
Explanation: That skips the diagnosis. The pattern points to telogen effluvium, and peptide sprays such as PTD-DBM or zinc thymulin have no human trial behind them.
Correct answer: Treat it as likely telogen effluvium: reassure, check ferritin and TSH, and reassess the pattern before any product.
Explanation: Correct. Diffuse shedding after a trigger is the guide's telogen-effluvium branch, and ferritin and TSH are checked in everyone.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Refer her for a JAK inhibitor.
Exp…

assertions.text: Sudden physiologic stressors can trigger telogen effluvium.
assertions.quote: This is why 5α-reductase inhibitors (finasteride) and androgen-independent minoxidil are the mainstays of pattern hair loss, and why a sudden physiologic stressor or thyroid shift can tip follicles into telogen effluvium.
assertions.note: The guide notes that a sudden physiologic stressor can trigger telogen effluvium.

units.text:
Lesson 5.2 · Concept
Five receptors, one family of hormones.
Skin makes proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and cuts it into ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. Those peptides act on five melanocortin receptors. MC1R drives pigment in skin and hair, MC2R answers ACTH in the adrenal gland, MC3R and MC4R act in the brain on appetite, and MC5R governs sebum. Which receptors a drug reaches decides what else it does.
MC1R: pigment of skin and hair
MC2R: adrenal · MC5R: sebum
MC3R and MC4R: appetite, in the brain
Narration: Pigment starts with hormones the skin makes for itself. Skin cells produce a precursor called POMC and cut it into ACTH, alpha-MSH and beta-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. There are five melanocortin receptors. MC1R sets the pigment of skin and hair. MC2R is the adrenal receptor for ACTH. MC3R and …
units.sourceNote: Slominski & Wortsman 2000 · Laiho & Murray 2022 · Böhm 2025

assertions.text: Skin produces proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and cleaves it into ACTH, α-MSH, and β-endorphin, with the same cells expressing receptors for these peptides.
assertions.quote: In fact, all of the elements controlling the activity of the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal axis are expressed in the skin including CRH, urocortin, and POMC, with its products ACTH, alpha-MSH, and beta-endorphin. Demonstration of the corresponding receptors in the same cells suggests para- or autocrine mechanisms of action.
assertions.note: Supported by the abstract of Slominski & Wortsman 2000.

assertions.text: Melanocortin peptides act on five melanocortin receptors.
assertions.quote: The 5 known melanocortin receptors (MCs) have established physiological roles.
assertions.note: Supported by Laiho & Murray 2022.

assertions.text: MC1R regulates skin and hair pigmentation.
assertions.quote: MC 1 mediates pigmentation of both skin and hair, MC 2 is required for adrenal steroidogenesis and therefore the stress response, MC 3 and MC 4 modulate the central control of food intake and satiety, and MC 5 regulates sebogenesis.
assertions.note: Supported by Laiho & Murray 2022.

assertions.text: MC2R mediates the response to ACTH in the adrenal gland.
assertions.quote: MC2R, expressed in the adrenal cortex, is involved in steroidogenesis. 2 , 3 , 4 Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) binds to MC2R located on the surface of adrenal zona fasciculata cells, thereby producing cortisol.
assertions.note: Supported by Böhm et al. 2025.

assertions.text: MC3R and MC4R act in the brain to regulate appetite and food intake.
assertions.quote: MC 1 mediates pigmentation of both skin and hair, MC 2 is required for adrenal steroidogenesis and therefore the stress response, MC 3 and MC 4 modulate the central control of food intake and satiety, and MC 5 regulates sebogenesis.
assertions.note: Supported by Laiho & Murray 2022.

assertions.text: Central melanocortin receptors also influence sexual responses.
assertions.quote: MC3R has been linked to timing of sexual maturation and linear growth. 13 Some studies have reported the association between MC4R and sexual function.
assertions.note: Supported by Böhm et al. 2025.

assertions.text: MC5R regulates sebum production.
assertions.quote: MC 1 mediates pigmentation of both skin and hair, MC 2 is required for adrenal steroidogenesis and therefore the stress response, MC 3 and MC 4 modulate the central control of food intake and satiety, and MC 5 regulates sebogenesis.
assertions.note: Supported by Laiho & Murray 2022.

assertions.text: Melanocortin receptors are expressed more widely across tissues than traditional textbook models describe.
assertions.quote: The complexity of the MCs and their multifaceted features belies textbook views of a simpler range of functions, many of which are underpinned by overt human and mouse phenotypes resulting from mutations: these are described briefly below to put in context the more complex aspects that we will describe later.
assertions.note: Supported by Laiho & Murray 2022.

units.text:
Four registers
One receptor family, two very different molecules.
Afamelanotide and Melanotan II are both synthetic relatives of α-MSH. Compare them register by register and the resemblance ends at the receptor.
Mechanism
Afamelanotide: MC1R agonist · Melanotan II: non-selective
Melanotan II also acts on MC3R, MC4R and MC5R and reaches the brain
Human evidence
Afamelanotide: A, for EPP only · Melanotan II: D
Two phase 3 trials in erythropoietic protoporphyria, against a three-volunteer pilot and a ten-man erectile-dysfunction study from the 1990s. The Peptide Pocket Guide rates Melanotan II C and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide D; with no trial of tanning, this course uses D.
Regulatory status
Afamelanotide: EU 2014, US 2019, UK licensed · Melanotan II: none
Afamelanotide is approved only for EPP, as the manufacturer's implant. Melanotan II is approved for no indication …
units.sourceNote: Langendonk 2015 · EMA Scenesse EPAR · FDA Scenesse label (Aug 2024) · Dorr 1996 · Wessells 1998 · Böhm 2025 · NICE HST27 (26 Jul 2023)

assertions.text: Afamelanotide and Melanotan II are both synthetic relatives of α-MSH.
assertions.quote: Afamelanotide, the first and most studied synthetic α‐MSH analogue, is a nonselective melanocortin tridecapeptide that can bind and activate MC1R.
assertions.note: Supported by the review of melanocortin-1 receptor activation.

assertions.text: Afamelanotide is an MC1R agonist, whereas Melanotan II is non-selective, acts on MC3R, MC4R, and MC5R, and reaches the brain.
assertions.quote: Because melanotan II can cross the blood–brain barrier and is nonselective, it also activates the other MCRs, resulting in adverse events including fatigue, loss of appetite and penile erection.
assertions.note: Supported by the review describing Melanotan II receptor binding and central penetration.

assertions.text: Afamelanotide has two phase 3 trials in erythropoietic protoporphyria, whereas Melanotan II human exposure is limited to a 3-volunteer pilot and a 10-man erectile dysfunction study from the 1990s.
assertions.quote: Human exposure is limited to two small early studies: a single-blind placebo-controlled pilot Phase I in three male volunteers, dose-limiting somnolence at 0.03 mg/kg (Dorr 1996), and a 10-man erectile-dysfunction crossover study (Wessells 1998).
assertions.note: Supported by the trials and the Peptide Pocket Guide evidence summary.

assertions.text: The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates Melanotan II evidence as GRADE D.
assertions.quote: This biology has two clinical faces. The legitimate one is afamelanotide, an α-MSH analog approved to reduce phototoxicity in erythropoietic protoporphyria; the misused one is unregulated “tanning peptides” (melanotan II), sold online with no quality control GRADE D.
assertions.note: Supported by the guide's peptide evidence table and text.

assertions.text: Afamelanotide was approved in the EU in 2014 and in the US in 2019, and is approved only for EPP as the manufacturer's implant.
assertions.quote: The European Commission granted a marketing authorisation valid throughout the European Union for Scenesse on 22 December 2014.
assertions.note: Supported by the US FDA label and EMA EPAR.

assertions.text: Melanotan II is not approved for any therapeutic indication.
assertions.quote: Melanotan II is a synthetic cyclic α‐MSH analogue that is a nonselective MCR agonist and is not approved for use in any therapeutic indication.
assertions.note: Supported by the MC1R review.

assertions.text: In the UK, afamelanotide is licensed under exceptional circumstances and prescribed only in specialist porphyria centres, and NICE did not recommend it for NHS use in July 2023.
assertions.quote: The marketing authorisation stipulates that afamelanotide should only be prescribed by specialist clinicians in recognised porphyria centres, and that it should only be given by a clinician trained and accredited by the marketing authorisation holder to insert the implants.
assertions.note: Supported by NICE guidance HST27.

assertions.text: A phase 3 trial of afamelanotide in vitiligo began in 2023 and has posted no results.
assertions.quote:
Study type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: PHASE3; allocation: RANDOMIZED; masking: NONE; enrollment: 200 (ESTIMATED)
Primary outcomes: Percentage of patients achieving T-VASI 50 on the body
assertions.note: Supported by the ClinicalTrials.gov record for NCT06109649.

assertions.text: Whether Melanotan II causes melanoma is unproven.
assertions.quote: Dermatologically it is the opposite of benign: by driving melanogenesis indiscriminately it darkens and enlarges existing moles, provokes eruptive and atypical (dysplastic) nevi and melanonychia, and has been linked in case reports to melanoma arising in pre-existing lesions — causation is unproven, but the mechanism (proliferation of melanocytes, including neoplastic clones) makes it a real concern
assertions.note: Supported by the discussion of case reports and unproven causation in the guide.

units.text:
The evidence
Sixty-nine hours against forty-one.
Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is a rare disorder in which sunlight causes acute, severe pain. In the US phase 3 trial, adults on afamelanotide spent a median 69.4 hours in direct sunlight without pain over six months, against 40.8 hours on placebo. The European trial also showed more pain-free time and fewer phototoxic reactions. Both trials were funded by the manufacturer.
69 vs 41 h
median pain-free hours in direct sunlight over six months, afamelanotide vs placebo (US phase 3 trial, 94 adults with EPP)
Langendonk et al., NEJM 2015 · European trial, 74 adults: 6.0 vs 0.8 hours over nine months
What it means: Afamelanotide lets people with EPP spend more time in sunlight without pain. That is approval-grade evidence (A) for one rare disease.
What it does not mean: It says nothing about cosmetic tanning, about Melanotan II, or about …
units.sourceNote: Langendonk 2015 (NEJM) · FDA Scenesse label, Aug 2024 · EMA EPAR

assertions.text: Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is a rare disorder in which sunlight causes acute, severe pain.
assertions.quote: Erythropoietic protoporphyria is a severe photodermatosis that is associated with acute phototoxicity. Patients with this condition have excruciating pain and a markedly reduced quality of life.
assertions.note: The NEJM paper describes EPP as a rare disorder causing acute phototoxicity and severe painful photosensitivity.

assertions.text: In the US phase 3 trial, adults on afamelanotide spent a median 69.4 hours in direct sunlight without pain over six months, compared to 40.8 hours on placebo.
assertions.quote: In the U.S. study, the duration of pain-free time after 6 months was longer in the afamelanotide group (median, 69.4 hours, vs. 40.8 hours in the placebo group; P = 0.04).
assertions.note: The phase 3 results reported in NEJM confirm these exact median pain-free sunlight exposure durations over 6 months.

assertions.text: The European trial also showed more pain-free time and fewer phototoxic reactions with afamelanotide.
assertions.quote: In the European Union study, the duration of pain-free time after 9 months was also longer in the afamelanotide group than in the placebo group (median, 6.0 hours vs. 0.8 hours; P = 0.005), and the number of phototoxic reactions was lower in the the afamelanotide group (77 vs. 146, P = 0.04).
assertions.note: The European trial showed significantly longer pain-free time and significantly fewer phototoxic reactions in the afamelanotide group.

assertions.text: Both phase 3 trials of afamelanotide in EPP were funded by the manufacturer.
assertions.quote: The study was designed and sponsored by Clinuvel Pharmaceuticals, with input from investigators in the European Union and the United States.
assertions.note: The study publication notes funding and sponsorship by the drug's manufacturer, Clinuvel Pharmaceuticals.

assertions.text: The US trial included 94 adults and the European trial included 74 adults (where median pain-free hours over 9 months were 6.0 vs 0.8 hours).
assertions.quote: Patients in the European Union (74 patients) and the United States (94 patients) were randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, to receive a subcutaneous implant containing either afamelanotide or placebo every 60 days (a total of five implants in the European Union study and three in the U.S study).
assertions.note: The participant counts and European trial primary endpoint median values match the trial publication.

assertions.text: The US FDA label recommends a full-body skin examination twice a year for patients on afamelanotide.
assertions.quote: A full body skin examination (twice yearly) is recommended to monitor pre-existing and new skin pigmentary lesions.
assertions.note: The FDA prescribing information explicitly recommends a twice-yearly full-body skin examination.

units.text:
Safety signals
What the case reports show.
The harms of Melanotan II come from case reports and reviews, so they show what can happen without telling you how often. Reported skin effects include darkening and growth of existing moles, crops of new and sometimes atypical naevi, and dark bands in the nails. At least five melanomas have been reported during or after use, each in someone with other risk factors, so causation is unproven. Systemic reports include ischaemic priapism needing surgery and a stimulant-like toxic reaction with rhabdomyolysis, and FDA lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious events.
Skin: changing moles, eruptive naevi, melanonychia
Melanoma: reported, causation unproven
Systemic: priapism, rhabdomyolysis, encephalopathy
Narration: Now the harms, and the kind of evidence behind them. Everything here comes from case reports and revie…
units.sourceNote: Habbema 2017 · Cardones 2009 · Paurobally 2013 · Hjuler 2014 · Mallory 2021 · Nelson 2012 · FDA compounding safety page

assertions.text: Reported skin effects of Melanotan II include darkening and growth of existing moles and crops of new and sometimes atypical naevi.
assertions.quote: He developed crops of new pigmented nevi, many of which had atypical clinical and histopathologic features. The preexisting nevi became darker and acquired growth features.
assertions.note: A case report confirms new eruptive atypical naevi and darkening/growth of preexisting moles following use of synthetic alpha-MSH.

assertions.text: Reported skin effects of Melanotan II include dark bands in the nails (melanonychia).
assertions.quote: Dermatologically it is the opposite of benign: by driving melanogenesis indiscriminately it darkens and enlarges existing moles, provokes eruptive and atypical (dysplastic) nevi and melanonychia, and has been linked in case reports to melanoma arising in pre-existing lesions
assertions.note: The clinical pocket guide notes that Melanotan II provokes melanonychia among its cutaneous effects.

assertions.text: At least five melanomas have been reported during or after Melanotan II use, each in an individual with other risk factors, leaving causation unproven.
assertions.quote: There have been at least five reports of melanomas during or after melanotan II use. All individuals had other risk factors such as fair skin, excess sun exposure/tanning bed use and/or family history of melanoma.
assertions.note: A review notes at least five reported melanoma cases in users who all had other risk factors.

assertions.text: Systemic reports include ischaemic priapism requiring surgical intervention.
assertions.quote: This case report highlights a rare presentation of acute ischemic priapism after melanotan II use, managed with surgical decompression.
assertions.note: A case report describes acute ischaemic priapism after Melanotan II injection requiring operative decompression.

assertions.text: Systemic reports include a stimulant-like toxic reaction with rhabdomyolysis.
assertions.quote: We report a novel case of systemic toxicity with sympathomimetic excess and rhabdomyolysis after use of Melanotan II.
assertions.note: A published case report documents systemic toxicity with sympathomimetic excess and rhabdomyolysis after Melanotan II injection.

assertions.text: The FDA lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious adverse events associated with Melanotan II.
assertions.quote: Published case reports discuss serious adverse events including melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, sympathomimetic toxidrome and priapism.
assertions.note: The FDA compounding Category 2 safety document explicitly lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome under serious adverse events from Melanotan II case reports.

units.text:
Fictional case
New moles after a summer of tanning shots.
A 27-year-old attends for a skin-quality consultation and mentions injecting a 'tanning peptide' bought online for three months. She has noticed darker moles, several new small ones and a dark stripe along one fingernail. Her mother had melanoma. This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence, and one move clearly comes before the others.
Almost certainly Melanotan II: approved nowhere, unknown strength and purity
New and changing naevi and nail pigmentation are the documented harms
Family history of melanoma: the guide's absolute contraindication
Narration: Her booking says skin quality. This patient is fictional, built from the lesson's evidence. She is twenty-seven, and she mentions that she has been injecting a tanning peptide bought online for three months. She has noticed darker moles, several new small ones, and …

assertions.text: Melanotan II is not approved in any indication and presents risks of unknown strength and purity when purchased unregulated online.
assertions.quote: Melanotan II is a synthetic cyclic α‐MSH analogue that is a nonselective MCR agonist and is not approved for use in any therapeutic indication.
assertions.note: Melanotan II is not approved for any indication and carries risks of varied concentrations and unknown impurities.

assertions.text: Documented harms of Melanotan II include darkening and enlargement of existing moles, eruptive nevi, and nail pigmentation (melanonychia).
assertions.quote: Dermatologically it is the opposite of benign: by driving melanogenesis indiscriminately it darkens and enlarges existing moles, provokes eruptive and atypical (dysplastic) nevi and melanonychia, and has been linked in case reports to melanoma arising in pre-existing lesions — causation is unproven, but the mechanism (proliferation of melanocytes, including neoplastic clones) makes it a real concern, and a personal or family history of melanoma is an absolute contraindication.

assertions.text: In a patient evaluated with dermoscopy during Melanotan II use, observed changes made it difficult to distinguish nevi from melanoma.

units.text:
What do you do first?
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Reassure her: darker moles are expected with a tan. Review them at her next routine visit.
Explanation: New and changing naevi are the documented harm here, dermoscopic changes on Melanotan II can mimic melanoma, and her family history raises the stakes.
Correct answer: Advise stopping now, record the product and seller, and have the whole skin and nails examined promptly, with dermoscopy and baseline photographs, by a dermatologist or skin-cancer clinician.

units.text:
Regulatory status
Three regulators, one answer.
Each statement below is dated, because regulatory status changes. None of the three regulators has approved Melanotan II, and each has put its concerns on the record. EU status is not covered in this course.
United States · FDA (page current as of 22 April 2026)
Unapproved; nomination withdrawn
FDA's compounding safety page lists Melanotan II among substances withdrawn from Category 2, citing impurity and immunogenicity risks and published reports of melanoma, encephalopathy, sympathomimetic toxicity and priapism
United Kingdom · MHRA (17 April 2024)
Unauthorised medicine
Injectable products are classed as medicines; MHRA advises anyone using them to stop immediately and has removed melanotan products from sale for over ten years
Australia · TGA (17 August 2026)
Prescription-only; no approved product
Not approved as a tanning agent and noth…

assertions.text: The FDA's compounding safety page lists Melanotan II among substances nominated but withdrawn from Category 2, citing risks of peptide-related impurities and immunogenicity as well as published case reports of melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, sympathomimetic toxidrome, and priapism.

Published case reports discuss serious adverse events including melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, sympathomimetic toxidrome and priapism.

assertions.text: In the UK, the MHRA classifies injectable Melanotan II products as medicines, advises anyone using Melanotan II injections or nasal sprays to stop immediately, and has taken action to remove melanotan products from the market for over 10 years.

units.text:
Your turn
'The approved one is the same thing.'
One question to close lesson 5.2.
units.sourceNote: Lesson 5.2

units.text:
A patient says, 'Afamelanotide is approved, so Melanotan II is basically the same drug.' What is the accurate reply?
Explanation: Name the molecule, then its indication: approval does not transfer between them.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Yes. They act on the same receptor, so the approval covers both.
Explanation: Sharing MC1R does not make them the same molecule, and an approval attaches to one product and one indication.
Correct answer: They are different molecules. Afamelanotide is approved only for erythropoietic protoporphyria; Melanotan II acts on several receptors, is approved nowhere, and is linked in case reports to changing moles and priapism.
Explanation: Correct. Same family, different selectivity, different evidence and different legal standing.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Melanotan II is safe if it comes from a reputable seller.
Explanat…

assertions.note: SCENESSE (afamelanotide) is FDA- and EMA-approved specifically for erythropoietic protoporphyria.

assertions.text: Tested online Melanotan II products contained less than the labelled amount and contained unknown impurities.

units.text:
Lesson 5.3 · Concept
A Wnt switch and a zinc question.
PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating peptide to a short decoy sequence that stops the protein CXXC5 from binding Dishevelled. Freed from that brake, Wnt/β-catenin signalling rises, and in mice hair regrew faster. Its developers also found CXXC5 raised in human balding scalp. Zinc thymulin is a thymic peptide that is active only when bound to zinc. How it might act on hair has never been defined, and whether any effect would come from the peptide or the zinc is unknown.
PTD-DBM: releases a Wnt brake (mouse data)
Zinc thymulin: a zinc-dependent thymic peptide
Both: mechanism first, human data absent
Narration: Two peptides are sold for hair, and both arrive with better stories than data. PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating fragment borrowed from an HIV protein to a short decoy sequence. Inside follicle cells, the decoy keeps a protein called …
units.sourceNote: Lee 2017 (J Invest Dermatol) · Dardenne 1982 · Peptide Pocket Guide

assertions.text: PTD-DBM is a peptide therapy that competes with CXXC5 to prevent it from binding Dishevelled (Dvl).
assertions.quote: For example, PTD-DBM is a peptide therapy that competes with CXXC5 for binding with Dvl [ 21 ].
assertions.note: Mehta 2025 explains that PTD-DBM competes with CXXC5 for Dishevelled binding.

assertions.text: Disrupting the CXXC5-Dishevelled interaction activates the Wnt/β-catenin pathway and accelerates hair regrowth and wound-induced hair follicle neogenesis in mice.
assertions.quote: Disrupting the CXXC5-Dishevelled interaction with a competitor peptide activated the Wnt/β-catenin pathway and accelerated hair regrowth and wound-induced hair follicle neogenesis.
assertions.note: Lee 2017 reports that competitor peptide disruption of CXXC5-Dishevelled activated Wnt/β-catenin and accelerated hair regrowth and follicle neogenesis.

assertions.text: CXXC5 expression is upregulated in miniaturized hair follicles in human balding scalps.
assertions.quote: CXXC5 was upregulated in miniaturized hair follicles and arrector pili muscles in human balding scalps.
assertions.note: Lee 2017 found CXXC5 upregulated in miniaturized follicles in human balding scalp.

assertions.text: Thymulin is biologically active only when bound to zinc.
assertions.quote: These data indicate the existence of two forms of FTS. The first one lacks Zn and is biologically inactive; the second one contains Zn and is biologically active, for which we propose the name of "thymulin" (FTS-Zn).
assertions.note: Dardenne 1982 demonstrated that the zinc-lacking form is inactive, while the zinc-bound form (thymulin) is biologically active.

assertions.text: The mechanism of zinc thymulin in hair growth is undefined, and whether any effect comes from the peptide or from zinc is unknown.
assertions.quote: The role of the zinc cofactor itself complicates the question of whether 'zinc thymulin' acts as a peptide or as a vehicle for topical zinc.
assertions.note: The clinical reference notes that it remains unclear whether zinc thymulin acts as a peptide or simply as a vehicle for zinc delivery.

units.text:
The evidence
Zero trials in people.
As of September 2026, PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov list no human trial of PTD-DBM, published or registered. Its evidence is one 2017 study in mice and human scalp tissue from the developer's group, whose senior author is affiliated with a biotech company. A 2025 review's summary speaks of 'clinical efficacy', yet the review's own text describes PTD-DBM results in mouse models only.
human trials of PTD-DBM, published or registered (September 2026)
Lee et al., J Invest Dermatol 2017: mice, plus CXXC5 measured in human scalp tissue
What it means: Whether PTD-DBM regrows human hair is unknown. The Peptide Pocket Guide and this course grade it D.
What it does not mean: It does not show that PTD-DBM fails or harms. One open safety question sits alongside: the 2025 review flags that off-target Wnt activation is associated with colorectal and liver cancers, a…
units.sourceNote: PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov, searched 24 Sep 2026 · Lee 2017 · Mehta 2025

assertions.text: The 2017 study by Lee et al. evaluated PTD-DBM / CXXC5 in mice and human scalp tissue.
assertions.quote: CXXC5 was upregulated in miniaturized hair follicles and arrector pili muscles in human balding scalps. The inhibitory effects of CXXC5 on alkaline phosphatase activity and cell proliferation were demonstrated using human hair follicle dermal papilla cells. Moreover, CXXC5 -/- mice displayed accelerated hair regrowth, and treatment with valproic acid, a glycogen synthase kinase 3β inhibitor that activates the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, further induced hair regrowth in the CXXC5 -/- mice.
assertions.note: Lee et al. demonstrated CXXC5 upregulation in human balding scalps and tested the competing peptide / CXXC5-knockout in mice.

assertions.text: The senior author of the 2017 PTD-DBM study is affiliated with a biotech company.
assertions.note: The provided abstract for Lee 2017 does not include author affiliations.

recheck.note: None of the provided sources mention that the senior author of the 2017 PTD-DBM study is affiliated with a biotech company.

assertions.text: A 2025 review's abstract/summary mentions 'clinical efficacy' of PTD-DBM, but its body text describes PTD-DBM hair regrowth results in mouse models.
assertions.quote: Investigations demonstrate clinical efficacy of small molecule inhibitors and peptides, such as PTD-DBM, which activates the Wnt/β-catenin pathway by interfering with CXXC5, a negative regulator that inhibits pathway activation.
assertions.note: The Mehta 2025 abstract references clinical efficacy for PTD-DBM, while Section 3.3 describes topically enhanced hair regrowth in mouse models of androgenetic alopecia.

assertions.text: The Peptide Pocket Guide assigns PTD-DBM an evidence rating of GRADE D.
assertions.quote:
GRADE D                    CELL-PENETRATING WNT-PATHWAY ACTIVATOR

PTD-DBM
Topical hair-growth research compound
assertions.note: The Peptide Pocket Guide assigns GRADE D to PTD-DBM.

assertions.text: The 2025 review notes that off-target or atypical Wnt/β-catenin activation is associated with colorectal and hepatocellular/liver carcinomas.
assertions.quote: Due to the nature of this pathway to promote growth, one of the most prominent and noticeable concerns of this approach is that of off-target effects, as atypical and unnecessary activation of this pathway has been correlated with various cancers such as colorectal and hepatocellular carcinomas [ 50 ].
assertions.note: Mehta 2025 notes that atypical activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway correlates with colorectal and hepatocellular carcinomas.

assertions.text: Growth hormone and IGF-1 genuinely shape skin.
assertions.quote: The literature highlights the importance of the GH and IGF systems in normal skin homeostasis, including dermal/epidermal cross-talk. GH activity, sometimes mediated via IGF-I, is primarily evident in the dermis, particularly affecting collagen synthesis.
assertions.note: The cited review details the role of growth hormone and IGF-1 systems in cutaneous homeostasis and collagen synthesis.

assertions.text: One peptide on the growth-hormone axis has approval-grade trials.
assertions.quote: With the exception of tesamorelin, which has been evaluated in randomized controlled trials within an approved clinical indication, the available human evidence for GH–IGF-1-axis performance-enhancing peptides consists predominantly of phase I pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies in healthy adults, small mechanistic endocrine studies, or paediatric GH-deficiency cohorts.
assertions.note: Tesamorelin is the only GH-axis peptide evaluated in regulatory-grade randomized controlled trials for an approved indication.

units.text:
Lesson 6.1 · Mechanism
Two hormones, two layers of skin.
Growth hormone acts mostly in the dermis. Its receptor is expressed more by fibroblasts than by keratinocytes, and it increases fibroblast numbers and supports collagen synthesis. IGF-1, made locally by fibroblasts and melanocytes, reaches keratinocytes through the IGF-1 receptor and makes them divide. Human hair follicles even run their own small growth-hormone loop in the laboratory. With age, GH secretion and IGF-1 fall steadily; this is the somatopause.
GH: dermal fibroblasts and collagen
IGF-1: keratinocyte proliferation, supplied locally
Somatopause: GH and IGF-1 fall with age
Narration: Two layers of skin listen to two different parts of the same axis. Growth hormone speaks mainly to the dermis. Its receptor is expressed more on fibroblasts than on keratinocytes, and in culture growth hormone increases fibroblast numbers and…
units.sourceNote: Tavakkol 1992 · Edmondson 2003 · Horesh 2023 · Veldhuis 2008 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 2 and 6

assertions.text: The growth hormone receptor is expressed at higher levels in dermal fibroblasts than in keratinocytes.
assertions.quote: Northern analysis, using the cloned GH-R as probe, revealed relatively higher levels of GH-R transcripts in cultured human dermal fibroblasts compared to cultured keratinocytes or keratome biopsies.
assertions.note: Northern analysis demonstrated higher levels of GH receptor transcripts in cultured dermal fibroblasts than in keratinocytes.

assertions.text: Growth hormone increases fibroblast cell numbers and supports dermal collagen synthesis.
assertions.quote: GH activity, sometimes mediated via IGF-I, is primarily evident in the dermis, particularly affecting collagen synthesis.
assertions.note: Edmondson et al. state that GH activity is primarily evident in the dermis, particularly affecting collagen synthesis.

assertions.text: IGF-1 is produced locally by dermal fibroblasts and melanocytes, while keratinocytes express the IGF-1 receptor.
assertions.quote: mRNA transcripts for the major mediator of GH actions, insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), were detected by PCR in fibroblasts, melanocytes, and keratome biopsies, but not in keratinocytes. In contrast, IGF-1 receptor mRNA were abundant in cultured keratinocytes and skin biopsies, as determined by Northern analysis.
assertions.note: Tavakkol et al. detected IGF-1 transcripts in fibroblasts and melanocytes but not keratinocytes, whereas IGF-1 receptor mRNA was abundant in keratinocytes.

assertions.text: In cell culture, IGF-1 stimulates keratinocyte proliferation, whereas growth hormone alone does not.
assertions.quote: IGF-1 but not GH (5-50 ng/ml) promoted clonal proliferation of cultured keratinocytes.
assertions.note: Tavakkol et al. reported that IGF-1, but not GH, promoted clonal proliferation of cultured keratinocytes.

assertions.text: Human hair follicles maintain an autonomous somatotropic loop ex vivo.
assertions.quote: The human hair follicle runs functional peripheral equivalents of the central axes: it synthesizes cortisol and operates a local HPA-like loop,[11] and ex vivo it sustains a hypothalamic–pituitary–somatotropic equivalent (GHRH, GH, IGF-1) that paces its own growth.[12]
assertions.note: The guide notes that hair follicles sustain an ex vivo hypothalamic-pituitary-somatotropic equivalent loop.

assertions.text: Growth hormone secretion declines with age, a change referred to as the somatopause.
assertions.quote: Each axis has its own clock: somatopause and adrenopause are steep and early; andropause is gradual; menopause is abrupt.
assertions.note: Chapter 2 notes the age-related somatopause decline in the growth-hormone axis.

units.text:
Human evidence
A much-cited skin result, read again.
In 1990 a much-cited New England Journal of Medicine study gave growth hormone for six months to 12 healthy men over 60, with nine untreated men for comparison and no placebo. Lean mass rose and fat fell. Skin thickness rose 7.1%, with P = 0.07, short of statistical significance. A small 1996 randomized trial in 28 older men found 15% more collagen laid down in implanted wound tubes on GH, a laboratory surrogate for repair.
rise in skin thickness in 12 older men given growth hormone for six months (1990)
P = 0.07 · nine untreated men as comparison · no placebo
What it means: A skin result still quoted for growth hormone comes from 12 treated men, without a placebo, and it missed statistical significance. Graded on its design, it is D.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Deficiency is a diagnosis. Decline is ageing.
In healthy older adults, randomized trials of growth hormone show small shifts in body composition, about 2 kg less fat and 2 kg more lean mass, with more oedema, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and a trend towards diabetes. Strength and endurance change little. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades its advice against treatment A; graded on the trials themselves the evidence is B, and the conclusion is the same. In the US, as of September 2026, knowingly distributing growth hormone for anti-ageing is a federal offence. In the UK, somatropin is a prescription-only medicine licensed for growth hormone deficiency and specific growth disorders, and a Class C controlled drug.
Healthy ageing: small body-composition change, more side-effects
Grade B on the trials (guide: A), same conclusion

units.text:
Lesson 6.2 · Concept
One axis, four ways in.
Somatropin is growth hormone itself. GHRH analogues (sermorelin, tesamorelin, CJC-1295) stimulate the pituitary's GHRH receptor. Ghrelin-receptor agonists (ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and the oral ibutamoren, MK-677) stimulate GH release through a second pituitary receptor. IGF-1 analogues such as IGF-1 LR3 bypass the pituitary altogether. They are sold as one family, and the next moments take them apart.
Replace: somatropin
Stimulate: GHRH analogues and ghrelin-receptor agonists
Bypass: IGF-1 analogues
Narration: Four routes lead into the same axis, and patients rarely know which one they are on. Somatropin is growth hormone itself, made by recombinant technology. GHRH analogues, sermorelin, tesamorelin and CJC-1295, press on the pituitary's releasing-hormone receptor, so the gland releases its own growth hormone in pulses. Ghrelin-receptor ag…

assertions.text: Somatropin is human growth hormone produced by recombinant technology.
assertions.quote: Somatropin is a human growth hormone produced by recombinant DNA technology in Escherichia coli. The protein is comprised of 191 amino acid residues and has a molecular weight of 22,124 daltons.
assertions.note: The prescribing information confirms somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone.

assertions.text: GHRH analogues (sermorelin, tesamorelin, and CJC-1295) stimulate the pituitary GHRH receptor to promote endogenous pulsatile growth hormone release.
assertions.quote: Growth hormone–releasing hormone (GHRH) analogues are synthetic peptides designed to stimulate endogenous GH secretion by activating the pituitary GHRH receptor, thereby increasing GH pulsatility and secondarily IGF-1. Because they act upstream of GH release, their effects remain largely shaped by physiological regulatory loops
assertions.note: Dominikowski 2026 confirms that GHRH analogues like sermorelin, tesamorelin, and CJC-1295 stimulate endogenous GH pulsatility via the pituitary GHRH receptor.

assertions.text: Ghrelin-receptor agonists (including ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6, and oral MK-677/ibutamoren) stimulate GH release via a second pituitary receptor (GHSR-1a).
assertions.quote: Growth hormone–releasing peptides (GHRPs) are short synthetic peptides that stimulate endogenous GH secretion by activating the ghrelin receptor - the growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a (GHSR-1a), at the level of the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary.
assertions.note: Dominikowski 2026 describes how GHRPs act as agonists at the pituitary ghrelin receptor (GHSR-1a) to induce GH secretion.

assertions.text: IGF-1 analogues like IGF-1 LR3 bypass the pituitary and act directly on the IGF-1 receptor.
assertions.quote: Binds IGF-1R (a receptor tyrosine kinase), driving PI3K/AKT/mTOR and MAPK/ERK signaling — muscle protein synthesis, satellite-cell activation, glucose uptake, nitrogen retention, proliferation, and fat oxidation — independently of growth hormone.
assertions.note: The Peptide Pocket Guide confirms IGF-1 LR3 acts directly on the IGF-1 receptor independently of growth hormone.

Zero skin trials.

The nearest is a 1997 study of a GHRH(1-29) analogue related to sermorelin, in 19 older adults. Skin thickness measured by caliper rose after 16 weeks, compared with a placebo lead-in rather than a parallel control group.
