units.text:
Lesson 6.3 · Recognition
What too much growth hormone looks like.
Sustained GH excess changes skin in ways you can see. In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema make the face, hands and feet puffy and thick; the skin turns oily with large pores; sweating increases; skin tags and acanthosis nigricans appear. Drugs on this axis bring their own signs: fluid retention with swelling, joint pain, tingling and carpal tunnel symptoms. The Endocrine Society recommends measuring IGF-1 when typical acral and facial features are present.
Soft tissue: puffy, thickened face, hands and feet
Skin: oily, sweaty, skin tags, acanthosis nigricans
On treatment: swelling, joint pain, tingling
Narration: Excess growth hormone leaves visible marks on skin and soft tissue, and noticing them early matters. In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema thicken the face, hands and feet, so featur…
units.sourceNote: Ben-Shlomo & Melmed 2006 · Endocrine Society guideline 2014 · Acromegaly consensus 2024 · somatropin label

assertions.text: In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema cause facial, hand, and foot puffiness and thickening, oily skin with large pores, increased sweating, skin tags, and acanthosis nigricans.
assertions.quote: Skin puffiness due to dermal glycosaminoglycan accumulation and edema are most prominent in the face, hands and feet. Oily skin with large pores, hypertrichosis, and excessive sweating are common features. Pigmented skin tags, acanthosis nigricans, and psoriasis are also encountered.
assertions.note: Supported by the review on cutaneous changes in acromegaly.

assertions.text: Growth hormone axis drugs cause fluid retention leading to swelling, joint pain, tingling, and carpal tunnel symptoms.
assertions.quote: Fluid retention during somatropin replacement therapy in adults may occur. Clinical manifestations of fluid retention (e.g., edema, arthralgia, myalgia, nerve compression syndromes including carpal tunnel syndrome/paresthesia) are usually transient and dose dependent.
assertions.note: Supported by the somatropin prescribing information.

assertions.quote: Characteristic changes in the face and head, including widening and malocclusion of the jaw and macroglossia, as well as enlarged hands, occur insidiously but are often apparent at initial assessment [ 2 , 17 ] (HQ).
assertions.note: Supported by the consensus statement on clinical examination in acromegaly.

assertions.quote: Monitor patients on somatropin therapy carefully for increased growth, or potential malignant changes, of preexisting nevi.
assertions.note: Supported by the warnings section of the somatropin label.

units.text:
Four registers
Does raising IGF-1 cause cancer?
The honest answer has four parts, and each has its own source. Keep them apart, or a mechanism will be heard as a measured risk.
Mechanism
Plausible
IGF-1 receptor signalling drives cell proliferation and survival, which gives any IGF-1-raising product a theoretical concern
Human observation
Modest associations
In large studies, higher natural IGF-1 goes with slightly higher risks of prostate, breast, colorectal and thyroid cancer; reverse causation is not excluded. In one Ecuadorian cohort, people with GH-receptor deficiency had almost no cancer.
Acromegaly
Slightly raised, inconsistently
Pooled studies show about 1.5 times the expected cancer incidence, with the highest estimates from small single-centre series; a Danish nationwide cohort found no clear rise
GH replacement
Largely reassuring
No clear raised risk in 23,984 GH-treated child…
units.sourceNote: Renehan 2004 · Knuppel 2020 · Dal 2018 · Swerdlow 2017 · Boguszewski 2022 · Guevara-Aguirre 2011

assertions.text: IGF-1 receptor signalling drives cell proliferation and survival, giving theoretical oncologic concern to IGF-1-raising agents.
assertions.quote: IGF−1 receptor signaling activates proliferative and anti−apoptotic pathways, including PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK, and contributes to cell−cycle progression, survival, and invasion ( 160 – 163 ).
assertions.note: Dominikowski et al. describe that IGF-1 receptor signalling activates proliferative and anti-apoptotic pathways promoting cell-cycle progression and survival.

assertions.text: In large studies, higher circulating IGF-1 concentrations are associated with increased risks of colorectal, breast, prostate, and thyroid cancer.
assertions.quote: Higher IGF-I concentration was associated with increased risks of thyroid cancer [HR per 5 nmol/L higher concentration 1.18; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.37] in addition to colorectal (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.03-1.13), breast (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.07-1.15), and prostate cancer (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.05-1.12), and reduced risks of ovarian and liver cancer.
assertions.note: UK Biobank analyses observed positive associations between serum IGF-1 and thyroid, colorectal, breast, and prostate cancer.

assertions.text: In large prospective studies of natural IGF-1 and cancer risk, reverse causality cannot be excluded.
assertions.quote: Mean follow-up was 6.9 years and the possibility that the observed associations may be influenced by reverse causality bias cannot be excluded.
assertions.note: The UK Biobank study explicitly states that reverse causality bias cannot be ruled out.

assertions.text: In an Ecuadorian cohort with growth hormone receptor deficiency, subjects had almost no cancer.
assertions.quote: The individuals with GHR deficiency (GHRD) exhibited only one non-lethal malignancy and no cases of diabetes, in contrast to 17% cancer and 5% diabetes prevalence in the controls.
assertions.note: Guevara-Aguirre et al. found only one non-lethal malignancy across 22 years of monitoring in the GHRD cohort compared to 17% in controls.

assertions.text: In acromegaly, pooled studies show an overall cancer standardized incidence ratio of about 1.5, with higher estimates in single-centre studies, while a Danish nationwide cohort found no clear rise (SIR 1.1).
assertions.quote: The cohort study identified 81 cases of cancer after exclusion of cases diagnosed within the first year [SIR 1.1; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.9 to 1.4]. SIRs were 1.4 (95% CI, 0.7 to 2.6) for colorectal cancer, 1.1 (95% CI, 0.5 to 2.1) for breast cancer, and 1.4 (95% CI, 0.6 to 2.6) for prostate cancer. Whereas overall mortality was elevated in acromegaly (SIR 1.3; 95% CI, 1.1 to 1.6), cancer-specific mortality was not. The meta-analysis yielded an SIR of overall cancer of 1.5 (95% CI, 1.2 to 1.8).
assertions.note: Dal et al. reported a nationwide cohort SIR of 1.1 (0.9 to 1.4) and a meta-analysis SIR of 1.5 (1.2 to 1.8), noting higher estimates in single-centre studies.

assertions.text: A European cohort of 23,984 childhood GH recipients found no clear raised cancer risk in patients treated for growth failure without other major disease.
assertions.quote: There was no clear raised risk in patients with growth failure without other major disease.
assertions.note: Swerdlow et al. analyzed 23,984 r-hGH patients and observed no clear raised cancer risk in those with isolated growth failure.

assertions.text: A 2022 consensus statement concluded that evidence does not support an association between GH replacement and primary tumour or cancer recurrence in survivors.
assertions.quote: Current evidence reviewed from the proceedings from the Workshop does not support an association between GH replacement and primary tumour or cancer recurrence.
assertions.note: Boguszewski et al. state that current evidence does not support an association between GH replacement therapy and primary tumour or cancer recurrence in survivors.

assertions.text: No long-term peer-reviewed human cancer data exist for secretagogues or IGF-1 LR3.
assertions.quote: This risk framing should be presented as theoretical but clinically relevant, especially in the absence of long-term safety data for off-label IGF-1 analogue use ( 117 ).
assertions.note: Dominikowski et al. highlight that IGF-1 LR3 lacks peer-reviewed human studies and that no long-term safety data exist for these off-label compounds.

units.text:
The evidence
Half the patients on the approved one.
Tesamorelin is the best-studied peptide on this axis. In its pivotal trials, 47% of treated patients had IGF-1 more than two standard deviations above the mean at 26 weeks, and 36% more than three. Its label states that the effects of prolonged IGF-1 elevation are unknown. For unapproved secretagogues bought for skin, nobody has published the equivalent figure.
of tesamorelin-treated patients with IGF-1 above +2 SD at 26 weeks in its pivotal trials
36% above +3 SD · label: effects of prolonged elevation unknown
What it means: Pushing IGF-1 above the normal range is common even with an approved GHRH analogue used as labelled, in monitored trials.
What it does not mean: It does not show that tesamorelin causes cancer, and it is no target to aim for. It shows why sustained, unmonitored use of any IGF-1-raising product is an open safety que…

assertions.note: The review notes that epidemiologic and mechanistic concerns regarding IGF-1 elevation do not establish that any specific PEP causes cancer in humans.

units.text:
What do you do first?
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Reassure her that mild water retention is expected on growth-hormone peptides and review in three months.
Explanation: Fluid retention is a known effect, but this cluster is the pattern the Endocrine Society says should prompt IGF-1 testing. Three more months on an unmonitored product leaves it unassessed.
Correct answer: Advise stopping the product, record exactly what she used, from where and for how long, and route her promptly to a prescriber for assessment of GH excess, including IGF-1.
Explanation: Right. Stop the exposure, capture the product details, and get the signs assessed. Fluid retention on these agents usually settles when treatment stops; signs that persist need an endocrine work-up.

Evidence, regulation and compliance · three lessons
Lesson 7.1 Grading the evidence behind an aesthetic claim · Lesson 7.2 Compounding law, the 40-amino-acid line and certificates of analysis · Lesson 7.3 Cosmetic, compounded or investigational: consent and the chart.
Module 07 · Evidence, regulation and compliance
Grade it, check it, write it down.
This last module turns the course into three habits. You will rate the certainty behind a claim with GRADE, read a compounding status and a certificate of analysis for what they do and do not prove, and write the consent and chart note that an unapproved product needs. The regulatory detail is given for the US and the UK: lesson 7.2 adds the UK route for unlicensed medicines and the UK rules on selling and advertising peptides. EU rules are not covered.
Your turn
Three trials, grade A?
One question to close lesson 7.1.
A clean certificate.
On…

Lesson 7.1 · Concept
GRADE rates certainty in an effect, one outcome at a time.
GRADE sorts the evidence on a specific question into four levels of certainty: high, moderate, low and very low. The rating applies to a body of evidence for one outcome, never to a single study or to a molecule. Randomized trials start high and observational studies start low; certainty then falls for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or suspected publication bias, and occasionally rises for a very large effect. Both Hormonaly guides print the letters A to D for the same idea, adapted, and attach each letter to a specific use.
Four levels, applied to a body of evidence
Five named reasons to rate down
The letter belongs to a use, never to a molecule
Narration: Every claim you hear about a skin peptide carries a hidden question. How sure can we be? GRADE answers it with four levels of cert…
units.sourceNote: Guyatt 2008 · Balshem 2011 · Core GRADE 2025 · Hormonaly guides

assertions.text: GRADE sorts evidence into four levels of certainty (high, moderate, low, and very low) applied to a body of evidence rather than individual studies.
assertions.quote: GRADE specifies four categories-high, moderate, low, and very low-that are applied to a body of evidence, not to individual studies.
assertions.note: GRADE defines four levels of certainty evaluated across a body of evidence.

assertions.text: Randomized trials begin as high-certainty evidence, whereas observational studies begin as low-certainty evidence.
assertions.quote: Randomized trials begin as high-quality evidence, observational studies as low quality.
assertions.note: Baseline certainty begins high for randomized trials and low for observational studies.

assertions.text: Certainty can be rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, or suspected publication bias.
assertions.quote: "Quality" as used in GRADE means more than risk of bias and so may also be compromised by imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness of study results, and publication bias.
assertions.note: The framework lists these five factors as reasons evidence certainty may be downgraded.

assertions.text: Evidence certainty can occasionally rise when an effect is very large.
assertions.quote: Core GRADE users appraising results from well conducted NSRI can consider rating up certainty of evidence when risk ratios from pooled estimates suggest large or very large effects.
assertions.note: Large or very large effect estimates are recognized grounds for rating up certainty.

assertions.text: Hormonaly guides adapt GRADE using the letters A to D attached to specific uses, rating clinical evidence rather than legality.
assertions.quote:
Every entry carries a GRADE letter. GRADE reflects the strength of the
clinical evidence for the listed use — not mechanistic plausibility, popularity,
compounding availability, or clinical fashion.
assertions.note: The guide assigns GRADE letters A through D to specific indications, separating evidence from regulatory legality.

units.text:
Who paid
Sponsored studies come out better.
A Cochrane methodology review brought together 75 papers, each comparing studies sponsored by the manufacturer with studies funded in other ways. Industry-sponsored drug and device studies more often reported favourable efficacy results and favourable conclusions, and the difference was not explained by the usual risk-of-bias checks. It is the pattern you met with oral collagen in module 04.
1.27
risk ratio for a favourable efficacy result, industry-sponsored versus other studies
Lundh et al., Cochrane 2017 · 95% CI 1.17–1.37 · moderate-certainty evidence
What it means: When a manufacturer pays for the trial, a favourable result is more likely. Funding is a reason to read a trial harder and to look for independent replication.
What it does not mean: It does not make a sponsored trial wrong or an independent one right. It describes an average ti…
units.sourceNote: Lundh et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2017 · Myung & Park 2025 · Core GRADE 4

assertions.text: A Cochrane methodology review included 75 papers comparing studies sponsored by the manufacturer with studies funded in other ways.
assertions.quote: Twenty-seven new papers were included in this update and in total the review contains 75 included papers.
assertions.note: The Cochrane review included a total of 75 papers comparing industry-sponsored studies with studies having other sources of sponsorship.

assertions.text: Industry-sponsored drug and device studies more often reported favourable efficacy results and favourable conclusions, and the difference was not explained by standard risk-of-bias assessments.
assertions.quote: Sponsorship of drug and device studies by the manufacturing company leads to more favorable efficacy results and conclusions than sponsorship by other sources. Our analyses suggest the existence of an industry bias that cannot be explained by standard 'Risk of bias' assessments.
assertions.note: The Cochrane review concluded that industry sponsorship leads to more favourable efficacy results and conclusions that are not explained by standard risk-of-bias checks.

assertions.text: The pooled risk ratio for a favourable efficacy result in industry-sponsored versus other studies was 1.27 (95% CI: 1.17 to 1.37) based on moderate-certainty evidence.
assertions.quote: Industry sponsored studies more often had favorable efficacy results, RR: 1.27 (95% CI: 1.17 to 1.37) (25 papers) (moderate quality evidence), similar harms results RR: 1.37 (95% CI: 0.64 to 2.93) (four papers) (very low quality evidence) and more often favorable conclusions RR: 1.34 (95% CI: 1.19 to 1.51) (29 papers) (low quality evidence) compared with non-industry sponsored studies.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Two checks, never one.
Evidence grade and regulatory status are separate axes, and both Hormonaly guides ask you to clear both. An approved drug can carry a low grade for the use a patient wants, and a compound with stronger human data can still have no lawful route. A plausible mechanism never raises a grade. Say the outcome, the grade and who ran the trials, then check the status as its own step.
Grade: certainty for this outcome
Status: what the law allows, checked separately
Mechanism never raises a grade
Narration: Suppose a patient asks whether a peptide works. Start with the outcome they care about, say fewer lines around the eyes, and give the certainty for that outcome, along with who paid for the trials behind it. Then, as a separate step, check what the product legally is. The Hormonaly guides keep these two checks apart for a reason. An approved drug …

assertions.text: Regulatory status and evidence grade are distinct axes; an approved drug can have a lower evidence grade for a specific use, while an agent with stronger evidence may lack a lawful route.

assertions.note: Supported by the editorial standards of the Peptide Pocket Guide.

Correct answer: Low or very low: small sponsor-run trials that measured hydration, not wrinkles.

assertions.note: Core GRADE begins the assessment of randomised controlled trials at high certainty.

units.text:
Lesson 7.2 · Concept
Two compounding routes, one strict order.
In the US, section 503A lets a licensed pharmacist or physician compound for an identified patient on a prescription, exempt from new-drug approval, adequate directions for use and good manufacturing practice. The bulk substance must meet a USP or NF monograph; failing that, be a component of an approved drug; failing that, appear on FDA's 503A bulks list. It must also come from an FDA-registered establishment with a valid certificate of analysis. Section 503B outsourcing facilities register with FDA, work to good manufacturing practice under inspection, and may compound without patient-specific prescriptions.
503A: patient-specific, three exemptions
Monograph, then approved component, then the bulks list
503B: registered, inspected, held to good manufacturing practice
Narration: Two routes exist for compounding in the United…
units.sourceNote: 21 U.S.C. 353a and 353b · FDA 503A bulks page (updated 14 May 2026) · FDA, information for outsourcing facilities

assertions.text: Under section 503A in the US, a licensed pharmacist or physician can compound for an identified patient based on a prescription, exempt from new-drug approval, adequate directions for use, and good manufacturing practice.

Dated to the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 and MHRA guidance as read on 25 September 2026.
The route (regulation 167)
One patient, one prescriber, an unsolicited order
Made to the specification of a doctor, dentist, nurse or pharmacist independent prescriber or supplementary prescriber, for a patient under their direct care. No advertisement may be published.
Who makes it
A manufacturer with a specials licence
The site is inspected for good manufacturing practice; the product itself is otherwise unassessed for safety, quality and efficacy. A pharmacist may a…

assertions.text: Under UK law (HMR 2012 reg 167), an unlicensed medicine may be supplied to meet an individual patient's special clinical needs, manufactured to the specification of an authorized prescriber for a patient under their direct care in response to an unsolicited order, and cannot be advertised.
assertions.quote: 167. —(1) The prohibitions in regulation 46 (requirement for authorisation) do not apply in relation to a medicinal product (a “special medicinal product”) if— (a) the medicinal product is supplied in response to an unsolicited order; (b) the medicinal product is manufactured and assembled in accordance with the specification of a person who is a doctor, dentist, nurse independent prescriber, pharmacist independent prescriber or supplementary prescriber; (c) the medicinal product is for use by a patient for whose treatment that person is directly responsible in order to fulfil the special needs of that patient; and (d) the following conditions are met.
assertions.note: Supported by Regulation 167 of the Human Medicines Regulations 2012.

assertions.text: UK specials manufacturers are inspected for Good Manufacturing Practice, but the unlicensed product itself is otherwise unassessed for safety, quality, and efficacy.
assertions.quote: 4. If none of these options will suffice, then a completely unlicensed product may have to be used, for example, UK manufactured "specials", which are made in GMP inspected facilities, but which are otherwise un-assessed (GMP inspection of “specials” manufacturers is not product specific).

assertions.text: A pharmacist may also prepare a medicine in a registered pharmacy against a prescription under Section 10 of the Medicines Act 1968.

units.text:
Concept
What a certificate can and cannot prove.
A certificate of analysis is the supplier's own report on a named lot. Mass spectrometry checks identity, and a careful certificate prints the expected mass beside the observed one. HPLC gives purity as a percentage, which says nothing about what the impurities are. Endotoxin, microbial, water, counter-ion, metal and solvent results complete it. A certificate cannot prove that the vial in your hand came from that lot, how it was stored since, or that it is sterile and suitable to inject.
Identity: mass spectrometry, observed against expected
Purity: an HPLC percentage, impurities unnamed
Suitability to inject needs sterility, endotoxin and the right lot
Narration: Picture the certificate a patient hands you, and read it line by line, asking what each line actually tests. Mass spectrometry checks identity, and a careful certificate shows th…
units.sourceNote: Peptide Pocket Guide, peptide fundamentals · FDA PCAC briefing, BPC-157 (July 2026) · FDA endotoxin guidance (2026) · Popławska 2019

assertions.text: A certificate of analysis is the supplier's own quality attestation on a named lot and cannot alone prove that the lot tested is the vial in hand, how the vial was stored, or that it is safe to inject.
assertions.quote: A COA is the supplier's own quality attestation, not an independent certification. A serious COA tells you what the supplier found on a named lot: whether the mass matches the expected molecule, how pure the material was by HPLC, what counter-ion it carries, and what the endotoxin and microbial results were.
assertions.note: The guide explains that a COA is a supplier attestation for a lot and cannot alone prove lot integrity, storage conditions, or suitability for injection.

assertions.text: Mass spectrometry confirms identity by comparing the observed mass against the theoretical expected mass.
assertions.quote: Mass spectrometry confirms the molecular weight matches the expected peptide. The theoretical monoisotopic mass should be reported alongside the observed mass. Deviations > 1 Da indicate sequence problems.
assertions.note: The text confirms mass spectrometry is used to verify peptide molecular weight by checking theoretical against observed mass.

assertions.text: HPLC purity reports the percentage of the main peak but does not specify or identify the impurity profile on its own.
assertions.quote: In the CoA provided by nominator 2, there is only a purity test with the testing result of 98.34%. There is no impurity attribute control to demonstrate the impurity profiles.
assertions.note: The briefing notes that reporting purity testing alone lacks attribute control to demonstrate impurity profiles.

assertions.text: The allowable endotoxin limit for a parenteral product is derived from the dose and route of administration rather than a single universal limit.
assertions.quote: There is no single universal per-milligram limit: the allowable endotoxin for a parenteral product is derived from the maximum human dose and the route, so the same concentration can pass for one product and fail for another. A COA reporting endotoxin without stating the dose and route it was judged against has not established suitability for injection.
assertions.note: The source states that parenteral endotoxin limits depend on the maximum dose and administration route.

assertions.text: In FDA's review of BPC-157 for the advisory committee, most public certificates listed purity alone, and the nominator's CoA omitted endotoxin testing.
assertions.quote: No bioburden/endotoxin test is mentioned in the CoA provided by the nominator. Endotoxin test is considered a critical quality attribute to control microbiological quality of a BDS intended for an injection product.
assertions.note: The briefing notes that public CoAs mostly reported only purity and the nominator's CoA omitted bioburden/endotoxin testing.

Label against laboratory
99% on the label.
Researchers made test purchases of semaglutide from illegal online pharmacies and analysed what arrived. The three vials that were delivered were all judged probably substandard or falsified: purity measured 7.7–14.4% against the 99% printed on the label, peptide content ran 29–39% above the labelled amount, and endotoxin was found in every vial, although none grew microorganisms.
measured purity of online semaglutide vials labelled 99%
Ashraf et al., J Med Internet Res 2024 · three delivered vials · endotoxin detected in all three
What it means: Purity printed on a label can be wildly wrong, and a vial that grows nothing can still carry endotoxin. Independent testing found what the paperwork hid.
What it does not mean: Three vials of one drug give no market-wide failure rate, and semaglutide is outside the skin-peptide shelf. It documents the g…

assertions.text: Researchers made test purchases of semaglutide from illegal online pharmacies and analysed what arrived, receiving three delivered vials.
assertions.quote: Test purchases were completed from 6 illegal online pharmacies with the highest number of links offering semaglutide products for sale without prescription at the lowest price range. Three injection vial purchases were delivered; none of the 3 Ozempic prefilled injection pens were received due to nondelivery e-commerce scams.
assertions.note: The study completed test purchases across illegal online pharmacies and received three vials for analysis.

assertions.text: All three delivered vials were judged probable substandard or falsified products.
assertions.quote: All purchased vials were considered probable substandard and falsified products, as visual inspection indicated noncompliance in more than half (59%-63%) of the evaluated criteria.
assertions.note: Visual inspection and evaluation classified all purchased vials as probable substandard and falsified.

assertions.text: Measured purity of the semaglutide vials ranged from 7.7% to 14.4% compared to the 99% claimed on the label.
assertions.quote: Furthermore, the measured semaglutide purity was significantly low, ranging between 7.7% and 14.37% and deviating from the 99% claimed on product labels by manufacturers.
assertions.note: Laboratory analysis found semaglutide purity between 7.7% and 14.37%, deviating from the 99% label claim.

assertions.text: Peptide content in the vials exceeded labelled amounts by 29% to 39% (28.56%–38.69%).

assertions.note: Semaglutide quantity substantially exceeded labelled amounts by 28.56% to 38.69%.

assertions.text: Endotoxin was detected in every delivered vial, although none of the samples grew viable microorganisms.

assertions.note: Microbiological analysis showed all samples were devoid of viable microorganisms but all contained endotoxin.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Research use only is a label, and never a route.
In the US, 'not for use in humans' labelling lets a supplier ship an investigational drug for laboratory or in-vitro research, and obliges the shipper to check that is how it will be used. FDA reads intended use from claims, marketing and the circumstances of sale, so the disclaimer changes nothing about a vial sold with injection instructions. A certificate cannot turn such a product into a pharmaceutical.
The label permits laboratory research only
Intended use is read from how a product is sold
A certificate cannot convert a research product
Narration: Research use only sounds like a category. In law it works as a shipping permission. The US rule lets a supplier send an investigational drug for laboratory or test-tube work if the label says it must stay out of people, and the shipper is meant to confirm that is h…

assertions.text: In the United States, 'not for use in humans' labeling permits a supplier to ship an investigational drug for in-vitro or laboratory animal research and obligates the shipper to verify that it will actually be used for such purposes.
assertions.quote: A person shipping a drug under paragraph (a) of this section shall use due diligence to assure that the consignee is regularly engaged in conducting such tests and that the shipment of the new drug will actually be used for tests in vitro or in animals used only for laboratory research.
assertions.note: 21 CFR 312.160 requires due diligence from the shipper to ensure the consignee regularly conducts laboratory/in-vitro tests and will use the shipment for those purposes.

assertions.text: FDA determines intended use objectively from labeling claims, advertising, and circumstances of distribution, so a disclaimer carries no weight when a product is marketed or sold for human use.
assertions.quote: Intended use is read objectively — from labeling claims, advertising, statements, and the circumstances of distribution — so status does not change because a label disclaims the contemplated use.
assertions.note: Intended use is derived objectively from promotional claims and sales context regardless of label disclaimers.

assertions.text: A certificate of analysis cannot convert a research-use-only product into a pharmaceutical.
assertions.quote: None of this turns RUO into pharmaceutical grade, but it surfaces problems before they reach a patient.
assertions.note: Testing documentation and certificates of analysis do not transform research-grade compounds into pharmaceutical-grade drugs.

Regulatory status (UK)
Selling and advertising peptides in the UK.
In the UK, MHRA decides whether a product is a medicine from its claims, including websites and social media, and from its form and the way it is used. units.text:
Lesson 7.3 · Concept
Off-label needs a label.
Off-label prescribing means using an approved drug for a use its labelling does not cover, and FDA accepts it as clinical judgment. A never-approved peptide has no label to depart from, so prescribing it is use of an unapproved drug. Introducing an unapproved new drug into interstate commerce is a prohibited act under the FD&C Act, and FDA's 2020 warning letter to a compounding pharmacy named BPC-157 and GHK-Cu on exactly this basis.
Off-label applies only to approved drugs
Compounded is still unapproved
Narration: Off-label is the phrase to get right first. FDA uses it for an approved drug prescribed outside its labelling, which prescribers generally may do when they judge it medically appropriate. The idea assumes a label exists. A peptide that was never approved has none, so prescribing it counts as using an unapproved drug, and the Peptid…

assertions.text: Off-label prescribing means using an approved drug for an unapproved use outside its approved labeling, which FDA accepts when healthcare providers judge it medically appropriate.
assertions.quote: From the FDA perspective, once the FDA approves a drug, healthcare providers generally may prescribe the drug for an unapproved use when they judge that it is medically appropriate for their patient.
assertions.note: The FDA page explains that healthcare providers generally may prescribe an approved drug for an unapproved use when clinically appropriate.

assertions.text: Off-label prescribing applies only to approved drugs, so prescribing a never-approved peptide is considered the use of an unapproved new drug.
assertions.quote: Off-label use is a legal pathway only for drugs holding at least one FDA-approved indication. Prescribing BPC-157 or any never-approved peptide is use of an unapproved new drug — IND, Expanded Access, and Right-to-Try do not cover routine wellness use.
assertions.note: The clinical reference guide states that off-label use applies only to approved drugs and prescribing a never-approved peptide constitutes use of an unapproved new drug.

assertions.text: Introducing an unapproved new drug into interstate commerce without an effective approved application is a prohibited act under federal law (the FD&C Act).
assertions.quote: Under sections 505(a) and 301(d) of the FDCA [21 U.S.C. § 331(d)], a new drug may not be introduced into or delivered for introduction into interstate commerce unless an application approved by FDA under section 505 of the FDCA is in effect for the drug.
assertions.note: The FDA warning letter cites sections 505(a) and 301(d) of the FDCA prohibiting the introduction of unapproved new drugs into interstate commerce.

assertions.text: In a 2020 warning letter to a compounding pharmacy, the FDA cited compounded BPC-157 and GHK-Cu as ineligible for 503A exemptions, making them unapproved new drugs.
assertions.quote: For example, the investigators noted that your firm compounded drug products using Follistatin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6, Endurobal, AOD 9604, BPC 157, Bremelanotide (PT-141), Cerebrolysin, DSIP, Epitalon, GHK-Cu, IGF1-LR3, Ipamorelin, LL-37, Melanotan II, PEG-MGF, Selank, Semax, CJC 1295, SARMS, LGD-4033, and MK 677.
assertions.note: The 2020 FDA warning letter to Tailor Made Compounding specifically listed BPC 157 and GHK-Cu among bulk drug substances failing section 503A conditions, subjecting them to unapproved new drug provisions.

Same molecule, different rulebooks.

Cosmetic
Appearance claims only
No premarket approval. A claim to affect structure or function, such as 'regenerates cells', makes it a drug; 'cosmeceutical' has no legal meaning.
Dietary supplement
Oral, no disease claims
The maker is responsible for safety and labelling before sale; FDA acts after products reach the market.
Approved drug
Labelled indications
Off-label use of an approved drug is lawful clinical judgment; document the reasoning.
Compounded (503A or 503B)
Unapproved, conditionally lawful
Only when the substance qualifies and the …

assertions.text: Under US law, cosmetics do not require FDA premarket approval.
assertions.quote: Under the FD&C Act, cosmetic products and ingredients, with the exception of color additives, do not require FDA approval before they go on the market.
assertions.note: Supported by the FDA cosmetic regulation page.

assertions.text: A claim to affect structure or function (such as regenerating cells) establishes a product as a drug under US law, and the term 'cosmeceutical' has no legal meaning.
assertions.quote: The FD&C Act does not recognize any such category as "cosmeceuticals." A product can be a drug, a cosmetic, or a combination of both, but the term "cosmeceutical" has no meaning under the law.
assertions.note: Supported by the FDA cosmetic or drug guidance.

assertions.text: For dietary supplements under US law, manufacturers are responsible for evaluating product safety and labelling before marketing, while the FDA acts after products reach the market.
assertions.quote: That means that these firms are responsible for evaluating the safety and labeling of their products before marketing to ensure that they meet all the requirements of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act as amended by DSHEA and FDA regulations. FDA has the authority to take action against any adulterated or misbranded dietary supplement product after it reaches the market.
assertions.note: Supported by the FDA dietary supplement landing page.

assertions.text: Healthcare providers may lawfully prescribe an approved drug for an unapproved (off-label) use based on their clinical judgment.
assertions.quote: From the FDA perspective, once the FDA approves a drug, healthcare providers generally may prescribe the drug for an unapproved use when they judge that it is medically appropriate for their patient.

assertions.text: Under FDA 503A compounding categories as of May 2026, non-injectable GHK-Cu is listed in Category 1.

On May 5, 2026, one of those nominators clarified that it intended to withdraw only its nomination of the injectable route of administration with respect to GHK-Cu and would like to retain its nomination for GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes of administration. GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) will be added back to category 1.
assertions.note: Supported by the FDA 503A categories roster.

assertions.text: Drugs shipped solely for investigational laboratory research or in vitro tests must be labelled not for use in humans and do not constitute a clinical route.
assertions.quote: CAUTION: Contains a new drug for investigational use only in laboratory research animals, or for tests in vitro. Not for use in humans.
assertions.note: Supported by 21 CFR 312.160.

units.text:
Fictional case
'Just prescribe it off-label.'
A 52-year-old patient, three weeks after a fractional laser treatment, asks you to prescribe compounded BPC-157 injections 'off-label' to speed healing. She has found a pharmacy willing to make it and shows you its certificate of analysis. This is a fictional case built from the module's sources, and one response is clearly best.
BPC-157 has no approval, so there is no label to go off
It has no 503A route; FDA staff advised against listing it
A certificate describes a lot and creates no route
Narration: A fictional patient, built from this module's sources, is fifty-two and three weeks past a fractional laser treatment. She asks you to prescribe compounded BPC-157 injections off-label to speed her healing. A pharmacy is willing to make it, and she shows you its certificate of analysis. Three facts shape your answer. BPC-157 has never been app…

assertions.text: BPC-157 has never been FDA-approved, meaning it cannot be prescribed 'off-label' because off-label prescribing requires an existing approved drug label.
assertions.quote: Off-label prescribing presupposes an approved product to be off the label of; for a never-approved peptide the marketing prohibition is unrelieved and the adequate-directions exemption is unavailable.
assertions.note: The pocket guide notes that off-label prescribing presupposes an approved drug to depart from, which does not exist for unapproved peptides.

assertions.text: BPC-157 lacks a 503A compounding route, its nominations were withdrawn, and FDA staff reviewers advised against listing it on the 503A Bulks List in July 2026 due to insufficient evidence of effectiveness.
assertions.quote: Accordingly, we propose not adding BPC-157 (free base) or BPC-157 acetate to the 503A Bulks List.

assertions.text: A certificate of analysis describes a batch but does not by itself establish a lawful 503A compounding route for a bulk drug substance.
assertions.quote: Under section 503A of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, a bulk drug substance may be used in compounding only if it meets a USP or NF monograph, is a component of an FDA-approved drug, or appears on FDA's 503A Bulks List.
assertions.note: The pocket guide explains that 503A compounding requires meeting a USP/NF monograph, being a component of an FDA-approved drug, or appearing on the Bulks List.

units.text:
What do you do?
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Prescribe it as off-label use and file the certificate in her chart.
Explanation: Off-label presupposes an approved drug. BPC-157 has no approval and no 503A route, FDA has warned a compounder about it, and a certificate changes neither fact.
Correct answer: Decline to prescribe it. Explain the evidence and the US status in plain terms, return to the aftercare plan her treating clinician set, and record her request, what you explained and her decision.
Explanation: Right. You keep the conversation, give her the real category and the grade, and leave a chart note a reviewer can follow.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Suggest she buy research-grade BPC-157 with a good certificate and come back for monitoring.
Explanation: Research-use-only products are labelled not for use in humans, and the Peptide Pocket Guide tr…

assertions.text: The Peptide Pocket Guide treats steering a patient to research-grade products as practising medicine, with accompanying liability.

units.text:
GHK-Cu appears in three products: a cream sold 'for the look of fine lines', the same cream sold 'to regenerate skin cells', and an injectable vial labelled research use only. In the US, which statement is right?
Explanation: Name the claim and the route, then the regime.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): All three are cosmetics, because the molecule is the same.
Explanation: The regime follows the claim and the route. A structure-or-function claim makes the second cream a drug, and the vial is no cosmetic at all.
Correct answer: The first is a cosmetic; the second makes a drug claim, so it is an unapproved drug; the vial is outside any clinical route.
Explanation: Correct. Claim and route decide the rulebook, whatever the molecule.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): All three are lawful, because GHK-Cu is in Category 1.
Explanation: Category 1 covers 503A compound…

assertions.text: Under US FDA regulations, cosmetic claims alter appearance, whereas claims to regenerate cells are structure-or-function drug claims that subject the product to drug regulatory requirements.
assertions.quote: Certain claims may cause a product to be considered a drug, even if the product is marketed as if it were a cosmetic. Such claims establish the product as a drug because the intended use is to treat or prevent disease or otherwise affect the structure or functions of the human body. Some examples are claims that products will restore hair growth, reduce cellulite, treat varicose veins, increase or decrease the production of melanin (pigment) in the skin, or regenerate cells.
assertions.note: FDA guidance explains that altering appearance is a cosmetic intended use, whereas cell regeneration claims establish the product as a drug.

assertions.text: A drug vial labeled for research use only is restricted to laboratory research animals or in vitro testing and is not for human clinical use.
assertions.quote: A person may ship a drug intended solely for tests in vitro or in animals used only for laboratory research purposes if it is labeled as follows: CAUTION: Contains a new drug for investigational use only in laboratory research animals, or for tests in vitro. Not for use in humans.
assertions.note: 21 CFR 312.160 requires research-only investigational drugs to be labeled for laboratory research animals or in vitro tests and not for human use.

assertions.text: FDA's 503A Category 1 includes GHK-Cu only for non-injectable routes under its interim policy on bulk drug substances under evaluation.
assertions.quote: o “GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) ” - GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) was removed from c ategory 1 on April 22, 2026, because the nominations for GHK-Cu were withdrawn by the nominators. On May 5, 2026, one of those nominators clarified that it intended to withdraw only its nomination of the injectable route of administration with respect to GHK-Cu and would like to retain its nomination for GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes of administration. GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) will be added back to category 1.
assertions.note: The 503A bulk drug substances document lists GHK-Cu in Category 1 explicitly excluding injectable routes of administration.

Closing Module 7: which statement keeps evidence, regulatory status and product quality apart?
Explanation: Grade, status and quality: three checks, never one sentence.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The certificate shows 99% purity, so the peptide is evidence-based and fine to compound.
Explanation: That blends product quality into evidence and legality. Purity says nothing about whether it works or whether any route is lawful.
Correct answer: Topical GHK-Cu: small-trial evidence (C); in the US, non-injectable use sits in 503A Category 1, under evaluation; its certificate can show identity and purity, never sterility or legality.
Explanation: Correct. Three separate answers, each with its own source.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): GHK-Cu is in Category 1, so it is approved for skin and the evidence question is settled.
Explanation: Category 1 is an enforcem…

assertions.text: Topical GHK-Cu is supported by small-trial evidence and carries a GRADE C evidence rating.
assertions.quote: Clinical caveat. Evidence base: topical cosmetic RCTs (cosmeceutical use) and preclinical wound-healing models — injectable human use rests on anecdote, no RCTs.
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni (2026) rates GHK-Cu as GRADE C based on topical cosmetic RCTs and preclinical models.

assertions.text: In the United States, non-injectable GHK-Cu is classified under 503A Category 1 (Bulk Drug Substances Under Evaluation).
assertions.quote: GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) will be added back to category 1. FDA has announced it intends to consult the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) before the end of February 2027 regarding the potential inclusion of GHK-Cu on the 503A bulks list.
assertions.note: FDA's 503A category lists confirm non-injectable GHK-Cu is in Category 1 for substances under evaluation.

assertions.text: 503A Category 1 represents an interim enforcement-discretion posture while FDA evaluates a substance rather than formal drug approval.
assertions.quote: Categories 1, 2 and 3 are something else: enforcement-discretion postures described in FDA guidance while nominations are evaluated.
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni (2026) explains that Category 1 is an enforcement posture during evaluation, not approval or statutory bulks listing.

units.text:
A single-cell RNA atlas predicts that a skin cell type can make a hormone. What would move that finding toward proof of secretion?
Explanation: Transcriptomic maps predict capacity; secretion and function need protein-level and functional evidence, and clinical use needs human trials.
Correct answer: Showing the hormone protein and its release by those cells, then its effect in tissue or in people.
Explanation: Correct. RNA is the first rung; protein, release and function are the next.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Finding the same RNA in a second atlas.
Explanation: Replicating the RNA confirms the transcript, which is still a prediction about secretion.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Finding the hormone's receptor RNA in neighbouring cells.
Explanation: That predicts a possible receiver; it does not show the hormone is made or released.

assertions.text: Transcriptomic data provide putative predictions of capacity rather than proof of functional hormones, requiring protein-level and functional validation to establish secretion and activity.
assertions.quote: Important: these predictions are based on transcriptomic data and should be considered as putative and hypothesis-generating, rather than as functional hormones and receptors. The user takes responsibility for validation using appropriate methods (e.g. in vitro, in vivo) and for describing appropriately their use of transcriptome-based scores and predictions.
assertions.note: The Hormone Cell Atlas portal emphasizes that transcriptome-based predictions are putative and hypothesis-generating, requiring validation using methods such as in vitro and in vivo testing.

units.text:
Which finding is a local cutaneous feedback loop rather than systemic endocrine signalling?
Explanation: A local loop is made and used within the skin; systemic signals travel through the blood, in either direction.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Skin-made vitamin D3 carried by the blood to the liver.
Explanation: That is the skin supplying a whole-body hormone system: skin to body.
Correct answer: Human scalp follicles in culture secrete cortisol and then reduce their own CRH.
Explanation: Correct. Made, sensed and fed back within the follicle, with no systemic connection.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Thin skin and striae in Cushing syndrome.
Explanation: Circulating cortisol excess acting on the skin: body to skin.

assertions.text: Human scalp hair follicles in culture synthesize and secrete cortisol and exhibit a local feedback loop where glucocorticoid signaling down-regulates follicular CRH expression.
assertions.quote: Finally, human hair follicles display HPA axis-like regulatory feedback systems, since the glucocorticoid receptor agonist hydrocortisone down-regulates follicular CRH expression.
assertions.note: Ito et al. demonstrated that isolated human scalp hair follicles secrete cortisol and down-regulate CRH expression in response to glucocorticoid receptor activation without systemic connections.

units.text:
Why can a blood or saliva cortisol level not tell you how much cortisol a patient's skin is generating?
Explanation: Local tissue cortisol and systemic cortisol are separate: the first is a research mechanism, the second is what diagnostic tests measure.
Correct answer: Because 11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol inside skin cells, and local availability is regulated independently of circulating levels.
Explanation: Correct: a mechanism shown in human skin samples and mice.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because skin cells cannot make or activate cortisol.
Explanation: They can: skin expresses an HPA-like axis, and 11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol locally.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because saliva and blood cortisol tests are unreliable for everything.
Explanation: Late-night salivary cortisol is a first-line test for Cushing's syndrome; it measures systemic cort…

assertions.text: 11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol inside skin cells, and local glucocorticoid availability is regulated independently of circulating levels.
assertions.quote: Within target tissues, GC availability is regulated at a prereceptor level, independently of systemic levels, by isozymes of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (11β-HSD) that interconvert active cortisol and inactive cortisone.
assertions.note: The abstract confirms that 11β-HSD1 activates cortisol and that glucocorticoid availability is regulated at a prereceptor level independently of systemic levels.

assertions.text: 11β-HSD1 expression and activity have been demonstrated in human skin samples and mice.
assertions.quote: 11β-HSD1 (which activates cortisol), but not 11β-HSD2 (which inactivates cortisol), was expressed in epidermal keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts in human skin and also in outer hair follicle root sheath cells in murine skin.
assertions.note: The abstract confirms 11β-HSD1 expression and activity in human and murine skin cells/explants.

assertions.text: Skin expresses an HPA-like axis.
assertions.note: The provided abstracts do not mention an HPA-like axis in the skin.

assertions.text: Late-night salivary cortisol is a first-line diagnostic test for Cushing's syndrome.
assertions.quote: We recommend initial use of one test with high diagnostic accuracy (urine cortisol, late night salivary cortisol, 1 mg overnight or 2 mg 48-h dexamethasone suppression test).
assertions.note: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends late-night salivary cortisol as one of the initial tests for Cushing's syndrome.

units.text:
A patient asks whether starting hormone therapy at menopause will stop her wrinkles. Which answer fits the evidence?
Explanation: Separate structural effects (small trials) from visible ageing (large trials) and from indications (symptoms and bone).
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Yes: estrogen rebuilds collagen, so her wrinkles will improve.
Explanation: Small trials show thicker skin, but the largest trials found no difference in wrinkles.
Correct answer: It may thicken the skin a little, the largest trials found no difference in wrinkles, and skin is not a reason to start; hot flashes or vaginal symptoms are worth discussing with a prescriber.
Explanation: Correct: a secondary effect, and an indication-led decision.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): It has no effect on skin at all.
Explanation: Small RCTs do show gains in thickness and collagen; what is unpro…

assertions.text: Estrogen therapy can increase skin and dermal thickness in small clinical trials.
assertions.quote: Treatment with conjugated estrogens for 12 months significantly increases, at the level of the right great trochanter, the thickness of the skin (p < 0.01), as assessed by ultrasonography, and of the dermis (p < 0.05), as assessed by skin biopsy.
assertions.note: A randomized trial showed conjugated estrogens significantly increased skin and dermal thickness compared to placebo.

assertions.text: Clinical trial evidence evaluating hormone therapy found no statistically significant difference in age-related facial wrinkling compared to placebo.
assertions.quote: There were slight decreases in all parameters for all treatment groups for the primary subject end points, but there were no statistically significant differences between the NA/EE groups and placebo.
assertions.note: A 485-subject randomized controlled trial found no statistically significant differences between hormone therapy and placebo for facial wrinkling.

assertions.text: Hot flashes and vaginal symptoms are approved indications for starting menopausal hormone therapy.
assertions.quote: The FDA has approved multiple hormone therapies for moderate-to-severe hot flashes, vaginal dryness and discomfort, and preventing bone loss.
assertions.note: The FDA notes approved indications for hormone therapy include hot flashes and vaginal dryness.

units.text:
A colleague says tirzepatide is 'GRADE A', so its effect on the face must be well established. What is wrong with that reasoning?
Explanation: An evidence grade belongs to a statement, not to a molecule. SURMOUNT-1 supports an A for weight loss; facial change rests on a 20-patient imaging study and a patient survey (C to D), and no randomized trial has measured the face.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Nothing: a drug's grade applies to all of its effects.
Explanation: Grades attach to a specific outcome in a specific population. The pivotal trials measured weight and never the face.
Correct answer: Grades attach to outcomes: weight loss is A from large randomized trials, while facial change rests on small observational studies.
Explanation: Correct. One grade per outcome.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Tirzepatide has no GRADE A evidence for anything.
Explan…

assertions.text: The SURMOUNT-1 phase 3 randomized controlled trial demonstrated substantial weight reduction with tirzepatide.
assertions.note: SURMOUNT-1 was a phase 3 randomized controlled trial evaluating tirzepatide for body weight reduction.

units.text:
Which statement about the gut–skin link is best supported by the evidence?
Explanation: High-fat feeding raises circulating endotoxin in mice and briefly in healthy men; a leading review finds it unproven that restoring barrier function improves disease outside the gut, and Cochrane found little or no patient-rated benefit from probiotics in eczema.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Probiotic capsules reliably clear eczema by repairing the gut barrier.
Explanation: Pooled trials show little or no difference in patient-rated eczema symptoms.
Correct answer: Metabolic endotoxaemia is shown in mice and small human studies, but restoring the gut barrier has not been shown to improve disease outside the gut.
Explanation: Correct. Mechanism in mice and short-term human physiology; no proof that barrier repair helps the skin.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): A zonulin b…

assertions.text: High-fat feeding chronically increases circulating endotoxin in mice.
assertions.quote: We found that normal endotoxemia increased or decreased during the fed or fasted state, respectively, on a nutritional basis and that a 4-week high-fat diet chronically increased plasma LPS concentration two to three times, a threshold that we have defined as metabolic endotoxemia.
assertions.note: Cani et al. found that a 4-week high-fat diet increased plasma LPS concentrations 2- to 3-fold in mice.

assertions.text: A high-fat meal induces a transient increase in circulating endotoxin in healthy men.
assertions.quote: Baseline endotoxin concentrations were 8.2 pg/mL (interquartile range: 3.4-13.5 pg/mL) but increased significantly (P < 0.05) by approximately 50% after a high-fat meal or after a high-fat meal with cigarettes but not after no meal or cigarettes alone.
assertions.note: Erridge et al. reported a significant ~50% increase in endotoxin levels following a high-fat meal in 12 healthy men.

assertions.text: It remains unproven that restoring intestinal barrier function improves disease outside the gut.
assertions.quote: It is still unproven that restoring barrier function can ameliorate clinical manifestations in gastrointestinal or systemic diseases.
assertions.note: Camilleri notes in the review that proof is lacking for barrier restoration improving systemic or extra-intestinal disease manifestations.

assertions.text: A Cochrane systematic review found little or no difference in patient-rated eczema symptoms from probiotics.

units.text:
Which statement about topical GHK-Cu keeps its evidence and its regulatory status apart correctly?
Explanation: Mechanism, human evidence and regulatory status are separate registers; GHK-Cu scores differently on each.
Correct answer: It is GRADE C on small trials, and in the US its non-injectable form sits in 503A Category 1, which means under evaluation.
Explanation: Correct. Two separate answers: small-trial human evidence, and an enforcement posture that is not an approval.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Its Category 1 listing shows FDA has found it effective for skin.

Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Its copper-enzyme mechanism makes its evidence grade A.
Explanation: A plausible mechanism is not human evidence; the trials are small (C).

assertions.text: GHK-Cu has human evidence rated as GRADE C based on small trials.

units.text:

Explanation: Funding and study quality can explain a pooled effect; ask who ran the trial before what it showed.

units.text:

Explanation: The US indication is to increase pain-free light exposure in adults with EPP; tanning is not an approved use.

Explanation: Its compounding nominat…

units.text:
A patient asks about a PTD-DBM hair spray. Which grade fits its evidence, and why?
Explanation: Grade the human evidence, then say who produced it; a strong mechanism with no trial in people is D.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): A, because it acts on the central Wnt pathway of hair growth.
Explanation: A plausible pathway is mechanism, and grades rest on human evidence.
Correct answer: D: one 2017 study in mice and scalp tissue from the developer's group, and no human trial published or registered as of September 2026.
Explanation: Correct. Animal and tissue data only, from one group with a commercial link.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): C, because small human trials show regrowth.
Explanation: No human trial of PTD-DBM exists, small or large.

assertions.text: PTD-DBM hair treatment is graded D because its evidence base is limited to preclinical animal and tissue data with no human clinical trials.
assertions.quote: Trial stage: preclinical only; no human RCTs.

assertions.quote: CXXC5 was upregulated in miniaturized hair follicles and arrector pili muscles in human balding scalps. The inhibitory effects of CXXC5 on alkaline phosphatase activity and cell proliferation were demonstrated using human hair follicle dermal papilla cells. Moreover, CXXC5 -/- mice displayed accelerated hair regrowth, and treatment with valproic acid, a glycogen synthase kinase 3β inhibitor that activates the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, further induced hair regrowth in the CXXC5 -/- mice.

units.text:
Why does a 'low' IGF-1 in a healthy 60-year-old not, on its own, justify growth-hormone therapy?
Explanation: Treat confirmed deficiency, not ageing: age-adjusted ranges plus the healthy-ageing trials.
Correct answer: IGF-1 falls normally with age, and trials in healthy older adults show small body-composition gains with more oedema, joint pain and glucose problems.
Explanation: Correct. The somatopause is physiology, and the trials point against treatment.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because growth hormone has no effect on skin at all.
Explanation: GH acts on dermal fibroblasts, and GH excess visibly changes skin. The problem is the balance of benefit and harm in healthy adults.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because IGF-1 cannot be measured reliably.
Explanation: IGF-1 is a standard test. The point is to read it against an age-matched range and to treat…

assertions.text: Trials of growth-hormone therapy in healthy older adults show small body-composition gains along with increased rates of oedema, joint pain (arthralgias), and glucose problems.

units.text:
In GRADE, what does a certainty rating attach to?
Explanation: Name the outcome before you name the grade; risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias can each lower it.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): A single well-run trial.
Explanation: GRADE rates a body of evidence, never one study on its own.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The molecule, across all its uses.
Explanation: The same molecule can be high certainty for one outcome and very low for another.
Correct answer: A body of evidence for a specific outcome.
Explanation: Correct. Certainty belongs to an outcome, across the studies that address it.

assertions.text: In GRADE, certainty ratings apply to a body of evidence rather than an individual study on its own.
assertions.quote: GRADE specifies four categories-high, moderate, low, and very low-that are applied to a body of evidence, not to individual studies.
assertions.note: GRADE quality ratings are applied to a body of evidence rather than individual studies.

assertions.text: In GRADE, quality/certainty ratings can be lowered or compromised by risk of bias, imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness, and publication bias.
assertions.quote: "Quality" as used in GRADE means more than risk of bias and so may also be compromised by imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness of study results, and publication bias.
assertions.note: GRADE guidelines state that quality may be compromised by risk of bias, imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness, and publication bias.

units.text:
Under section 503A, in what order does the statute let a bulk substance qualify for compounding?

Explanation: Reversed. The bulks list is the last route, open only when the first two are not.
Correct answer: A USP or NF monograph first, then a component of an approved drug, then the 503A bulks list, with a valid certificate of analysis in every case.
Explanation: Correct. The routes are hierarchical, and the certificate and a registered manufacturer are conditions throughout.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Any substance whose certificate of analysis shows high purity.
Explanation: A certificate is a condition, never a route on …

units.text: The Hormone Cell Atlas (Fei, Huang-Doran et al., Science 2026) read RNA for 379 hormone and receptor genes in about 14 million cells and nuclei from 47 human tissues and predicted which cell types could make or respond to hormones. Its own authors call these predictions putative and hypothesis-generating: RNA shows capacity, not secretion or effect. Treat any 'skin has receptors for it' product claim as a hypothesis until protein, function and a human trial back it. A few skin outputs are established in people, such as vitamin D3 formed under UVB and released into the blood.

Using hormone2cell, we mapped putative hormone-producing and hormone-receiving cell types, defining tissue-specific and cross-tissue endocrine signatures.

units.text: Most 'cortisol face' is puffiness from sleep, alcohol, salt and weight, as the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide describes it. Endogenous Cushing's syndrome is rare (two to three new cases per million people a year), and its commonest form comes from a glucocorticoid the patient is using, so ask about tablets, inhalers, injections and creams, including skin-lighteners. The features that best discriminate Cushing's are easy bruising, facial plethora, proximal muscle weakness and reddish-purple striae wider than 1 cm; a round face alone is a weak signal. If several are present and progressing, the next step is formal testing arranged by a prescriber and an endocrinologist, not a supplement or a consumer cortisol panel. Local skin cortisol (11β-HSD1) is a research mechanism with no approved treatment.

units.text: 'Ozempic face' describes facial hollowing and laxity during weight loss on incretin drugs. No randomized trial has measured the face. assertions.text: A retrospective imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, primarily in superficial fat compartments, and about 7% per 10 kg lost.

The average duration of GLP-1 agonists was 321 days (SD = 291), and the average weight loss was 11.0 kg (SD = 6.9). The median percent decrease in total midfacial volume was 9.0% (IQR 3%-14%).
assertions.note: The retrospective cohort study of 20 patients found a median 9.0% decrease in total midfacial volume and 7% facial volume loss per 10 kg weight lost, predominantly in superficial fat pads.

assertions.text: A survey of 1,226 patients found that skin sagging, facial volume loss, and hair shedding were reported significantly more often with greater weight loss.
assertions.quote: Cochran–Armitage trend testing identified significant positive trends across the < 10%, 10–20%, and > 20% body weight loss categories for skin sagging ( Z = 15.22), hair loss ( Z = 9.91), decreased facial volume ( Z = 10.70), and reduced strength ( Z = 7.85), with P values of < 0.001.
assertions.note: The survey of 1,226 patients confirmed significant positive trends across weight loss categories for skin sagging, hair loss, and decreased facial volume.

( 1 ) • to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in: o adults and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with obesity. ( 1 ) o adults with overweight in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition. ( 1 ) • for the treatment of noncirrhotic metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), formerly known as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis (consistent with stages F2 to F3 fibrosis) in adults.

For weight management, including weight loss and weight maintenance, as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity in adults with an initial Body Mass Index (BMI) of • ≥ 30 kg/ m 2 (obesity) or • ≥ 27 kg/m 2 to < 30 kg/m 2 (overweight) in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition

units.text: Mechanism: bacterial lipopolysaccharide crossing a leaky gut barrier ('metabolic endotoxaemia') drives inflammation and insulin resistance in mice, and a single high-fat meal briefly raised plasma endotoxin in a study of 12 healthy men (D). Human evidence for skin: an independent Cochrane review of 39 trials found probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated eczema symptoms (B); a 2024 meta-analysis in children without food allergy reported small score improvements (C); one small randomized trial found rosacea improved after small-intestinal bacterial overgrowth was treated (C). A leading review concludes it is unproven that restoring barrier function improves disease outside the gut, and a widely used commercial zonulin assay detects proteins other than zonulin. A fibre-rich diet has strong evidence for cardiometabolic outcomes and has not been tested on skin outcom…

assertions.text: Bacterial lipopolysaccharide crossing a leaky gut barrier ('metabolic endotoxaemia') drives inflammation and insulin resistance in mice.
assertions.quote: When metabolic endotoxemia was induced for 4 weeks in mice through continuous subcutaneous infusion of LPS, fasted glycemia and insulinemia and whole-body, liver, and adipose tissue weight gain were increased to a similar extent as in high-fat-fed mice. In addition, adipose tissue F4/80-positive cells and markers of inflammation, and liver triglyceride content, were increased.
assertions.note: A mouse study established that metabolic endotoxemia induced by LPS infusion triggers inflammation and insulin resistance.

assertions.text: A single high-fat meal briefly raised plasma endotoxin in a study of 12 healthy men.
assertions.quote: Plasma endotoxin and endotoxin neutralization capacity were measured for 4 h in 12 healthy men after no meal, 3 cigarettes, a high-fat meal, or a high-fat meal with 3 cigarettes by using the limulus assay. Results Baseline endotoxin concentrations were 8.2 pg/mL (interquartile range: 3.4-13.5 pg/mL) but increased significantly (P < 0.05) by approximately 50% after a high-fat meal
assertions.note: A trial in 12 healthy men showed baseline endotoxin concentrations increased by approximately 50% following a high-fat meal.

assertions.text: A Cochrane review of 39 trials found probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated eczema symptoms.
assertions.quote: We included 39 randomised controlled trials involving 2599 randomised participants. [...] Probiotics probably make little or no difference in participant- or parent-rated symptoms of eczema (13 trials; 754 participants): symptom severity on a scale from 0 to 20 was 0.44 points lower after probiotic treatment (95% confidence interval (CI) -1.22 to 0.33; moderate-quality evidence).
assertions.note: The Cochrane systematic review of 39 trials concluded probiotics probably make little or no difference in participant- or parent-rated symptoms.

assertions.text: A 2024 meta-analysis in children without food allergy reported small score improvements in eczema with probiotics.
assertions.quote: A meta-analysis of 20 RCTs assessing probiotics, alone or combined with prebiotics, revealed a significant reduction in SCORAD scores, suggesting a consistent trend in alleviating AD symptoms in children without food allergies.
assertions.note: The 2024 EAACI meta-analysis of 20 RCTs found a significant reduction in SCORAD scores.

assertions.text: One small randomized trial found rosacea improved after small-intestinal bacterial overgrowth was treated.
assertions.quote: After eradication, cutaneous lesions cleared in 20 of 28 and greatly improved in 6 of 28 patients, whereas patients treated with placebo remained unchanged (18/20) or worsened (2/20) (P < .001).
assertions.note: A randomized trial evaluating rifaximin eradication of SIBO in rosacea found cutaneous lesions cleared or improved significantly compared to placebo.

assertions.text: A leading review concludes it is unproven that restoring barrier function improves disease outside the gut.
assertions.quote: Although chemicals, nutrients, prebiotics, and even plant extracts (e.g., indigo naturalis) improve barrier function, there are no validated drug treatments yet, and the impact of restoring barrier function to ameliorate clinical manifestations in local gastrointestinal disease or systemic diseases is as yet unproven.
assertions.note: Camilleri's review explicitly concludes that the impact of restoring barrier function to ameliorate systemic disease remains unproven.

assertions.text: A widely used commercial zonulin assay detects proteins other than zonulin.
assertions.quote: Our study suggests that the zonulin ELISA does not recognize pre-haptoglobin2, rather structural (and possibly functional) analog proteins belonging to the mannose-associated serine protease family, with properdin being the most likely possible candidate.
assertions.note: The Scheffler et al. study demonstrated that the commercial ELISA kit detects properdin and other proteins rather than pre-haptoglobin2.

assertions.note: The guide assigns Grade D to the leaky gut repair stack of L-glutamine, zinc carnosine, and BPC-157.

assertions.text: In the UK, an unlicensed medicine can be supplied as a 'special' only for an individual patient's special clinical need that no licensed product meets, on the prescriber's responsibility.
assertions.quote: An unlicensed medicinal product may only be supplied in order to meet the special needs of an individual patient.  An unlicensed medicinal product should not be supplied where an equivalent licensed medicinal product can meet the special needs of the patient.
assertions.note: MHRA guidance states unlicensed 'specials' are exempted solely to meet an individual patient's special clinical needs where licensed alternatives cannot, under the prescriber's direct responsibility.

units.text: Topical GHK-Cu has a plausible copper-enzyme mechanism and small-trial human support (GRADE C); injected GHK-Cu has no randomized trials and commonly irritates. In the US, as of FDA's 14 May 2026 list, non-injectable GHK-Cu is in 503A Category 1 (under evaluation, not approved); the injectable route is excluded. In the UK, a GHK-Cu serum presented for appearance is regulated as a cosmetic, and cosmetics law excludes anything injected; MHRA decides from its claims, form and use whether an injected product is a medicine, and a medicine with no UK marketing authorisation may not be sold, supplied or advertised. This course gives no doses or sourcing advice — for an individual patient, that is the prescriber's decision.

assertions.note: Supported by MHRA Guidance Note 8 and the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 (regulations 46 and 279).

Its only controlled human data are two tiny 1990s studies, and case reports describe darkening and new moles, nail pigmentation, melanomas in people with other risk factors (causation unproven), priapism and rhabdomyolysis. FDA (April 2026), MHRA (April 2024) and TGA (August 2026) have all put warnings on record. Hair loss starts with a workup (pattern, trigger, patches, androgens; ferritin and TSH in everyone), and the approved options, minoxidil, finasteride in men and baricitinib for severe alopecia areata, carry grade A evidence. In the UK, a men's minoxidil foam is on general sale, finasteride for hair loss is a private prescription carrying MHRA's strengthened warnings on depression and sexual dysfunction (May 2026), baricitinib is licensed for severe alopecia …
